title: Maintenance that makes sense
description: Know what each service does, when it is due and how to approach it. Browse practical guides, then open the exact repair article for your engine and equipment.

categories.title: Plan your service
categories.description: Turn dates, mileage and findings into a useful service plan.

categories.title: Special maintenance
categories.description: Major, condition-based repairs explained as complete projects: diagnosis, preparation, precise assembly and checks. Start with the 3.7L V6 head-gasket guide. These are repairs when needed, not extra routine service intervals.

categories.title: Advanced maintenance
categories.description: Go beyond routine checks with measurements, targeted service and repair follow-up. Each guide explains what makes the task worthwhile, which equipment it needs and where to find the full procedure. These are condition-based jobs, not extra items to do at every oil change.

notes: The linked filter-inspection procedure is for investigating debris in a removed filter; cutting a filter open is not a required step at every routine oil change.

The linked engine articles explain component layout and filter diagnosis. They are not a complete base-engine oil drain-and-refill walkthrough; use the oil-change instructions and specifications for the fitted engine.
guides.title: Engine oil and filter: make the oil-life monitor useful
guides.summary: Plan an oil change around actual use, choose the correct oil and filter, and reset the monitor only after the work is done.
guides.introduction: Oil is doing several jobs while the engine runs: keeping moving surfaces apart, carrying heat away and transporting contamination to the filter. The useful habit is to treat the oil and filter as a service pair, then keep an eye on the level between changes. The oil-life display estimates when that pair needs service; it does not tell you how much oil is in the sump.
guides.why: Short trips, idling, temperature and engine load affect how quickly oil is used up. That is why a fixed mileage picked from a friend’s driving pattern can be the wrong plan for your car.

when.summary: Follow the oil-life message. The maximum is one year or 10,000 mi (16,000 km) between services.
notes: After a service message, arrange the change within two weeks or 500 mi (800 km).
If the monitor is inoperative or was reset prematurely, use six months or 5,000 mi (8,000 km) from the last actual change.
The mileage ranges in the schedule are estimates, not permission to ignore an earlier message.

prepare.title: Identify the engine
prepare.detail: Choose the oil grade, Ford specification, quantity and filter for the actual engine. Do not borrow the 5.2L oil procedure for a base-engine car.

prepare.title: Plan the complete job
prepare.detail: Arrange safe access, oil collection and disposal, the correct replacement filter, and the correct service instructions before draining anything.

steps.title: Confirm what is due
steps.body: Check the service record, odometer, date and oil-life message. Include the inspections that are due at an oil-change service.

steps.title: Change both service items
steps.body: Use the correct engine-specific oil-change instructions. A replacement filter and fresh oil work together; changing one is not a substitute for changing the other.

steps.title: Finish with verification and a record
steps.body: Confirm the final oil level and check the serviced area for leakage. Record the date, mileage and oil specification.

steps.title: Reset the display after the change
steps.body: With the vehicle safely parked, use the information display’s Settings → Vehicle → Oil Life Reset entry and hold OK to reset. Menu presentation can vary with equipment.

watchFor.title: A level that keeps changing
watchFor.body: Repeated topping up or an unexpectedly rising level deserves investigation; an oil-life reset cannot correct it.

watchFor.title: An oil-pressure warning
watchFor.body: Treat a pressure warning as a problem requiring immediate action, not as a reminder that an oil change is nearly due.

Identify the 2.3L engine components.
Identify the 5.0L engine components.
Investigate debris in a removed filter when diagnosis calls for it.

notes: This guide covers the 2015 Mustang 2.3L EcoBoost, 3.7L V6 and 5.0L V8 oil-level check and top-up. It does not teach an oil-and-filter change.
The oil requirements above use the supplied 2015 owner instructions. Complete refill capacities are not top-up quantities.
guides.title: Check and top up your Mustang’s engine oil
guides.summary: Read the dipstick correctly, decide whether oil is needed and top up cleanly on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.
guides.introduction: I like a maintenance job with a clear finish line: read the dipstick, add oil only if needed and close everything properly. Getting a trustworthy reading includes a 15-minute wait after shutdown. Waiting can be a pain in the ass, but “a little extra for luck” is a lousy substitute: oil above the maximum mark can damage the engine. [Ford oil check and top-up](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.why: The dipstick shows the oil level after oil has drained back into the oil pan—the reservoir beneath the engine. Ford’s warm-engine check includes a 15-minute wait after shutdown because checking sooner can give an inaccurate reading. The Intelligent Oil-Life Monitor tells you when an oil change is due; checking or topping up the level does not replace that service. [Ford oil-level instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Ford maintenance guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

when.summary: Check monthly and before investigating a suspected oil-level problem.
notes: Continue the oil-and-filter service schedule separately.

prepare.title: Bring the simple stuff
prepare.detail: Have a clean, lint-free cloth for the dipstick, an absorbent cloth for spills and a clean funnel if needed for pouring. Bring the correct engine oil only if a top-up is necessary. [Ford checking and filling instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

prepare.title: 2.3L EcoBoost oil
prepare.detail: The 2015 owner instructions specify SAE 5W-30 meeting Ford WSS-M2C946-A. Motorcraft synthetic blend is recommended, with full synthetic also listed as an option. If using another brand, retain the specified viscosity and Ford requirement; Ford also requires API SN performance and the API Certification Mark for gasoline engines. [2015 2.3L oil requirements](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1635371&Uid=G1689459&ProcUid=G1689461&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: 3.7L V6 oil
prepare.detail: The 2015 owner instructions specify SAE 5W-20 meeting Ford WSS-M2C945-A. Motorcraft synthetic blend is recommended, with full synthetic also listed as an option. If using another brand, retain the specified viscosity and Ford requirement; Ford also requires API SN performance and the API Certification Mark for gasoline engines. [2015 3.7L oil requirements](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1635371&Uid=G1660535&ProcUid=G1660537&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: 5.0L V8 oil
prepare.detail: The 2015 owner instructions specify SAE 5W-20 meeting Ford WSS-M2C945-A. Motorcraft synthetic blend is recommended, with full synthetic also listed as an option. If using another brand, retain the specified viscosity and Ford requirement; Ford also requires API SN performance and the API Certification Mark for gasoline engines. [2015 5.0L oil requirements](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1635371&Uid=G1689460&ProcUid=G1689462&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Before inspecting under the hood, disable remote start if equipped. The owner display lists a Remote Start menu with a System setting that can be disabled. Once the engine has been warmed and switched off, remove the key from the vehicle so another person cannot start it while you work. An unexpected start can cause serious injury. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Ford remote-start controls](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1642764&Uid=G1634745&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Park level, warm the engine and wait
steps.body: Set the parking brake. With an automatic transmission, select Park (P); with a manual, select Neutral (N). Run the engine until it reaches normal operating temperature and make sure the car is on level ground. Switch the engine and ignition off, then wait 15 minutes for oil to drain into the pan. Keep the dipstick and filler cap installed while the engine runs. [Ford oil-check setup](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Open the hood and identify the dipstick
steps.body:
Open the hood and make sure it is securely supported before reaching into the engine compartment. Ford calls the dipstick the oil level indicator or oil indicator. Use the branch for your engine:

- 2.3L: item 43 in Engine — Front and Upper Components. [2.3L component identification](#/document/G1660455)
- 3.7L: item 2 in Engine Upper — LH Cylinder Head. [3.7L component identification](#/document/G1681496)
- 5.0L: item 18 in Engine — Upper Components; item 17 is its tube. [5.0L component identification](#/document/G1685309)

These are identification references, not instructions to dismantle the engine. Keep clear of cooling fans: they can operate with the ignition off. With the ignition off, look for visible fan damage; do not proceed with under-hood work if a fan is cracked, separating or otherwise damaged. Have it replaced. If reaching your work area would put you near a fan, have the fan disabled first to prevent injury. [Under-hood safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Wipe, reseat and read
steps.body: With the engine off, pull out the dipstick and wipe it clean with the lint-free cloth. Insert it fully into its normal seated position, then withdraw it again. Read where the oil reaches relative to the minimum and maximum marks. If smearing makes the boundary unclear, repeat the wipe, fully insert and read sequence before deciding to add anything. Never remove the dipstick with the engine running. [Ford dipstick instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Choose the next action
steps.body: If the reading is between the minimum and maximum marks, the level is acceptable: do not add oil. At the minimum mark, add the correct oil immediately. A reading below minimum also needs correction rather than being treated as acceptable. If the reading is above maximum, add nothing; repeat the check under the same conditions to confirm it and arrange correction if it remains high. Ford warns that exceeding the maximum can damage the engine. You do not need to reach the upper mark when the level is already acceptable. [Ford level limits and filling guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: If needed, identify and open the oil filler
steps.body:
Keep the engine off. As a practical identification check, look for an explicit engine-oil marking on the actual filler cap and confirm that it identifies the engine-oil opening before removing it. If the marking is absent, unreadable or ambiguous, stop the top-up until that opening is positively identified; do not choose by cap color or guess from a nearby component.

Once identified, clean around the cap so dirt is not carried into the opening. Turn the cap counterclockwise and remove it. Never remove the oil filler cap while the engine runs. [Ford filler-cap and filling instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Add the right oil and recheck
steps.body: Use the oil requirement for your engine from Preparation. Pour carefully into the oil filler opening, using the funnel if needed. Add a little at a time and repeat the wipe, fully insert and read sequence to check progress. Stop once the level is within the marked range; never exceed maximum. The dipstick determines the top-up amount, not the engine’s complete oil-change capacity. Do not add supplemental engine-oil additives: Ford says they are unnecessary and can cause engine damage. Soak up any spilled oil immediately with the absorbent cloth. [Ford top-up instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Seat the dipstick and secure the cap
steps.body: After the final acceptable reading, reinstall the dipstick fully. If you removed the filler cap, reinstall it and turn it clockwise until you feel strong resistance. Check that it is correctly fitted, and absorb any remaining spillage. Remove your cloths, funnel and oil container from the engine compartment before closing the hood securely. [Ford dipstick seating, cap closure and cleanup](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Record the result and preserve the service reminder
steps.body: My suggestion: note the date, mileage, final level and any oil added. Comparable notes make a changing level easier to assess. A level check or top-up is not an oil change, so leave the oil-life reset alone; Ford ties that reset to completing an oil change. Continue the separate oil-and-filter service schedule. [Ford oil-life and maintenance guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

watchFor.title: A rising level
watchFor.body: More oil on the dipstick is not automatically good news. Ford notes that short trips without full warm-up, extended idling and prolonged low-speed driving can dilute the oil and raise its level. A rising reading deserves assessment; the dipstick alone does not establish the cause. [Ford oil-dilution guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

watchFor.title: Repeated additions or fresh wetness
watchFor.body: Keep a record of repeated top-ups and point out visible oil wetness when arranging an inspection. Ford includes oil and fluid leak checks in its maintenance inspections. Treat wetness as something to trace, not permission to start buying seals at random. [Ford inspection guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

watchFor.title: Contamination alongside discoloration
watchFor.body: Color alone does not establish that a fluid needs changing. If discoloration comes with signs of overheating or foreign material, Ford calls for immediate inspection by a qualified expert. [Ford fluid-condition guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

procedures.purpose: Identify the 2.3L oil indicator in the front and upper component view.
Identify the 3.7L oil level indicator in the LH cylinder-head component view.
Identify the 5.0L oil indicator and indicator tube in the upper component view.
Apply unexpected-start and cooling-fan precautions during under-hood inspection.

stepGroups.title: Set up and get a clear reading
stepGroups.summary: Establish the checking conditions and identify your engine’s dipstick.

stepGroups.title: Decide whether oil is needed
stepGroups.summary: Use the marked range and add the correct oil only when required.

stepGroups.title: Close up and keep a useful record
stepGroups.summary: Secure the openings, clean up and preserve the service reminder.

diagnostics.finding: Oil is between the minimum and maximum marks.
diagnostics.meaning: The level is acceptable.
diagnostics.next: Do not add oil. Fully seat the dipstick and finish closing up. [Ford acceptable range](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: Oil is at or below minimum.
diagnostics.meaning: The level needs correction; Ford explicitly requires immediate addition at minimum.
diagnostics.next: Keep the engine off while topping up with the correct oil and rechecking. If you cannot obtain a readable level, arrange assistance rather than guessing a quantity. [Ford minimum-level action](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: Oil remains above maximum on a repeated check.
diagnostics.meaning: The level exceeds Ford’s limit and can cause engine damage.
diagnostics.next: Stop adding oil and have the excess level corrected before operating the engine. Removing oil and diagnosing a rising level are separate jobs. [Ford overfill warning](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: Readings are unclear or were taken before the 15-minute wait.
diagnostics.meaning: You do not yet have a dependable basis for adding oil.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the check on level ground after the required warm-engine shutdown wait, wiping and fully reinserting the dipstick before reading. [Ford measurement conditions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

verification.title: The final reading is acceptable
verification.body: Confirm a clear reading within the marked range, obtained on level ground after the prescribed warm-engine shutdown wait. If you added oil, confirm the level again before calling the job finished. [Ford final level check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

verification.title: Everything opened is closed
verification.body: The dipstick is fully seated. If removed, the filler cap is correctly installed and turned clockwise to strong resistance. Spills are absorbed, your supplies are out of the engine compartment and the hood is securely closed. [Ford closure and cleanup](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

notes: Applicability remains the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Match filters, fluids and follow-up procedures to the actual engine, transmission and fitted equipment.
Keep the existing maintenance schedule separate. This checklist does not replace scheduled service.
Coordinate conditional wheel removal with other planned service. This inspection requires no suspension disassembly, brake hydraulic disconnection or removal of a complete air-cleaner assembly.
guides.title: An oil-service visual and operating inspection worth a damn
guides.summary: Check your 2015 Mustang’s accessible systems, record useful readings and observations, and give each concern a concrete next action.
guides.introduction: I want an inspection to produce something better than “looks fine”—preferably before a mystery clunk becomes an expensive parts-guessing contest. This checklist covers the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine: tires, operating checks, basic fluid readings, accessible engine-bay and underbody inspection, and reassembly of any wheels removed. Battery-performance testing, measured brake wear, parking-brake holding assessment and alignment are separate follow-up work. Completing this checklist records what you checked; it does not certify the whole car or establish that its oil was changed. Ford recommends a multi-point inspection alongside scheduled service. [Ford inspection checklist](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.why: Tires, brakes, steering and suspension can produce maddeningly similar symptoms. I start with pressures, visible condition and the circumstances of a noise, then choose the next test. Previous repairs matter, too. Ford cautions against replacing components through a diagnostic test when its required symptom is absent. A specific observation helps; a confident shrug is still a shrug. [Diagnostic preparation](#/document/G1693185) [Suspension diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

when.summary: At every oil-change service; a multi-point inspection is recommended.
notes: For this schedule, the oil-service interval must not exceed one year or 10,000 mi (16,000 km).

prepare.title: Bring the car’s details and history
prepare.detail: Record mileage, engine, transmission, fitted wheel and tire sizes, modifications, previous repairs and fluid additions. Have a notebook or phone ready for corner-by-corner readings and photographs. Ford’s standard suspension specifications do not apply to aftermarket equipment. [Preliminary checks](#/document/G1693185) [Equipment applicability](#/document/G1686610)

prepare.title: Prevent remote starting before inspection
prepare.detail: Before beginning work around or underneath the car, disable remote start, if fitted, through Vehicle settings → Remote Start Setup. For hands-on checks, switch the ignition off and remove the key. Restore ignition power only for the deliberate operating checks, with people and tools clear of moving parts. Unexpected starting can seriously injure someone working on the car. [Start prevention](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Gather the basic inspection supplies
prepare.detail: Have a reliable tire-pressure gauge, tread-depth gauge, light, clean lint-free dipstick cloth, and a soft cloth or sponge with water or washer fluid for the wipers. Locate the tire/certification label near the driver’s door. Begin with cold tires and a cold engine for the coolant check; check oil later under its specified warm-engine conditions. Wear eye and ear protection during service and protective gloves for sharp-edged parts. [Tire preparation](#/document/G1686610) [Service protection](#/document/G1693189) [Oil-check conditions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Wiper cleaning](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405324&Uid=G1634804&ProcUid=G1448670&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a suitably rated hoist according to its manufacturer’s instructions, or suitable service lifting equipment, stands and wheel blocks on a hard, level surface. Identify the stamped triangles marking the vehicle lifting locations. A jack alone is never support for working underneath. [Lifting locations](#/document/G1663631) [Equipment and support precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Prepare for conditional wheel removal
prepare.detail: Have a socket matching the actual wheel nuts, hand tools, a torque wrench capable of 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), mounting-face cleaning supplies, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2. Read the lubricant’s safety information. Coordinate access with any separately planned tire rotation so each wheel comes off only once. [Wheel service](#/document/G1686507) [Material precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Optional coolant-strength equipment
prepare.detail: If measuring concentration today, have a coolant refractometer and its operating instructions. Ford recommends a refractometer, such as Robinair 75240, rather than a hydrometer or test strips. Follow the instrument manufacturer’s calibration, sampling and reading instructions. [Coolant testing equipment](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Build a record you can use next time
steps.body:
Write down mileage, engine, transmission, modifications and current concerns. Describe each symptom by location and trigger: braking, turning, acceleration, bumps or road speed. Review previous repairs before selecting a suspect. [Diagnostic history](#/document/G1693185) [Suspension preliminary checks](#/document/G1686610)

For each checklist item, record location → observation or reading → next action. Mark an inaccessible area “not inspected.” This recording convention keeps an unseen component from quietly becoming a passed component.

steps.title: Check cold road tires and identify the spare
steps.body:
Check pressures with normal vehicle loads and cold tires. Ford defines cold as stationary and out of direct sunlight for at least an hour, before driving 1 mi (1.6 km). Compare fitted road-tire sizes and pressure targets with the vehicle’s tire/certification label. Use the vehicle’s recommended pressure, not the maximum molded into the road tire’s sidewall. Do not bleed a hot tire down to a cold-pressure target. Underinflation can cause internal damage and tire failure without an obviously flat appearance. [Tire-check setup](#/document/G1686610) [Ford tire-pressure guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Remove a valve cap, press the gauge firmly onto the valve and record the pressure. Adjust to the applicable cold target, recheck and replace the cap. Repeat at every road tire. If a spare is fitted, identify its type before adjusting it: maintain a T-type mini-spare at 60 psi (4.15 bar); maintain a full-size or dissimilar spare at the higher of the front and rear pressures shown on the Tire Label. Do not automatically give a temporary spare the road-tire pressure. [Pressure method and spare branches](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Inspect visible tread, sidewalls and valve stems, including the spare, for cuts, cracking, bulges, embedded objects and abnormal wear. Measure tread with the gauge according to its instructions; identify each measurement location in the record. Tires require replacement at 2/32 in (1.6 mm), when tread reaches the wear bars. Damage or suspected internal damage needs professional tire assessment. Route detailed condition, age and rotation decisions to the [tire guide](#/maintenance/tires). [Tire condition and wear limits](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

If a temporary mobility kit is fitted, check the sealant canister’s Use By date and replace expired sealant. [Mobility-kit check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Operate the lights, horn, washers and wipers
steps.body:
Operate the exterior lamps, hazards and horn. Walk around to check illumination, using a helper where needed for brake lamps. Observe washer spray and the resulting wipe; record failed spray, streaking and missed areas separately. Inspect the windshield for chips, cracks and pitting. Note abnormal brake, ABS, airbag or seatbelt warning-lamp operation, and record reported parking-brake sticking, failure to release or failure to hold for follow-up. [Ford operating checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

Stop the wipers and switch the ignition off before touching the blades. Gently run a fingertip along each rubber edge to feel for roughness. Clean with water or washer fluid on a soft cloth or sponge, then repeat the spray-and-wipe observation. If cleaning does not restore satisfactory wiping, record the problem and arrange blade replacement or further diagnosis. [Blade inspection and cleaning](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405324&Uid=G1634804&ProcUid=G1448670&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Ignition-off precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Make the engine bay safe for hands-on checks
steps.body:
Switch the ignition off, remove the key and confirm remote start remains disabled before hands-on work. Keep hands and tools outside the cooling fans’ operating area: fans can run with the ignition off. Work near a fan requires its applicable disabling procedure. [Unexpected-start and fan precautions](#/document/G1693189)

From a safe position, inspect the fans for visible damage, cracks or separation. If damage is present, stop underhood work until the fan is corrected; it can break apart during operation and cause serious injury. [Damaged-fan warning](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Read the coolant, brake and washer levels
steps.body:
With the engine cold, read the coolant reservoir against MIN and MAX. The level should be between them. A level at or below MIN requires immediate correction with prediluted coolant meeting the fitted engine’s specification. Never open the reservoir or add coolant while the engine is running or hot: pressurized steam and liquid can cause severe burns. Do not fill beyond MAX. Use the [cooling-system guide](#/maintenance/cooling-check) for coolant selection, filling and leak follow-up. [Cold coolant-level check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Read the brake/clutch fluid reservoir against MIN and MAX. Between the lines is normal; do not add fluid merely to reach MAX. A level outside that range requires immediate service because system performance may be compromised. [Brake and clutch fluid](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

Record the washer reservoir’s visible level where readable, alongside the spray result. Arrange attention to a low or unreadable level during service. Keep fluids in their designated systems: coolant sprayed from the washer reservoir can obscure the windshield. [Fluid checklist](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Fluid separation](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Record coolant strength separately from level
steps.body:
A full reservoir does not establish freeze protection. If testing concentration today, follow the refractometer manufacturer’s instructions for calibration, sampling and reading, with the engine cold. If sampling requires opening the reservoir, loosen the cap slowly to release remaining pressure and secure it afterward. Ford’s normal concentration target is 48–50%, corresponding to a freeze point between −30°F (−34°C) and −34°F (−37°C). Record the reading and units. [Coolant-strength method and target](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Route unexpected readings, contamination or recurring low level to the [cooling-system guide](#/maintenance/cooling-check). Deliberate extreme-climate concentration adjustments need separate Ford service assessment. If no measurement is taken, record concentration testing as a separate service action. [Coolant assessment and climate exceptions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Look over belts, hoses, connections and the battery
steps.body:
With the engine stopped, inspect accessible accessory belts and visible radiator, cooler, heater and air-conditioning hoses. Follow visible hoses toward their connections, noting damage, wetness, restrictions or questionable routing. Inspect accessible intake and vacuum connections for disconnection, damage or leakage clues. Record the component and exact location; leave hoses and connections assembled. [Inspection targets](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Mechanical preliminary checks](#/document/G1693185)

Look at accessible battery connections for corrosion, visible damage or an apparently displaced connection. Arrange cleaning or connection service where needed. Request a battery-performance test as part of the wider inspection or starting-concern diagnosis, and record its actual result separately. A connection observation does not establish battery performance. [Battery inspection items](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Inspect the air-filter element where the owner procedure applies
steps.body:
The owner procedure uses a housing cover secured by two clamps. Confirm that the fitted housing matches this arrangement before using that access method. For a different or modified housing, arrange the applicable engine-specific element inspection. Keep the engine off; never remove the air cleaner while it is running or start it with the air cleaner removed, because injury and vehicle damage can result. [Air-filter access and precautions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1514262&Uid=G1634802&ProcUid=G1649556&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Release both clamps, carefully lift the cover and remove the element, noting its seating. Look for accumulated dirt, debris and visible damage to the element or sealing edges. Keep foreign material out of the intake; on the EcoBoost engine, even small particles can damage the engine and turbocharger. Wipe dirt from the housing and cover without letting it enter the induction system. If replacement is needed, match the specified element to the actual engine and vehicle. [Element handling](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1514262&Uid=G1634802&ProcUid=G1649556&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Refit the serviceable element or correct replacement squarely in its seat. Replace the cover without trapping or crimping the element’s edges, then engage both clamps. Check that the cover is seated and secured before running the engine. Poor seating can let unfiltered air enter. [Air-filter closure](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1514262&Uid=G1634802&ProcUid=G1649556&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Check engine oil under the specified conditions
steps.body:
Finish air-cleaner reassembly and clear people and tools from the engine bay before deliberately running the engine. With the car on level ground, parking brake applied and transmission in PARK or NEUTRAL as applicable, run the engine to normal operating temperature. Switch it off and wait 15 minutes for oil to return to the pan. Remove the key again before hands-on work; keep remote start disabled. [Oil-check setup](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Start prevention](#/document/G1693189)

Remove the dipstick, wipe it with a clean lint-free cloth, reinstall it and withdraw it again. Between MIN and MAX is acceptable; do not add oil. At MIN, oil must be added immediately using the fitted engine’s specification. Record any low or above-MAX result for correction; excess oil can damage the engine. Fully seat the dipstick afterward. Never remove the dipstick or filler cap while the engine is running. This step checks level; oil selection and an oil change remain separate jobs. [Oil reading and decisions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

For an automatic transmission, record the applicable fluid-level service requirement: Ford calls for inspection if a dipstick is fitted and directs owners to their dealer for requirements. Keep this separate from the engine-oil check. A manual transmission does not inherit that automatic-transmission instruction. [Transmission branch](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Establish supported access underneath
steps.body:
For the hoist route, position the vehicle in NEUTRAL and use the lifting locations identified by stamped triangles. Confirm capacity for the car, cargo and modifications. Position arms and adapters clear of suspension, steering, exhaust, brackets and the axle/rear cover. Check underbody clearance before using a drive-on lift. Follow the equipment manufacturer’s operating instructions, including positioning and restraint. Keep the engine off; do not power the wheels for this checklist. [Hoist positioning](#/document/G1686507) [Lifting points and clearance](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

For the floor-jack route, use a hard, level surface and adequately rated equipment. Apply the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Support the raised vehicle with stands before going underneath. Never rely on the jack alone: unexpected lowering can cause fatal crushing injuries. The emergency tire-change jack is unsuitable for this service work, and neither bumper is a lifting point. [Jack-and-stand restraint](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Screen for wheel drag before removing wheels
steps.body:
Perform this screening only with the whole vehicle correctly supported on a hoist, all four wheels clear of the ground and every wheel still installed. Confirm NEUTRAL, release the service brake and parking brake, then turn each wheel by hand and record whether it turns freely. Keep the engine off. [Wheels-installed screening](#/document/G1686610) [Released-brake condition](#/document/G1721936)

Resistance calls for brake-drag diagnosis; it does not identify a failed caliper or establish bearing condition. Record the affected corner and route it to the [brake guide](#/maintenance/brakes). Once screening is finished, reapply the parking brake before continuing; confirm it again before lowering in step 16. Follow the hoist manufacturer’s instructions for access and operation. [Drag follow-up](#/document/G1721936) [Vehicle restraint](#/document/G1693189)

Skip this screening on a partly raised, chocked floor-jack setup. Leave its parking brake applied and its grounded wheels blocked. [Floor-jack restraint](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Remove wheels only where visibility requires it
steps.body:
Assess what you can see first. Where a wheel prevents an adequate wheel-area or brake observation, remove its nuts and the wheel after safe support is established. Coordinate access with any separately planned tire rotation. Never apply heat to a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and bearing. [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507)

Keep this access limited to inspection. Leave calipers, pads, hoses, springs and suspension arms assembled. Their removal belongs to the applicable measurement or repair procedure.

steps.title: Inspect the accessible brake parts
steps.body:
At each corner, inspect visible pads, disc surfaces, caliper, retaining hardware, flexible hose and disc shield. Record damage, suspected fluid wetness, visibly missing hardware and marked differences between corners. State whether both pads and the relevant disc surfaces were visible. Leave hydraulic connections and caliper fasteners undisturbed. Continuous squeal calls for pad inspection; continuous grinding or moaning calls for inspection of pads, discs and attaching hardware. [Brake inspection targets and symptoms](#/document/G1721936)

Use the [brake inspection guide](#/maintenance/brakes) for measurements and fitted brake-package limits. Record parking-brake concerns for functional assessment: a freely turning wheel with the brake released does not prove that the parking brake holds. Ford includes pads, discs, hoses and parking brake in its oil-service inspection list. [Scheduled brake inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Trace the exhaust, driveline and visible leaks
steps.body:
Inspect accessible exhaust sections and heat shields for damage, displaced parts and apparently loose attachments. Look along the rear axle, driveshaft, U-joints and half-shafts for wetness or damage. Half-shafts run toward the driven wheels; inspect their visible protective boots for splits or other damage. Remove excessive mud or road deposits where they conceal the chassis inspection. [Underbody inspection targets](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Chassis preparation](#/document/G1686610)

As a recording aid, photograph the highest visible wet area and the components below it. This gives leak diagnosis a starting point without declaring the wettest part guilty.

steps.title: Inspect steering and suspension without loosening them
steps.body:
Inspect accessible steering linkage, tie-rod ends, ball joints, control arms, bushings, springs, struts, shocks, wheel hubs and mountings. Record damaged boots, leakage, broken or displaced parts, and apparently loose or missing hardware by corner and component. Bushings are flexible mounts at component connections. Leave fasteners untouched during this visual pass; a suspect attachment needs its component-specific assessment. [Suspension inspection](#/document/G1686610)

Ford’s rear-suspension component names are: coil spring; stabilizer and links; shock absorber; wheel knuckle; wheel bearing/hub assembly; wheel studs; lower-arm vertical link; toe link; lower arm and bushing assembly; and upper arm. Use the appropriate name to make a finding specific. [Rear suspension identification](#/document/G1697533)

Record a low corner or lean alongside vehicle loading, then use the [suspension guide](#/maintenance/suspension) for follow-up. Ride-height measurement may be needed before deciding a spring is at fault. [Lean and ride-height decisions](#/document/G1686610)

Identify actual grease fittings and record any required lubrication as a service action. Ford calls for lubrication where fittings are provided. Do not lubricate front or rear stabilizer bars or their bushings; lubricant can damage the bushings. [Fitted grease points](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Front bushing restriction](#/document/G1692534) [Rear bushing restriction](#/document/G1686652)

steps.title: Refit wheels, restore restraint and lower safely
steps.body:
For every wheel removed, clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting face and corresponding hub/disc mounting face. Confirm any disc-to-hub fasteners are secured without interfering with wheel seating. Poor seating can let the nuts loosen and the wheel detach in use, causing loss of control. [Wheel seating requirements](#/document/G1686507)

Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft XL-2 only at the interface between the wheel’s center pilot bore and hub pilot—the locating surfaces around the center opening. Keep lubricant off mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces. Position the wheel and install its nuts finger-tight. [Pilot lubrication and initial assembly](#/document/G1686507)

Whether or not wheels were removed, confirm the parking brake is applied before lowering. It must not remain released after the NEUTRAL drag screening. On the floor-jack route, retain blocks at every wheel remaining on the ground throughout lifting and lowering. Clear people, tools and loose materials from beneath the car, then lower according to the equipment manufacturer’s instructions. [Restraint and support precautions](#/document/G1693189) [Wheel-service sequence](#/document/G1686507)

With the car resting on its tires, keep the parking brake applied and block the wheels against rolling before final tightening. Tighten each removed wheel’s nuts in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), with clean, dry stud and nut threads. The pattern helps prevent disc runout and subsequent brake vibration. Arrange retightening within 160 km (100 mi), because wheels can loosen after initial tightening. [Ground-level restraint](#/document/G1693189) [Final torque and retightening](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Close the inspection with specific decisions
steps.body:
Confirm the air-filter cover is clamped, the dipstick is fully seated, any coolant cap opened for sampling is secured, and all removed wheels have received final tightening. Check that tools and loose materials are clear before closing up. [Air-cleaner closure](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1514262&Uid=G1634802&ProcUid=G1649556&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Dipstick seating](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Coolant-cap handling](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Wheel completion](#/document/G1686507)

If no unresolved finding makes driving unsafe, an ordinary smooth-road drive can help confirm a reported suspension concern. Record when it occurs and where it is felt. Leave specialized braking and parking-brake road tests to dedicated diagnosis. [Suspension road assessment](#/document/G1686610) [Brake symptom assessment](#/document/G1721936)

Give each record entry an outcome: no concern observed within the inspected area; correction required; diagnosis required; or not inspected. Assign remaining concerns a next action and responsible person or guide. Carry recurring leaks and noises forward with their earlier records. An absent symptom does not establish a repair. Keep scheduled maintenance and oil-change completion separate. [Diagnostic discipline](#/document/G1693185)

watchFor.title: Brake findings that stop a routine road check
watchFor.body: A sinking or low/spongy pedal, suspected brake-fluid leakage, locking under light braking or excessive pedal effort requires diagnosis before routine road assessment. Several faults can cause these symptoms; adding fluid does not establish a repair. [Brake symptoms](#/document/G1721936)

watchFor.title: Tire damage that pressure cannot fix
watchFor.body: Bulges, separation, cuts or suspected internal damage need professional assessment before driving. Tires at the wear bars or 2/32 in (1.6 mm) require replacement. A corrected gauge reading does not clear damaged rubber. [Tire condition decisions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: An easy-moving stabilizer link
watchFor.body: Ford describes the front and rear stabilizer-link ball joints as low-friction designs with low breakaway torque. Easy movement alone is not proof of wear. [Front link characteristics](#/document/G1692535) [Rear link characteristics](#/document/G1686653)

watchFor.title: Fluid color becoming a sales pitch
watchFor.body: Color alone does not establish that fluid needs replacing. Discoloration accompanied by overheating signs or foreign-material contamination needs prompt expert assessment. [Ford fluid-condition guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

watchFor.title: The same finding on every service sheet
watchFor.body: Give a recurring leak, noise or wear pattern a named next action. “Still there” can be an accurate observation, but it is a lousy repair plan.

procedures.purpose: Identify rear suspension components when recording findings.
Interpret tire, steering, suspension and wheels-installed drag observations.
Route brake symptoms and drag findings to diagnosis.
Identify vehicle lifting locations and restrictions.
Provide conditional wheel removal and complete wheel installation requirements.

stepGroups.title: Establish the baseline
stepGroups.summary: Record concerns, check cold road tires and the spare, and operate exterior equipment.

stepGroups.title: Inspect the engine bay
stepGroups.summary: Control starting hazards, read fluids, inspect connections and check the filter.

stepGroups.title: Establish access and screen drag
stepGroups.summary: Support the car, screen with wheels installed on a hoist, restore the parking brake and remove wheels only as needed.

stepGroups.title: Inspect underneath
stepGroups.summary: Observe brakes, exhaust, driveline, steering and suspension.

stepGroups.title: Reassemble and finish
stepGroups.summary: Refit wheels, confirm restraint before lowering, complete final torque and assign follow-up work.

diagnostics.finding: Uneven tire wear or harsh ride
diagnostics.meaning: Pressure, alignment and suspension can contribute; the wear pattern alone does not identify the cause. [Tire and ride symptoms](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Correct cold road-tire pressures to the vehicle label, record wear and damage, and use the [tire guide](#/maintenance/tires) for assessment before rotation. [Initial tire decisions](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Pulling, wandering or a visible lean
diagnostics.meaning: Loading, tires, brake drag, alignment and steering or suspension faults can overlap. [Pull and lean diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Record loading and tire readings, then route the concern to the [suspension guide](#/maintenance/suspension). Alignment or ride-height measurement may follow; appearance alone does not condemn a spring. [Diagnostic route](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: A wheel resists hand rotation during hoist screening
diagnostics.meaning: Brake drag is possible. Parking-brake parts, calipers, hoses and hydraulic components are among the potential causes. [Brake-drag causes](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Record the corner and released-brake conditions, restore the parking brake after screening and arrange brake-drag diagnosis. Leave hydraulic connections closed during this checklist. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936) [Restraint precautions](#/document/G1693189)

diagnostics.finding: Continuous brake squeal, grinding or moaning
diagnostics.meaning: Continuous squeal calls for pad inspection; continuous grinding or moaning calls for pads, discs and hardware to be checked against specifications. Brief first-morning squeal can occur with humidity and cold pads. [Brake-noise distinctions](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Record duration and conditions and use the [brake inspection guide](#/maintenance/brakes) for inspection and measurement before selecting parts. [Brake inspection decisions](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Red brake and yellow ABS warnings remain illuminated
diagnostics.meaning: Ford directs diagnosis toward ABS diagnostic trouble codes. [Warning-lamp diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Arrange an ABS-capable diagnostic scan and assessment. Keep the warnings recorded as an unresolved fault. [ABS diagnostic route](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Brake/clutch fluid outside MIN–MAX
diagnostics.meaning: The level is outside the normal operating range and system performance may be compromised. [Fluid-level limits](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
diagnostics.next: Seek immediate service instead of using a top-up to close the inspection entry. [Ford service decision](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: Cold coolant at/below MIN or an unexpected concentration
diagnostics.meaning: Level and freeze protection are separate results. Ford’s normal concentration target is 48–50%; deliberate extreme-climate adjustments require separate consideration. [Coolant limits](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)
diagnostics.next: Arrange immediate low-level correction with specified coolant and use the [cooling-system guide](#/maintenance/cooling-check) to investigate loss or concentration concerns. Keep the system closed while hot. [Coolant follow-up](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

diagnostics.finding: Engine oil at MIN or above MAX
diagnostics.meaning: MIN requires immediate oil addition; oil above MAX can damage the engine. [Oil-level decisions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
diagnostics.next: Arrange correction using the fitted engine’s oil specification and repeat the level check under the stated conditions. Record the correction separately from any oil-change job. [Oil-check and correction requirements](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

verification.title: The record identifies actual checks
verification.body: Confirm tire pressures identify their corners and spare type, fluid readings include checking conditions, and symptom notes describe triggers. Keep inaccessible areas and separately requested tests visible in the record.

verification.title: Opened items are secured
verification.body: Confirm both air-filter cover clamps are engaged without trapping the element, the dipstick is fully seated and any coolant cap opened for sampling is secured. [Filter closure](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1514262&Uid=G1634802&ProcUid=G1649556&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Dipstick seating](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1612345&Uid=G1634792&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Coolant-cap handling](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Restraint was restored before lowering
verification.body: Confirm the parking brake was reapplied after drag screening and checked before lowering. Keep it applied, with the wheels blocked against rolling, during ground-level final tightening. Retain the floor-jack branch’s grounded-wheel blocks throughout lifting and lowering. [Vehicle restraint](#/document/G1693189)

verification.title: Removed wheels have their final torque
verification.body: Confirm clean seating faces, clean and dry threads, star/cross tightening to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the car resting on its tires, and retightening arranged within 160 km (100 mi). [Wheel completion](#/document/G1686507)

verification.title: Each finding has a next action
verification.body: Recheck simple corrections against their original observations. Assign remaining concerns to tire, brake, cooling, battery or suspension assessment as appropriate. An absent symptom does not establish that a repair occurred. [Diagnostic limits](#/document/G1693185)

verification.title: Oil-service completion has its own entry
verification.body: This checklist does not establish that the oil and filter were changed. Reset the oil-life monitor only after the engine oil and filter change has actually been completed. [Ford oil-service requirements](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

notes: Scope remains the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.

The executable rotation route uses a hoist and compatible non-directional wheel/tire assemblies. The vehicle's emergency jack is not used for this maintenance procedure. [Lifting restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

Tire dismounting, bead seating, valve/sensor replacement, alignment adjustment, balancing and runout correction are separate jobs. New tire or wheel installation requires a new valve stem; those replacement requirements do not turn ordinary assembly rotation into valve replacement. [Tire service](#/document/G1686509)
guides.title: Tires: cold pressure, tread checks and non-directional rotation
guides.summary: Check pressure and condition, measure tread, choose the supported non-directional rotation pattern, and finish with correct wheel tightening and TPMS location calibration.
guides.introduction: I start with the gauge before reaching for the wheel wrench. Moving a worn tire to another corner can relocate the problem beautifully while fixing absolutely damn nothing. This guide covers the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine: cold-pressure checks, tire and wheel inspection, and rotation of compatible non-directional assemblies using a hoist. Directional tires get inspected here; their rotation arrangement goes to a tire professional rather than borrowing a pattern that does not apply. Tire dismounting, replacement, alignment and vibration measurements are separate jobs. [Tire inspection](#/document/G1686502) [Ford rotation guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)
guides.why: Correct inflation supports tire performance and wear; underinflation can build heat and damage a tire internally. Tread should wear evenly across its width and around its circumference. Uneven wear can point toward alignment, inflation, balance or suspension concerns, so rotation belongs after the cause is assessed. The tire pressure monitoring system, or TPMS, uses battery-powered sensors attached to the valve stems. Its warning can indicate low pressure or a system fault, but it cannot inspect rubber for you. [Wear diagnosis](#/document/G1686502) [TPMS operation](#/document/G1686515) [Ford tire care](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

when.summary: Check pressure and wear monthly. At every oil service, inspect wear, measure tread depth and rotate where the fitted tire arrangement permits.
notes: Include the spare if fitted.

prepare.title: Pressure and tread equipment
prepare.detail: Have a digital tire-pressure gauge, an air source, a tread-depth gauge and a way to record results by wheel position. Ford's workshop procedure requires a digital gauge whenever pressure is measured. Find the tire/certification label on the driver door or door pillar before starting. [Pressure equipment](#/document/G1686509) [Tread measurement](#/document/G1686502)

prepare.title: Cold tires
prepare.detail: Plan the pressure check after the vehicle has stood out of direct sunlight for at least one hour and before driving. The tires must be cool, not heated by driving even a mile. This guide uses the cold-pressure route throughout. [Ford cold-pressure conditions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: For wheel rotation
prepare.detail: Arrange access to a suitable hoist and someone competent to operate it. Its capacity must cover the car, cargo and modifications. Have a wheel-nut tool matched to the fitted fasteners, a torque wrench capable of 150 lb-ft (204 Nm), suitable mounting-surface cleaning tools, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2. The supported removal route places the transmission in Neutral on a hoist; the emergency jack is not a maintenance lift. [Wheel service](#/document/G1686507) [Lifting locations](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: For TPMS location calibration
prepare.detail: Have Ford TPMS tool 204-D081A (204-D081). Location calibration can be entered manually with the start/stop switch, so a scan tool is not essential for the route taught below. Read the activation tool's operating instructions before use. [Sensor location calibration](#/document/G1686523)

prepare.title: Protection and handling
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service and gloves when handling sharp damage. Read the lubricant's material safety information before using it. Never inflate a tire that has been driven flat until it has been removed from the wheel and inspected internally; hidden damage can cause failure during inflation. [Service protection](#/document/G1693189) [Run-flat damage precaution](#/document/G1693193)

steps.title: Secure the car and prevent an unexpected start
steps.body:
Park on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and turn the engine off. Put an automatic transmission in Park (P); with a manual transmission, select Reverse (R) after shutting the engine off. Keep this secured ground setup for the inspection. Neutral is used later for the supported hoist operation. [Ground setup](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Service setup precautions](#/document/G1693189)

Keep the key under your control so nobody starts the car during inspection. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle. An unexpected start can injure someone working nearby. Keep the ignition off during physical wheel work; ignition-on TPMS work comes after the car is back on its tires and secured again. [Starting precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Identify what is fitted at each corner
steps.body:
Make a record for left front, right front, left rear and right rear. Copy the applicable cold pressure and tire size from the vehicle label, then compare the actual tires with it. Note directional markings and any difference between front and rear tire or wheel specifications. Ford requires the recommended tire size, speed rating, load range and construction, with wheel size and offset matching the original specification for that tire. A matching tire diameter alone does not establish wheel interchangeability. [Fitment requirements](#/document/G1686502)

Identify the spare separately, if fitted. A dissimilar spare—different in brand, size or appearance from the road assemblies—is for temporary use and stays out of the rotation. [Ford spare and rotation restrictions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Measure and set cold pressure
steps.body:
Confirm the tires are cool after at least an hour stationary out of direct sunlight, before driving. Remove one valve cap, press the digital gauge firmly onto the valve and record the reading. Reseat it if the connection leaks or the reading is inconsistent. Add air to reach that position's vehicle-label pressure. If you overfill a cold tire, release air through the valve's center pin, then measure again. Refit the cap and repeat at every corner. Use the vehicle label, not the maximum pressure molded into the tire. [Digital-gauge requirement](#/document/G1686509) [Ford pressure-check procedure](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Do not bleed a hot tire down to the cold label value: pressure normally rises with driving. Return to the cold condition for this guide's final adjustment. Underinflation can produce heat, internal damage and tire failure even when the tire does not look flat. [Ford inflation precautions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Include the spare or check the mobility kit
steps.body:
Inspect and measure the spare if fitted. Ford specifies storage pressure of 60 psi (4.15 bar) for a T-type mini-spare; full-size and dissimilar spares are maintained at the higher of the front and rear pressures on the tire label. Identify the spare type before choosing its setting. Refit its valve cap. [Ford spare-pressure guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

If the car has a temporary mobility kit instead, check the sealant canister's Use By date and replace expired sealant. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Inspect rubber, valves, wheels and tire age
steps.body:
Look across the tread and around accessible sidewalls for cuts, bruises, abrasions, cracking, blisters, bulges, separation and embedded objects. Examine valve stems for cracks or cuts; damaged stems require replacement. Check wheels for bends, cracks, dents, heavy corrosion or leakage. Ford also requires replacement for established elongated wheel-bolt holes or excessive runout, although measuring runout is outside this inspection. [Tire and wheel inspection](#/document/G1686502)

Damaged tires need professional assessment before further use. Do not reinflate one that has been driven flat without an internal inspection. A cracked wheel's tire must be deflated before wheel removal; arrange qualified handling rather than proceeding with ordinary rotation. Do not weld or peen a damaged wheel back into service. [Wheel and tire hazards](#/document/G1693193)

Record the DOT date code: its last four digits give the manufacturing week and year, so 2501 means week 25 of 2001. Ford generally calls for tire replacement after six years regardless of tread, potentially sooner with severe heat or loading; the spare is replaced with the road tires or after six years even if unused. [Ford damage and age guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Measure tread across the width and around the tire
steps.body:
Use the tread-depth gauge to compare the inner shoulder, center ribs and outer shoulder. Shoulders are the tread's edges; ribs are the strips between grooves. Seat the gauge on the tread with its probe reaching the groove bottom, avoiding a raised wear bar when measuring groove depth. Repeat around the circumference and at visibly worn areas. Record the lowest readings rather than averaging readings across the tire. Ford's wear tests specifically measure the affected shoulder or wear pattern. [Tread measurement and wear tests](#/document/G1686502)

Find the molded wear bars across the groove bottoms. Replace a tire when its tread is level with them, or when the affected tread measures 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less. A deeper center does not clear a worn shoulder. [Wear limits](#/document/G1686502)

As a practical inspection method, reposition the car normally to expose tread previously resting on the ground. Keep clear while it moves. Before resuming inspection, shut the engine off, set the parking brake and select Park (P) for an automatic or Reverse (R) for a manual transmission. [Ground securing sequence](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Do not crawl underneath to reach a hidden patch; complete inaccessible areas during the supported hoist inspection or have them checked. Never get beneath a vehicle held only by a jack. [Support precautions](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Decide whether rotation should proceed
steps.body:
Compare the readings and wear patterns using the diagnostic decisions below. Even wear across and around the tire is normal. Abnormal wear may remain serviceable only with tread greater than 1.6 mm (0.0629 in), no noise/vibration concern and no other disqualifying damage. [Wear assessment](#/document/G1686502)

Have uneven wear assessed and its alignment, balance or mechanical cause corrected before rotation. Rotation manages wear; it is not permission to keep using a damaged tire. If inspection is today's whole job, continue to the applicable TPMS check in step 18 and the record in step 19 without removing wheels. [Ford pre-rotation guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Choose the non-directional rotation pattern
steps.body:
Use left and right as viewed from the driver's seat. Confirm that the actual assemblies meet the fitment requirements before assigning destinations. [Wheel and tire compatibility](#/document/G1686502)

For compatible, same-size non-directional assemblies, Ford's rear-wheel-drive diagram moves the rear tires straight forward and crosses the fronts to the rear: left rear → left front; right rear → right front; left front → right rear; right front → left rear. [Ford rear-wheel-drive rotation diagram](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

For non-directional tires with different front and rear sizes, the separate diagram keeps each size on its axle: left front ↔ right front and left rear ↔ right rear. Do not move these assemblies between axles. [Ford different-size rotation diagram](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

These are the non-directional branches. If directional markings or an unusual wheel arrangement prevent applying one, leave the assemblies in their existing positions and have a tire professional establish the appropriate service. Keep every dissimilar spare out of the pattern. Write down each original position and destination before lifting. [Ford rotation restrictions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Position and raise the car on the hoist
steps.body:
Have the competent hoist operator position the car and change from the secured ground setup to the supported lifting setup. Keep the engine off, set the parking brake and place the transmission in Neutral for the hoist operation. Neutral is the wheel-removal setup; restore Park or Reverse after lowering, as directed in step 14. [Wheel-removal setup](#/document/G1686507) [Parking-brake precaution](#/document/G1693189)

Verify adequate hoist capacity for the car's actual weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the four side-body lifting locations identified by stamped triangles: behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels, as shown in Ford's lifting illustration. Position the hoist adapters at those designated locations. Lifting elsewhere can let the car shift or fall. [Mustang lifting locations](#/document/G1663631) [Capacity precautions](#/document/G1693189)

Before raising, check that the arms and adapters clear suspension, steering and exhaust parts, brackets, the axle and rear cover. Do not lift against either bumper.
