Keep the engine off throughout this wheel work. Use the hoist according to its operating instructions; the supplied emergency jack is reserved for an emergency flat-tire change. Never get beneath a car supported only by a jack. [Lift placement precautions](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Remove and identify the wheel assemblies
steps.body:
Remove the wheel nuts and lift each assembly off its hub, keeping its original position and planned destination clear in your record. Do not use heat on a seized nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Stop that removal if the nut cannot be released with the supported method. [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507)

Finish inspecting the inner sidewalls, wheel surfaces and tread areas that were hidden on the ground. Damage overrides the rotation plan. Do not pull valve stems or dismantle tires during rotation: each stem is connected to a TPMS sensor, which can be damaged by pulling it from the wheel. [Condition inspection](#/document/G1686502) [Sensor handling](#/document/G1686509)

steps.title: Clean the wheel and hub mounting faces
steps.body: Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel's mounting face and the mating hub or brake-disc face. Make sure any rotor-to-hub retaining fasteners are secure and do not obstruct the wheel's seating surface. Contamination or interference can keep the wheel from seating properly, allowing nuts to loosen and the wheel to separate while driving. [Mounting-face preparation](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Lubricate only the centering interface
steps.body: Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot—the central bore and the hub's matching centering projection. Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. Lubricant in those excluded areas can damage components and invalidate the clean, dry thread condition required for wheel-nut tightening. [Lubricant and application limits](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Install each assembly at its planned destination
steps.body: Check the destination against your written rotation map, position the wheel on the hub and start the wheel nuts by hand. Tighten them finger-tight only at this stage. Wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads must remain clean and dry because the specified torque depends on that condition. [Initial wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Lower, secure the car and complete tightening
steps.body:
Lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires. Before ground-level tightening, keep the engine off, set the parking brake and restore the transmission from Neutral to Park (P) for an automatic or Reverse (R) for a manual. Keep this secured setup through the pressure checks and TPMS work that follow. [Ground securing sequence](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

With the vehicle resting on its tires, use the torque wrench to tighten every wheel's nuts to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern: move across the wheel between nuts rather than tightening neighboring nuts around a circle. The wrong sequence can contribute to brake-disc runout, brake roughness, shudder and vibration. This specification is for clean, dry threads. [Final wheel tightening](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Verify pressure at the final wheel positions
steps.body: With the car on the ground and secured as described in step 14, use the digital gauge to check each tire against the label setting for its new position. Complete any adjustment while the tires meet the cold condition established earlier; if they have become hot from driving, do not bleed them down to the cold value. Refit every valve cap. Ford explicitly requires pressure to be checked and adjusted after rotation. [Digital-gauge requirement](#/document/G1686509) [Ford post-rotation pressure check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Enter TPMS location-calibration mode
steps.body:
After moving the assemblies, use Ford's sensor location-calibration procedure below to register the sensors at their final corners. Physical wheel work must be finished. Keep the engine off, the parking brake set and the transmission in Park (automatic) or Reverse (manual) while cycling the ignition. [Ground securing sequence](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

With the ignition OFF, press and release the brake pedal. Using the start/stop switch, cycle ignition OFF → RUN three times, ending in RUN. Press and release the brake pedal, switch ignition OFF, then cycle OFF → RUN three more times, again ending in RUN. [Manual training-mode entry](#/document/G1686523)

Successful entry produces one horn sound and a flashing TPMS indicator; the message center, if equipped, displays TRAIN LF TIRE. If that confirmation does not occur, training mode has not been established. Recheck the entry sequence before attempting to train sensors. [Mode-entry confirmation](#/document/G1686523)

steps.title: Train the four final sensor locations
steps.body:
Keep the grounded car secured throughout training. Within two minutes of the entry horn, hold tool 204-D081A (204-D081) against the left-front tire sidewall at the valve stem. Press and release its test button. Keep it in place while the sensor activates; this can take up to six seconds. A brief vehicle horn sound confirms that the body control module, or BCM, recognized that sensor. [Sensor training](#/document/G1686523)

Continue in this exact order: left front → right front → right rear → left rear. At each next corner, position the tool at the valve stem and press and release its test button within two minutes of the preceding horn sound. [Training order and timing](#/document/G1686523)

After the last tire, an equipped message center displays TIRE TRAINING COMPLETE. Without a message center, turn ignition OFF: successful completion produces no horn sound. Two horn sounds when switching OFF mean training failed. Record completion only when the appropriate confirmation occurs; a failed sequence needs correction or TPMS diagnosis. [Calibration completion checks](#/document/G1686523)

steps.title: Wake sensors if a pressure warning remains after correction
steps.body:
Use this activation check when pressures have been corrected but the warning remains, including an inspection where no wheels moved. Activation wakes sleeping sensors so they can transmit current pressure; location calibration in steps 16–17 assigns their corners. They are different operations. [Sensor activation](#/document/G1686522) [Location calibration](#/document/G1686523)

Before switching the ignition ON, confirm the grounded car has its parking brake set and its transmission in Park (automatic) or Reverse (manual). Keep the engine off. [Ground securing sequence](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Turn ignition ON. Hold tool 204-D081A (204-D081) against the left-front sidewall at the valve stem and press its test button to activate that sensor at least twice. Repeat at the remaining tires. The tool may flash green and beep, but its own feedback does not prove the vehicle received the sensor. [Activation procedure and feedback](#/document/G1686522)

If a sensor does not respond, move the grounded vehicle enough to rotate the wheels at least one-quarter turn. Before retrying, shut the engine off, set the parking brake and select Park (automatic) or Reverse (manual), then turn ignition ON with the engine remaining off. [Activation repositioning](#/document/G1686522) [Secure the repositioned car](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Retry the same sensor. Ford then specifies trying the customer activation tool if available; if it still fails to train, try training with the doors open. A warning remaining after correct inflation and activation requires TPMS diagnosis. Do not keep adding air to chase a warning. [Activation retry and diagnostic route](#/document/G1686522)

steps.title: Record the result and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
Record cold pressures, lowest tread readings, wear patterns, damage, tire dates and any outstanding action. For a rotation, also record original and final positions, completed wheel torque and the TPMS calibration result. An inspection record is a set of findings, not a guarantee against hidden damage. [Inspection criteria](#/document/G1686502) [Location verification](#/document/G1686523)

Whenever a wheel has been reinstalled, retighten its nuts within 160 km (100 mi). Initial tightening can be followed by loosening, potentially allowing wheel separation. Use the specified 150 lb-ft (204 Nm), star/cross pattern and clean, dry threads, with the car resting on its tires and secured as in step 14. [Required recheck and torque](#/document/G1686507)

watchFor.title: A tire that has been driven flat
watchFor.body: Do not simply refill it. Have it demounted and inspected internally first because hidden damage can cause failure during inflation. [Inflation hazard](#/document/G1693193)

watchFor.title: Pressure that repeatedly falls
watchFor.body: Have the tire, valve and wheel evaluated for leakage or damage. Repeated top-ups do not establish that the assembly is sound. [Condition checks](#/document/G1686502)

watchFor.title: A good center hiding a worn shoulder
watchFor.body: Measure the affected area. A shoulder or wear pattern at 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less requires replacement even when another part is deeper. [Wear tests](#/document/G1686502)

watchFor.title: Cracked wheels or contaminated mounting faces
watchFor.body: A cracked wheel requires controlled deflation before removal and replacement, not welding or peening. A serviceable wheel still needs clean mating faces to avoid loosening after installation. [Cracked-wheel precautions](#/document/G1693193) [Mounting preparation](#/document/G1686507)

watchFor.title: Tool beeps being mistaken for vehicle confirmation
watchFor.body: Activation-tool feedback alone does not prove the BCM heard a sensor. During location training, use the vehicle horn responses and the specified completion check. [Activation feedback](#/document/G1686522) [Training confirmation](#/document/G1686523)

watchFor.title: A sudden vibration while driving
watchFor.body: Reduce speed and pull off safely to inspect. If the cause cannot be found, Ford directs towing for inspection. Do not use a high-speed test to investigate an assembly already suspected of damage. [Ford highway-hazard guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

procedures.purpose: Inspect tire and wheel condition, measure tread, identify wear patterns and route further diagnosis.
Apply the digital-gauge requirement, vehicle-label pressure reference and valve-mounted sensor precautions.
Remove and refit assemblies, prepare mounting surfaces, apply XL-2 correctly and complete wheel tightening.
Identify the Mustang's triangle-marked lifting locations and apply lifting restrictions.
Explain pressure monitoring and the distinction between low-pressure and fault indications.
Enter training mode, calibrate final sensor locations and verify completion.
Wake sensors after pressure correction and route a remaining warning to diagnosis.
Handle driven-flat tires and cracked wheels safely and retain the wheel-nut recheck requirement.
Apply remote-start, personal-protection, parking-brake and hoist-capacity precautions.

stepGroups.title: Set up and check cold pressure
stepGroups.summary: Secure the car, identify the fitted assemblies and measure all applicable pressures.

stepGroups.title: Inspect, measure and choose destinations
stepGroups.summary: Find damage and wear before selecting a supported non-directional pattern.

stepGroups.title: Raise, rotate and refit
stepGroups.summary: Use the marked hoist locations, prepare the mating surfaces, lower and secure the car, then complete wheel tightening.

stepGroups.title: Verify pressure and calibrate TPMS locations
stepGroups.summary: Check final settings and obtain the vehicle's training confirmation.

stepGroups.title: Resolve warnings and close the record
stepGroups.summary: Activate sensors when needed and arrange the required wheel-nut recheck.

diagnostics.finding: Wear is even across the width and around the circumference.
diagnostics.meaning: This matches normal wear, but does not establish remaining life or rule out damage. Ford gives no guaranteed mileage for normal tire life. [Normal wear](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Compare the lowest tread reading with the wear limit and complete the damage and age checks before retaining the tire. [Wear assessment](#/document/G1686502) [Ford age guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

diagnostics.finding: Outer-shoulder tread depth is at least 50% greater than inner-shoulder depth.
diagnostics.meaning: This meets Ford's inner-edge/shoulder wear definition. Excessive toe-out or negative camber are usual associations; rotation history and high-speed cornering are also possible contributors. Appearance does not measure an alignment angle. [Inner-edge wear](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Measure the inner shoulder. Replace the tire at 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less. Above that limit, arrange alignment assessment and correction before permitted rotation. Use the separate [wheel-alignment guide](#/maintenance/wheel-alignment) for the follow-on job. [Inner-shoulder test](#/document/G1686502)

diagnostics.finding: Inner-shoulder tread depth is at least 50% greater than outer-shoulder depth.
diagnostics.meaning: This meets Ford's outer-edge/shoulder wear definition. Excessive toe-in or positive camber are usual associations, alongside rotation history and high-speed cornering. [Outer-edge wear](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Measure the outer shoulder. Replace the tire at 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less; otherwise arrange alignment assessment and correction before using the applicable rotation pattern. [Outer-shoulder test](#/document/G1686502)

diagnostics.finding: Shoulder tread blocks differ in height between their leading and trailing edges.
diagnostics.meaning: This is heel/toe wear, also called feathering. Ford lists excessive toe-in/out and incorrect rotation intervals as possible causes. [Heel/toe identification](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Measure the worn pattern. At 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less, replace the tire and arrange alignment correction. Above the limit, correct pressure and have suspension condition and alignment assessed before rotation. The [suspension guide](#/maintenance/suspension) covers the related inspection. [Heel/toe test](#/document/G1686502)

diagnostics.finding: Wear bands run diagonally across the tread and repeat around the tire.
diagnostics.meaning: This matches diagonal wear, for which Ford lists toe and rotation history among possible causes. [Diagonal wear](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Measure the worn bands. Replace at 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less. Above the limit, continued service depends on no noise/vibration concern and no other disqualifying damage. Correct pressure and arrange suspension/alignment assessment before permitted rotation. [Diagonal-wear test](#/document/G1686502)

diagnostics.finding: Cuts, bulges, separation, embedded objects or valve-stem damage are present.
diagnostics.meaning: Tread depth alone cannot clear these conditions. A cracked or cut valve stem requires replacement, and suspected internal tire damage requires a demounted inspection. [Damage checks](#/document/G1686502) [Ford internal-inspection guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)
diagnostics.next: Take the affected assembly out of the rotation plan and arrange professional evaluation or replacement before further use. Valve replacement is separate work involving the attached TPMS sensor. [Valve and sensor precautions](#/document/G1686509)

diagnostics.finding: The car wobbles or shimmies.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford's diagnostic sequence checks loose wheel nuts first, then bent wheels and damaged tires. Vibration is a symptom, not a shopping list. [Wobble diagnosis](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Check wheel-nut torque and physical condition before further driving tests. If those checks do not resolve it, arrange pressure, suspension, alignment and permitted-rotation assessment. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G1686502) [Wheel torque](#/document/G1686507)

diagnostics.finding: High-speed shake or vibration persists after basic condition checks.
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel/tire runout or other wheel, tire and suspension concerns may need measurement. Rotation alone does not confirm the cause. [Vibration diagnosis](#/document/G1686502)
diagnostics.next: Use the separate [wheel/tire runout guide](#/maintenance/wheel-tire-runout-matching) or arrange professional diagnosis. Do not mark balancing, runout or alignment as checked merely because this inspection is finished. [Runout diagnostic route](#/document/G1686502)

diagnostics.finding: The TPMS warning remains after correct pressure and sensor activation.
diagnostics.meaning: The indicator can report a system fault as well as low pressure. A flashing indicator indicates malfunction in Ford's owner guidance. [TPMS overview](#/document/G1686515) [Ford warning interpretation](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)
diagnostics.next: Arrange TPMS diagnosis. If location training failed, do not record it as complete; use the specified mode-entry, order, timing and completion checks when repeating it. [Activation diagnostic route](#/document/G1686522) [Location calibration](#/document/G1686523)

verification.title: The grounded car is secured
verification.body: After lowering or any repositioning, confirm the engine is off, the parking brake is set and the transmission is in Park for an automatic or Reverse for a manual before continuing ground-level work. Neutral is confined to the hoist operation. Finish TPMS work with the ignition OFF. [Ground securing sequence](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Hoist setup](#/document/G1686507)

verification.title: Pressure readings are cold and position-specific
verification.body: Every road tire has a recorded digital-gauge reading matching its final position's label value, with caps refitted. Include the identified spare type at its applicable setting. A hot reading has not been bled down to the cold specification. [Pressure equipment](#/document/G1686509) [Ford inflation checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Inspection findings have a clear disposition
verification.body: Confirm tread was checked across the width and around the circumference, with the lowest readings recorded. No tire at the wear bars or at 1.6 mm (0.0629 in) or less is marked acceptable. Damage, age concerns and inaccessible areas have a stated next action. [Inspection and wear limits](#/document/G1686502) [Ford age and damage guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Rotated assemblies match the chosen branch
verification.body: Compare final positions against the written same-size or different-size non-directional map. Different front/rear sizes remain on their original axles, and no dissimilar spare entered the rotation. [Ford rotation patterns](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Every removed wheel has a completed torque check
verification.body: Confirm clean mating faces, XL-2 confined to the pilot interface, clean dry threads and star/cross tightening to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires. Arrange the retightening within 160 km (100 mi). [Wheel installation checks](#/document/G1686507)

verification.title: TPMS completion is demonstrated
verification.body: For location calibration, record TIRE TRAINING COMPLETE when displayed, or the successful ignition-OFF/no-horn check on a vehicle without a message center. Two horn sounds on switching OFF mean failure. Any warning remaining after correct pressure and activation stays an open diagnostic concern. Switch ignition OFF when finished. [Training verification](#/document/G1686523) [Remaining-warning diagnosis](#/document/G1686522)

applicability.equipment: Factory 2015 wheel-end arrangements. Optional brake-off steps cover the standard front and rear disc procedures, not the separate SVT package. Confirm the fitted brakes and any wheel/suspension modifications before using specifications.

notes: This is an original diagnostic walkthrough for the documented 2015 U.S. Mustang configurations. It does not establish coverage for the separate SVT brake/hub package or modified wheel-end arrangements.

The hand-position illustration is independently designed to explain the checks. It is not a lifting-point drawing or a component identification template. Use the linked Ford illustrations for actual mounting locations.
Online supplier references supplement the Ford material. Their general symptoms are clues, not automatic replacement rules. No mileage-based bearing replacement interval is adopted.
guides.title: Wheel and hub checks: find the cause of noise and looseness
guides.summary: Track down a hum, wobble or dragging wheel with tire checks, a safe noise assessment, hands-on movement checks and an optional brake-off hub inspection. Learn what each finding means before buying parts.
guides.introduction:
I want to find the part making the complaint before asking your wallet to participate. A wheel bearing is one suspect; the tire, brake, wheel mounting, steering and suspension all share the neighborhood.

The **wheel hub** is the rotating mounting point for the wheel. Its **wheel bearing** supports that rotation. The **wheel knuckle** carries the hub; suspension joints and, at the front, steering links position the knuckle. If something rocks, we need to see **which connection moves**, not just feel movement at the tire.

This guide takes you from checks on the ground to supported, engine-off inspection. The optional brake-off branch is **advanced brake work** and is only needed when the earlier checks do not separate brake contact from a hub concern. No wheel-bearing clearance limit is invented here: a measured pass/fail decision needs the current Ford method and limit for the fitted assembly.
guides.why: A sound is a clue, not a parts number. Finding the actual source avoids replacing a perfectly useful hub while a damaged tire or dragging brake keeps making the same guest appearance. It also separates an irritating noise from movement, overheating or damage that makes driving inappropriate.

when.summary: Inspect wheel-related condition at each oil-change service; investigate a new noise, looseness or drag sooner.
notes: Predominantly dusty or sandy operation calls for these checks every 5,000 mi (8,000 km).

prepare.title: Choose your stopping point before the tools come out
prepare.detail:
**On the ground:** symptom notes, cold tire pressure, visible damage and wheel mounting. **Supported wheel:** hand rotation, gentle rocking and observing the moving joint. **Advanced branch:** remove and restore the fitted brake assembly to inspect the hub without brake-disc contact. If you cannot safely support the car or identify the brake fasteners, take your observations to a workshop; that is useful diagnosis, too.

Have a helper for watching movement. Keep fingers out of gaps between moving parts. Let hot brakes cool naturally; do not touch a disc to judge its temperature.

prepare.title: Gather the right kit
prepare.detail:
| Equipment | What I use it for |
|---|---|
| Digital tire-pressure gauge and tread-depth gauge | Record cold pressure and wear across the tread. |
| Flashlight, mirror and a notebook or phone used while parked | See inner tire edges, hardware and the exact place movement occurs. |
| Rated workshop jack, correctly rated stands, wheel chocks and the Ford lifting-point drawing; or a suitable hoist | Support the car securely before a wheel leaves the ground. |
| Correct wheel-nut socket and calibrated torque wrench capable of 204 Nm / 150 lb-ft | Wheel removal and final tightening, if needed. |
| For brake-off work: correct sockets, replacement bolts for the fitted caliper branch, caliper hanger and suitable brake cleaner | Move the brake assembly safely and restore it correctly. |
| For unresolved cases: dial indicator with suitable rigid mounting, or chassis-listening equipment | Workshop measurement or noise localization using the correct setup. |

A floor jack holds the car up while you position supports; it is not the support system. The emergency wheel-change jack is not the tool for this inspection.

prepare.title: Know the car you are checking
prepare.detail:
Write down the year, engine, front or rear location, brake package, wheel/tire sizes and recent work. Note spacers, different-offset wheels, lowered suspension, an impact or a recent wheel removal. Ford specifically excludes aftermarket-equipped vehicles from some standard suspension specifications. Use the current instructions for those parts.

Keep [the lifting-point illustration](#/document/G1663631) and [wheel fitting instructions](#/document/G1686507) available. For the optional branch, identify the actual assembly using [front brake-disc access](#/document/G1693784) or [rear brake-disc access](#/document/G1693754).

steps.title: Decide whether the car should stay parked
steps.body:
Before a road test, look for a visibly tilted or wobbling wheel, missing or loose wheel nuts, a damaged tire, severe grinding, smoke, a burning smell, a fluid leak near the brake, or changed braking/steering control. **If any is present, do not drive to “see if it gets worse.”** Arrange inspection and suitable transport. Do the same if supported checks later reveal unexplained mechanical looseness or binding.

No roadside shaking test can certify a damaged wheel end as safe. The aim here is to gather evidence without adding another problem.

steps.title: Give the tire a fair hearing
steps.body:
With the tires cold, measure and record each pressure against the vehicle tire label on the driver’s door/door pillar. Use the vehicle specification, not the maximum printed on the tire sidewall.

1. Look at both sidewalls and all the tread you can see. Check for bulges, cuts, exposed cords, embedded objects and uneven wear. Do not run a bare hand across suspected exposed cord.
2. Compare tread depth at the inner shoulder, center and outer shoulder, then at several points around the tire as access allows. Inspect the hidden circumference after safe lifting.
3. Look for alternating high/low patches or tread blocks with different leading/trailing heights. These patterns can produce noise and point to tire, alignment or suspension work. Record them rather than calling every pattern a bearing symptom.
4. Verify tire sizes and rotation direction. Do not swap staggered front/rear sizes or reverse a directional tire as a casual noise experiment.

A tire can supply its own soundtrack. Finding wear does not prove it is the only fault. References: [wheel/tire diagnosis](#/document/G1686502), [suspension preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686610).

steps.title: Check the wheel mounting before rocking anything
steps.body:
Inspect for missing nuts, damaged studs or wheel holes, a cracked wheel and visible gaps or debris at the wheel mounting. A wheel loose on its studs can imitate bearing play. If fasteners are loose, stop driving and have the mounting faces, wheel holes, studs and nuts checked for damage; simply tightening them is not proof that no damage occurred.

For the documented factory wheel fitment, final wheel-nut torque is **204 Nm / 150 lb-ft**, on **clean, dry stud and nut threads**, in a star/cross pattern with the vehicle resting on its tires. This is a wheel-nut value, **not a hub or spindle-nut value**. Do not loosen the large center nut to check the bearing. Reference: [wheel installation](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Write a useful noise description
steps.body:
Record what you already noticed: speed range, straight road versus curves, braking versus brakes released, smooth versus coarse pavement, cold versus warmed up, and whether you feel it in the steering wheel or seat. Include recent tire, brake or hub work.

Try this note: **“Low hum at a steady road speed; changes on coarse pavement; no obvious brake-pedal effect; left-front location is only my impression.”** That is much more useful than “wheel sounds expensive.” Do not type or handle a recording device while driving.

Ford warns that sound can travel through the structure and seem to come from a different place. Treat the apparent corner as a lead, not a verdict. Reference: [NVH preparation and symptom verification](#/document/G1663637).

steps.title: If safe, observe the noise during an ordinary drive
steps.body:
Only do this after the ground checks reveal no reason to stop, and only if steering and braking feel normal. Choose a quiet, familiar route, stay within legal speeds, turn off the audio/blower if practical, and have a passenger record observations or make notes after parking.

- Gently reach the speed where the complaint normally occurs; do not increase speed to chase a new or severe noise.
- Compare normal smooth and coarse pavement. A surface-related change puts tire/road interaction on the list.
- Note changes through ordinary gentle curves, staying in your lane. **Do not weave or perform abrupt steering maneuvers.**
- Observe ordinary light braking. A change directs attention to the brakes and suspension as well as the hub; it is not a diagnosis by itself.
- If the symptom only appears over bumps, inspect the suspension/steering connections rather than forcing it into a bearing explanation.

Stop the test if control changes, grinding develops or vibration worsens. Do not use a “turn left means replace right” rule. Ford lists bearings, hubs **and tire tread wear** as possible causes of a steering-sensitive noise. This is a conservative observation exercise, not the manual’s full professional road-test sequence. Reference: [NVH road-test interpretation](#/document/G1663637).

steps.title: Support the car for engine-off checks
steps.body:
Work on firm, level ground with the engine off and the key secured. Chock the wheels that remain on the ground against rolling in either direction. Use a workshop jack and stands suited to the car and the approved locations, or a suitable hoist. Identify the stamped triangle markers and the exact support geometry in [Ford’s lifting-point drawing](#/document/G1663631); do not improvise on the floorpan, differential cover, exhaust or suspension links.

Lower onto the supports and confirm they are seated and the vehicle is stable before working at the wheel. Never put any part of your body under a car held only by a jack. If the jack and stand cannot safely occupy the required locations, use a suitable lift instead.

For **front** hand checks, keep the car secured against rolling. For **rear** rotation, the parking brake and transmission can prevent movement: only select Neutral and release the parking brake after the car is securely supported, with the grounded wheels chocked. If you cannot establish that arrangement, have a workshop perform the rotation test. Restore the securing controls before lowering. **Never run the engine to spin raised wheels.**

steps.title: Rotate each wheel by hand and compare
steps.body:
With the wheel secured to the hub, turn it slowly by hand through a complete revolution. Listen for scraping, grinding or a repeating tick, and feel whether the resistance is smooth or catches at a particular position. Record which corner and where in the revolution it happens. Compare the opposite wheel on the **same axle**, with equivalent brake/gear conditions.

A light pad-on-disc brushing sound may be present. Rear wheels also turn driveline parts, so their resistance is not directly comparable with a free front wheel. There is **no “must spin three turns” rule** here. A wheel that spins quietly unloaded has not ruled out a noise that appears under road load.

Keep hands, clothing and tools clear of pinch points. Use hand force only. References: [wheel rotation and brake-drag check](#/document/G1686610), [Timken’s hand inspection]( https://www.timken.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/LV3-Checking-Hub-Assembly.pdf ), [MOOG’s note on noise that appears only while driving](https://www.moogparts.com/en-eu/pdf/technical-tips/lv/en/MOOG-ESB-Diagnosis-of-worn-wheel-end-bearings.pdf).

steps.title: Rock at 3 and 9, then at 12 and 6
steps.body:
Imagine a clock on the wheel face. Grip the tire at **3 and 9 o’clock**, gently push one side away while pulling the other toward you, then reverse. Repeat with your hands at **12 and 6 o’clock**. Feel for a knock or free movement and have your helper watch the assembly. Do not shake hard enough to disturb the vehicle supports.

This checks movement in two directions; the hand position does **not** identify the failed part. Tire sidewall flex and normal steering movement are different from a loose joint. Reference: [Timken’s two-position hand check](https://www.timken.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/LV3-Checking-Hub-Assembly.pdf).

steps.title: Find the connection that actually moves
steps.body:
Repeat the gentle rocking while your helper uses a light or mirror to watch from a safe position. Keep fingers out of the joints.

| What moves relative to what? | What that tells us |
|---|---|
| Wheel shifts on the studs/mounting face | Investigate the wheel mounting first; do not condemn the bearing from this result. |
| Wheel and hub move relative to the knuckle | Investigate hub/bearing attachment and bearing condition. Correct clamping matters. |
| Knuckle and wheel move together, with a joint visibly shifting | Trace the movement to suspension links, ball joints or steering connections. |
| Front wheel steers smoothly but no free movement is localized | Steering motion is not a bearing-play measurement. Continue diagnosis if the symptom persists. |

At the front, watch the tie rod connection and lower suspension joints. At the rear, look at the locating links and their knuckle connections. Do not assume all play at 12/6 is a bearing, or all play at 3/9 is a tie rod. If the source is hidden or unclear, record **“movement present; source not localized”** and stop using the car until assessed. Do not pry on a boot or loosen a joint to make the test easier. References: [suspension symptom chart](#/document/G1686610), [steering diagnosis](#/document/G1757488).

steps.title: Check whether the brake releases
steps.body:
With the brakes fully assembled and the car safely supported, have a helper apply and release the service brake. Then turn the wheel by hand again. For rear wheels, confirm the parking brake is released under the securing conditions in step 6.

Compare before/after resistance. If one wheel is substantially harder to rotate or binds after release, investigate its brake caliper, sliding/mounting parts and, at the rear, parking-brake mechanism. If several wheels drag, the cause can be elsewhere in the brake system. These are different branches in Ford’s diagnosis.

Do not open a bleeder, loosen a hydraulic line, disconnect a hose or adjust a hub nut as an exploratory shortcut. Those actions change the system and require their own repair/bleeding procedure. If the disc is hot, let it cool; a hot corner does not distinguish brake heat from bearing trouble. Reference: [brake-drag component check](#/document/G1721936).

steps.title: Choose the next check from your findings
steps.body:
**Tire damage or a loose wheel mounting:** stop and correct that condition first, then reassess. **Visible movement at a suspension/steering joint:** follow that component’s diagnosis. **Binding after brake release:** follow the brake branch. **Roughness or play not yet localized:** the optional brake-off inspection below can help separate disc/pad contact from the hub itself.

If everything feels smooth but the road noise remains, skip speculative disassembly and use the workshop-localization step later in this guide. A result of “not reproduced on stands” is useful information; it is not a certificate of bearing health. The findings table below collects these branches in one place.

steps.title: Optional advanced branch: remove the wheel and inspect behind it
steps.body:
Proceed only if you can identify and correctly restore the fitted brake assembly. Let it cool, secure the car as in step 6, remove the wheel nuts and wheel, and inspect the wheel’s rear mating face, hub/disc mating area, studs, disc shield, visible pad wear, caliper mounting and hose routing. Look for fresh contact marks, trapped debris or a shield contacting the disc. Do not bend, pry or replace parts until the actual interference is identified.

Do not loosen the center hub/spindle nut. This diagnosis keeps the bearing clamped in its assembled condition. If the nut or hub attachment is suspect, stop for the correct repair and damage assessment.

For disc removal, choose **one** of the next two steps according to the axle. The separate SVT procedure and modified brake kits are outside these branches. Read the restoration step before undoing anything. References: [wheel removal](#/document/G1686507), [standard front hub construction](#/document/G1692537), [rear hub construction](#/document/G1686657).

steps.title: Front only: move the caliper assembly aside and remove the disc
steps.body:
Identify the caliper by the actual fitted hardware, not engine size alone. Follow [the standard front disc drawing](#/document/G1693784) to identify the **two mounting bolts**; do not confuse them with hose or bleed fittings.

1. Arrange a proper caliper hanger before removing the bolts.
2. Remove the two mounting bolts and move the caliper/pad assembly aside. Support it without stretching, twisting or loading the brake hose.
3. For the **4-piston or 6-piston branch**, discard those bolts and have the specified new bolts ready. The 2-piston branch does not give that same discard instruction.
4. Remove the brake disc to expose the hub’s rotating mounting face.

Do not disconnect the hydraulic hose and **do not press the brake pedal with the caliper/disc removed**. Skip the rear-only step and continue to the hub check. Reinstallation torque for the specified front mounting bolts is **115 Nm / 85 lb-ft**; identify them using the figure, not this number alone.

steps.title: Rear only: move the caliper and anchor plate aside
steps.body:
Use [the standard rear disc drawing](#/document/G1693754) to locate the **two caliper/anchor-plate mounting bolts**. The parking brake must be released with the car secured as described in step 6.

1. Arrange support for the complete caliper/anchor-plate assembly.
2. Remove and **discard the two mounting bolts**. Position the assembly aside with the hose and parking-brake cable unstressed; do not let either carry its weight.
3. Remove the brake disc. Leave the halfshaft and spindle nut installed for this diagnosis.

Do not operate the brake pedal or parking brake with the assembly removed. On restoration, use the specified **new mounting bolts at 175 Nm / 129 lb-ft**. This is the rear caliper/anchor-plate value, not the hub-bolt or spindle-nut specification.

steps.title: Check the exposed hub and compare with the assembled result
steps.body:
Turn the exposed hub by hand and check for roughness, noise or looseness with the bearing clamping untouched. Compare with the earlier wheel-on result. If a scraping sound disappears, inspect the removed brake parts and contact marks; disappearance alone does not certify the bearing. If roughness or movement remains, localize it at the hub/knuckle and assess bearing condition and attachment. The rear halfshaft still transmits driveline resistance.

Do not spin the hub with compressed air, dismantle the sealed bearing or add grease as a diagnostic experiment. A confirmed bearing fault needs the correct assembly repair. If uncertain, restore the brakes and wheel correctly before moving the vehicle and continue with specialist diagnosis. Reference: [Timken’s exposed-hub check](https://www.timken.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/LV3-Checking-Hub-Assembly.pdf); Mustang assembly references: [front hub](#/document/G1692537), [rear hub](#/document/G1686657).

steps.title: Restore the brakes and wheel before moving the car
steps.body:
1. Clean the disc/hub mating surfaces using the specified method and brake cleaner. Keep debris and lubricant away from friction surfaces. Refit the disc.
2. Restore the correct caliper assembly, with replacement bolts where required: **front 115 Nm / 85 lb-ft**; **standard rear, new bolts 175 Nm / 129 lb-ft**. Check hose/cable routing and remove the hanger.
3. With every brake component fully installed, apply the brake pedal several times and confirm normal firm pedal feel. Check for leaks and that the brake applies/releases. If pedal travel or feel is abnormal, do not drive.
4. Clean the wheel and hub/disc mounting faces; confirm no retaining hardware prevents the wheel sitting flush. Fit the wheel and finger-start all nuts.
5. Ford specifies a thin coat of XL-2 only at the **wheel pilot bore/hub pilot interface**, not on the flat mounting faces, studs, nuts or brake friction surfaces. Keep the wheel-nut threads clean and dry.
6. Restore the vehicle’s securing controls and lower it using the proper lifting procedure. Final-tighten wheel nuts in a star/cross pattern with the vehicle resting on the tires: **204 Nm / 150 lb-ft**. Recheck within **100 mi / 160 km** after wheel reinstallation.

Never use a road test to find out whether the brakes went back together correctly. References: [front brake restoration](#/document/G1693784), [rear brake restoration](#/document/G1693754), [wheel installation](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: For an unresolved noise, ask for a targeted next test
steps.body:
Bring your notes and ask for **localization**, not an automatic hub replacement. Useful next checks include chassis-listening equipment during a controlled road test, a tire/wheel investigation for imbalance or out-of-round condition, or a dial-indicator check using the current Ford setup and specification.

**Bearing endplay** is movement along the axle direction under an applied load. **Runout** is the measured variation as a surface rotates. They are not interchangeable readings. A loose mounting or an incorrectly positioned gauge can mislead either test; this guide supplies no universal millimeter limit.

If an ABS warning accompanies the complaint, record the codes with a capable scan tool and investigate the wheel-speed signal, sensor and wiring as directed. An ABS lamp alone is not proof of a failed bearing. References: [NVH tools and diagnosis](#/document/G1663637), [wheel/tire diagnosis](#/document/G1686502), [ABS diagnosis](#/document/G2117220).

steps.title: Prove the result, and write it down
steps.body:
After the confirmed cause is repaired and all safety checks pass, repeat the original observation under comparable safe conditions. Check that the noise, looseness or drag is resolved—not merely quieter on a different road. Recheck the disturbed area for correct mounting, leaks, rubbing and abnormal heat symptoms. If the complaint persists, return to the recorded findings rather than replacing the next part on the shelf.

Record **corner → symptom → observed movement/noise → confirmed cause → repair → verification**. Include the wheel-nut recheck if a wheel was removed. I would much rather leave the next owner a useful trail than “vibes were off; installed shiny thing.”

watchFor.title: The giant center nut is not an adjustment knob
watchFor.body: The supplied front and rear hub procedures require new fasteners and different tightening methods. Do not tighten or loosen the hub/spindle nut experimentally to hide play.

watchFor.title: A brake-off result needs careful interpretation
watchFor.body: Removing brake contact changes what you feel. Rear driveline resistance remains. A noise disappearing on stands does not settle a load-dependent bearing complaint.

watchFor.title: A numeric limit without its measurement setup
watchFor.body: Do not borrow a generic endplay or runout limit from a different bearing design. The instrument position, load direction, assembled condition and vehicle specification belong together.

procedures.purpose: Suspension inspection and symptom charts; distinguishes wheel-bearing, steering, tire and brake concerns.
Tire wear, damage and wheel/tire vibration diagnosis.
Noise and vibration diagnosis, symptom recording and electronic listening tools.
Approved lifting points and supported-vehicle precautions.
Wheel removal and installation: clean mating faces, dry threads, star pattern, 204 Nm and 100-mile recheck.
Brake-drag checks and the distinction between one-wheel and multiple-wheel concerns.
Standard front brake-disc access: caliper-specific bolt replacement, 115 Nm and pedal restoration.
Standard rear brake-disc access: supported caliper/anchor assembly, new bolts, 175 Nm and pedal restoration.
Standard front bearing/hub repair after diagnosis; new hub nut and grease cap.
Rear bearing/hub repair after diagnosis; new fasteners and staged spindle-nut tightening.
Steering diagnosis when movement or noise is traced to steering components.
ABS and stability-control diagnosis when wheel-speed faults accompany the complaint.

stepGroups.summary: Steps 1–3 · Decide whether to drive, inspect the tires and check wheel mounting.

stepGroups.title: Describe and safely reproduce the noise
stepGroups.summary: Steps 4–5 · Collect clues without treating one sound as a diagnosis.

stepGroups.title: Check rotation, looseness and brake release
stepGroups.summary: Steps 6–11 · Engine off, car securely supported: find what actually moves or drags.

stepGroups.title: If needed: inspect the hub with the brakes moved aside
stepGroups.summary: Steps 12–16 · Advanced branch. Choose the fitted front or rear brake procedure, inspect, then restore everything.

stepGroups.title: Resolve the remaining clues and verify the result

diagnostics.finding: Damaged tire, loose/missing wheel nuts, wobble, severe grinding or impaired control
diagnostics.meaning: There is a condition that can make further driving unsafe.
diagnostics.next: Keep the car parked; arrange inspection and suitable transport. Do not continue a road test.

diagnostics.finding: Hum changes with pavement; tire has uneven tread
diagnostics.meaning: Tire/road interaction is a credible source. More than one fault can coexist.
diagnostics.next: Record pressure, wear and conditions; follow tire/wheel diagnosis before condemning a hub.

diagnostics.finding: Noise changes on ordinary curves
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel loading changes; tire wear and hub/bearing concerns remain possible.
diagnostics.next: Compare supported checks and use professional localization if needed. Do not select a side from turn direction alone.

diagnostics.finding: Wheel moves relative to its mounting face
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel attachment must be investigated.
diagnostics.next: Check the wheel, studs, nuts and mating surfaces for damage; do not drive on unexplained looseness.

diagnostics.finding: Wheel/hub moves relative to knuckle
diagnostics.meaning: Bearing condition or hub attachment/clamping needs assessment.
diagnostics.next: Keep the central fastener undisturbed for diagnosis. Use the correct front/rear repair after confirming the cause.

diagnostics.finding: Knuckle and wheel move together; movement is visible at a joint
diagnostics.meaning: Suspension or steering movement may be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Identify the exact joint and apply its inspection method; hand position alone is not a diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: One wheel binds after the brake is released
diagnostics.meaning: A local brake or parking-brake issue is possible.
diagnostics.next: Follow brake diagnosis. Several dragging wheels require a different system-level investigation.

diagnostics.finding: Hand checks are quiet but road noise persists
diagnostics.meaning: The unloaded test has not reproduced the operating condition.
diagnostics.next: Use chassis listening, tire/wheel diagnosis or specified measurements. Do not declare the bearing good solely because it has no detectable hand play.

verification.title: Before any road observation
verification.body: No unresolved dangerous tire/wheel condition, abnormal brake or steering control, severe grinding, binding or unexplained mechanical looseness. If present, transport the car for assessment.

verification.title: After a wheel or brake was removed
verification.body: Correct parts and required new bolts installed; specified torque applied; hoses/cables unstressed; normal firm brake pedal and brake release verified; wheel seated flush; dry-thread wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern; tools and supports cleared.

verification.title: A diagnosis you can explain
verification.body: You can identify the observed fault and the evidence linking it to the symptom. If you cannot, record the uncertainty and the next specific test. A replacement part is not evidence by itself.

verification.title: After repair
verification.body: Original symptom checked under comparable safe conditions; no remaining looseness, drag, leak or rubbing; wheel nuts rechecked within 100 mi / 160 km if a wheel was reinstalled.

references.title: Timken · Checking a hub bearing assembly
references.description: Two-position hand check and exposed-hub inspection; general technique, not Mustang fastener specifications.

references.title: Timken · Symptoms of a worn wheel hub bearing
references.description: Explains overlapping symptoms and why noise, wobble or brake effects need diagnosis.

references.title: MOOG · Diagnosis of worn wheel-end bearings
references.description: Notes that a wheel-bearing noise may only be noticeable while driving. Its generic replacement mileage is not used here.

notes: Applicability remains the 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines. Front access branches follow the fitted caliper package; rear access follows the standard rear pad procedure.

Pad replacement, disc removal or machining, hose replacement, pressure bleeding and parking-brake service remain separate jobs. Complete any required repair before returning the vehicle to use. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)
guides.title: Visual brake inspection: pads, discs and hoses
guides.summary: Inspect your 2015 Mustang’s brake condition, access the pads using the correct brake-package procedure, and put everything back securely. Wear specifications are included as references; this visual inspection does not certify measured dimensions.
guides.introduction: I start with what the brakes are doing, then inspect the hardware. A squeal, a pull and a sinking pedal tell different stories; ordering pads for all three is expensive parts roulette. This guide covers visual inspection and package-specific pad access and restoration on the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Choose the fitted 2-, 4- or 6-piston front branch and the standard rear branch. Precision wear measurements, runout testing and repairs are follow-on jobs when the findings call for them. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936), [2-piston front](#/document/G1693786), [4-piston front](#/document/G1693790), [6-piston front](#/document/G1693791), [Rear pads](#/document/G1693756)
guides.why: The pads grip the disc’s friction surfaces during braking. Inspecting both pads, their retaining hardware, the disc and the flexible hose helps distinguish worn friction material from a caliper, guide-pin or hydraulic problem. Uneven wear or drag can have several causes; fresh pads can leave the damn problem exactly where it was. [Brake symptom chart](#/document/G1721936)

when.summary: Inspect pads, discs, hoses and parking-brake condition at each oil-change service.
notes: A change in stopping performance, a fluid leak or a brake warning needs attention before the next scheduled service.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted brakes
prepare.detail: Confirm which front caliper package is installed: 2, 4 or 6 pistons. Piston count describes the caliper’s hydraulic pistons, not its retaining pins. Select the matching branch and thickness references; do not assume the engine alone identifies the brakes. The rear instructions here cover the standard rear pad procedure. [2-piston front](#/document/G1693786), [4-piston front](#/document/G1693790), [6-piston front](#/document/G1693791), [Rear pads](#/document/G1693756)

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and personal protection
prepare.detail: Have a suitably rated workshop jack and stands, or a suitably rated hoist, plus wheel chocks. Locate the stamped triangles identifying the lifting points. The emergency tire-changing jack is not the service jack for this work. Wear eye and ear protection during service and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged components. [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631), [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Gather access tools and keep parts organized
prepare.detail: Match hand tools to the actual wheel nuts and applicable brake fasteners. Have a torque wrench suitable for the branch-specific settings and the wheel-nut setting of 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). The 4- and 6-piston front branches require a brake pad spreader. Arrange an independent caliper support for the 2-piston front and rear branches; their illustrations show a support hook. A light and a way to label each pad’s position will make the inspection easier. [Wheel service](#/document/G1686507), [2-piston access](#/document/G1693786), [4-piston access](#/document/G1693790), [6-piston access](#/document/G1693791), [Rear access](#/document/G1693756)

prepare.title: Keep friction surfaces clean from the start
prepare.detail: Keep oil, grease and wheel lubricant away from the pads and disc friction surfaces throughout handling. Wheel installation specifies Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, applied sparingly only at the hub-pilot/wheel-pilot-bore interface—the surfaces that center the wheel. Keep it off the flat mounting faces, studs and nuts as well. Review the product’s safety information before use. [Wheel lubricant restrictions](#/document/G1686507), [Material precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Set up a useful inspection record
prepare.detail: Record findings separately for each wheel and for each inner and outer pad. Keep visual observations separate from actual measurements. The specification values below help identify what a properly equipped dimensional inspection must assess; they are not an invitation to estimate millimeters by eye. [Wear specifications](#/document/G1694687)

steps.title: Record the symptoms before taking anything apart
steps.body: Note noise, pulling, vibration, dragging, unusual pedal effort or unusual pedal travel. Record when it happens: first application, continuously, during braking or after release. Include recent brake work, because an earlier repair can contribute to the present concern. Use observations already available; this guide does not require reproducing a dangerous fault on the road. Ford’s diagnostic routes depend on the actual symptom being present. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936), [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the car. Switch the ignition off and remove the key to prevent someone starting the vehicle during service. Unexpected starting can cause serious injury. Put on the protection listed in preparation before handling components. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Raise and support the car securely
steps.body:
For jack access, work on a hard, level surface, apply the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack’s capacity covers the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Identify the lifting locations by their stamped triangles, raise the vehicle at the correct points and support it on stands. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack: unintended lowering or movement can crush you. [Jacking safety](#/document/G1693189), [Lifting locations](#/document/G1663631)

For hoist access, the wheel procedure specifies positioning the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Use adequate hoist capacity and the prescribed lifting locations. Check lift-arm and adapter clearance around suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components before raising. Do not lift by either bumper. [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507), [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189), [Lifting restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

Keep the car immobilized throughout the work. The rear-access branch includes a controlled parking-brake release; the parking brake and wheel restraints must be restored before lowering and final wheel tightening. [Vehicle restraint precautions](#/document/G1693189), [Rear brake mechanism](#/document/G1693756)

steps.title: Remove the wheel and make an initial visual check
steps.body:
Remove the wheel nuts and wheel at the position being inspected. Do not heat a seized wheel nut: heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507)

Look at the accessible pads, disc surfaces, flexible hose and retaining hardware. Record damage, apparent uneven wear, missing clips, broken springs and leakage. If the view does not let you assess both pads properly, use the matching access branch below. Follow only the applicable branch at each wheel. Disc removal is not part of this visual inspection. [Component inspection](#/document/G1721936)

steps.title: Access the pads: 2-piston front
steps.body:
Remove the two caliper guide-pin bolts and position the caliper aside on independent support. Never suspend it from the flexible hose; its weight can damage the hose. These guide-pin bolts tighten to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) during reassembly. [2-piston caliper access](#/document/G1693786)

Note each pad’s position before removing it. Remove the pads, then the upper and lower pad clips, preserving their positions. The clips differ: the one with a tab belongs at the top of the anchor plate, the bracket carrying the pads. Ford makes piston compression conditional on installing new pads in this branch, so do not add it to routine inspection. [2-piston pads and clips](#/document/G1693786)

steps.title: Access the pads: 4-piston front
steps.body: Remove the pad spring, then the pad-pin clip, then the two pad pins. Preserve their fitted positions. Use a brake pad spreader to compress the caliper pistons and remove the pads. Label the pads by their original positions. This access route leaves the caliper mounted. [4-piston pad access](#/document/G1693790)

steps.title: Access the pads: 6-piston front
steps.body: Remove the two pad pins, then the pad spring retainer clip, then the caliper pin bolt. Keep their positions clear. Use a brake pad spreader to compress the pistons, then remove and identify the pads. The caliper pin bolt tightens to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) during reassembly; it is distinct from the caliper mounting bolts. [6-piston pad access](#/document/G1693791)

steps.title: Access the pads: standard rear
steps.body:
Before releasing the parking brake, confirm the car is securely supported and every wheel remaining on the ground is blocked. Release the parking brake only after those restraints are established, and keep the car immobilized while the rear brake is apart. This sequencing allows access to the caliper containing the parking-brake mechanism without relying on that brake to secure the car. [Vehicle restraint precautions](#/document/G1693189), [Rear brake mechanism](#/document/G1693756)

Remove the two caliper bolts and support the caliper aside independently. Do not let it hang from its hose. Remove and identify the pads, then remove the clips. The two caliper bolts tighten to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) on reassembly. Rear piston retraction is conditional on fitting new pads; it is not required merely to inspect the existing pads. [Rear pad access](#/document/G1693756)

steps.title: Inspect both pads and the retaining hardware
steps.body:
Examine each pad’s friction material and attaching hardware for damage. Compare the inner pad—the one toward the vehicle—with the outer pad. Note visible differences in wear, including a pad that appears thinner at one edge. Keep the wheel position and pad position attached to each finding. Ford calls for pad, disc and hardware inspection when grinding or moaning is continuous. [Pad inspection](#/document/G1721936)

Check the clips, pins and springs used by your brake package for missing, broken or damaged pieces. Inspect accessible guide pins and their bolts for obvious damage. Rattling can come from these components or a loose disc shield. A damaged or missing retainer needs the matching repair, not a hopeful reassembly. [Rattle diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

For reference, minimum pad thickness is **0.118 in (3 mm)** and maximum taper wear in any direction is **0.118 in (3 mm)**. Taper is the difference in wear across the pad, separate from its minimum thickness. Visual inspection can identify suspicious wear; it cannot establish compliance with either number. Arrange dimensional inspection when remaining thickness or taper is uncertain, or when symptoms require verification against specifications. [Pad wear limits](#/document/G1694687), [Grinding diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

steps.title: Inspect the discs and keep their limits straight
steps.body:
Inspect the accessible braking surfaces for damage and excessive corrosion, rust or pitting. Record which face and wheel position are affected. Significant surface deterioration needs further disc assessment; do not treat noise alone as permission to machine a disc. [Disc condition](#/document/G1694691), [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

These are **reference minimum thicknesses**, not results of this visual inspection:

| Disc application | Minimum thickness |
| --- | --- |
| Front, 2-piston caliper | 1.122 in (28.5 mm) |
| Front, 4-piston caliper | 1.201 in (30.5 mm) |
| Front, 6-piston caliper | 1.244 in (31.6 mm) |
| Rear, solid disc | 0.390 in (9.9 mm) |
| Rear, vented disc | 0.925 in (23.5 mm) |

Use the fitted front package and rear disc type when arranging measurements. A valid measurement below the applicable minimum establishes that the disc is outside specification. Apparent condition alone cannot establish remaining thickness. [Disc thickness specifications](#/document/G1694687)

For pulsation or vibration, continue with [Brake pulsation and disc runout](#/maintenance/brake-pulsation-runout). Ford distinguishes normal ABS feedback from vibration associated with brake or suspension faults. [Vibration diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

steps.title: Inspect the flexible hoses and connections
steps.body:
Inspect accessible hose lengths and connections for external damage, leakage and routing problems. Record the location of each defect. A hose that looks sound externally has not thereby passed an internal-blockage test. Ford’s preliminary checks include hose damage, leakage, blockage and routing. [Hose checks](#/document/G1693185)

Keep the hydraulic connections closed for this inspection. Hose replacement is a separate repair and requires brake-system bleeding afterward. [Front hose service](#/document/G1693794), [Rear hose service](#/document/G1693757)

steps.title: Restore the 2-piston front brake
steps.body:
If the findings permit reassembly of the existing components, install the lower and upper pad clips, with the tabbed clip at the top of the anchor plate. Return the pads to their recorded positions. Position the caliper over the pads, install its two guide-pin bolts and tighten them to **24 lb.ft (32 Nm)**. Maintain independent support until the caliper is secured. [2-piston reassembly](#/document/G1693786)

If pads or hardware need replacement, use the matching replacement procedure before returning the car to use. New front pads require all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the kit, with lubricant applied according to its instruction sheet. [2-piston replacement requirements](#/document/G1693786)

steps.title: Restore the 4-piston front brake
steps.body:
If no repair is required, return the pads to their recorded positions. Reinstall the two pad pins, then the pad-pin clip, then the pad spring. Check that all retaining components are seated in their fitted positions. These are the actual restoration actions behind Ford’s instruction to reverse removal. [4-piston reassembly](#/document/G1693790)

If new pads are required, complete the matching replacement procedure using all new kit hardware and the supplied lubricant as directed by the pad instruction sheet. [4-piston replacement requirements](#/document/G1693790)

steps.title: Restore the 6-piston front brake
steps.body:
If no repair is required, return the pads to their recorded positions. Install the caliper pin bolt and tighten it to **22 lb.ft (30 Nm)**. Reinstall the pad spring retainer clip, then the two pad pins. Confirm all retaining components are seated in their fitted positions. [6-piston reassembly](#/document/G1693791)

If new pads are required, complete the matching replacement procedure using all new kit hardware and the supplied lubricant according to the pad instruction sheet. [6-piston replacement requirements](#/document/G1693791)

steps.title: Restore the standard rear brake
steps.body:
Reinstall the clips and return the pads to their recorded positions if no repair is required. Before fitting the caliper, make sure the notch in the piston aligns with the pin on the inboard pad. Position the caliper, install its two bolts and tighten them to **24 lb.ft (32 Nm)**. Keep the parking brake released until the disturbed rear brakes are completely assembled. [Rear reassembly](#/document/G1693756)

If fitting new pads is necessary, use the rear replacement procedure and its brake caliper piston retractor. Ford requires force toward the piston to engage the internal parking-brake mechanism during retraction; do not substitute the front compression operation. Replacement is a separate job from the visual inspection taught here. [Rear piston requirements](#/document/G1693756)

steps.title: Restore pedal operation and check for leakage
steps.body:
With every disturbed pad, caliper and retainer fully installed, depress the brake pedal and check the brake-fluid reservoir level. Each pad procedure requires these completion checks. If topping up is necessary, the specified fluid is **Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2**. Use [Brake and clutch fluid](#/maintenance/brake-fluid) for the separate reservoir-level check. [2-piston completion](#/document/G1693786), [4-piston completion](#/document/G1693790), [6-piston completion](#/document/G1693791), [Rear completion](#/document/G1693756), [Fluid specification](#/document/G1694687)

If excessive pedal travel was a concern, Ford calls for inspecting the flexible hoses during brake application. Have an assistant apply the pedal while you observe the accessible hoses and connections, keeping clear of moving brake components. Leakage, hose damage, or a low, spongy or sinking pedal requires further diagnosis and repair. A top-up does not repair the cause. [Pedal and hose diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

steps.title: Prepare the wheel mounting surfaces
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting surface and the mating hub or disc surface. Check that any rotor-retaining fasteners are secured and do not interfere with the mounting faces. Debris or interference can allow wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to detach while driving. [Wheel mounting safety](#/document/G1686507)

Apply a thin coat of **Motorcraft XL-2 high-temperature nickel anti-seize** only between the hub pilot and wheel pilot bore. Keep it off the flat mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces. [Wheel lubricant placement](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Refit the wheels and restore restraints before lowering
steps.body:
Position each removed wheel and install its nuts finger-tight initially. [Initial wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

After all disturbed rear brakes are fully assembled and the pedal completion check is done, reapply the parking brake while the car is still supported. Retain wheel chocks on wheels already on the ground, and have chocks positioned to restrain the car as the tires return to the ground. Keep the parking brake and wheel restraints in place during lowering and ground-level final tightening, including when the hoist route began in NEUTRAL. Do not lower an unsecured car and then try to catch up with the restraints. [Parking-brake mechanism and completion](#/document/G1693756), [Vehicle restraint requirements](#/document/G1693189), [Wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Complete final wheel tightening
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires and secured against movement, tighten the wheel nuts in a **star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm)**. This specification requires clean, dry wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads. The tightening pattern matters: uneven tightening can increase disc runout and contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration. [Final wheel tightening](#/document/G1686507)

Retighten the nuts within **160 km (100 mi)** after wheel reinstallation. Wheels can loosen after the initial tightening, so record this follow-up rather than trusting memory. [Wheel-nut follow-up](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Close the visual inspection and route any further work
steps.body:
Record each wheel’s pad condition, visible wear differences, disc condition, retaining-hardware condition and hose findings. Mark areas that could not be adequately seen. Record any actual measurements separately, using the correct package-specific limits. Complete this job as a visual inspection; do not label unmeasured parts dimensionally within specification. [Component inspection](#/document/G1721936), [Wear specifications](#/document/G1694687)

Arrange further inspection or repair for damage, uncertain wear, continuous grinding, pulling, dragging or vibration. Use [Parking brake](#/maintenance/parking-brake) for its separate holding-and-release check. Do not return the car to driving with an unresolved leak, reduced braking or abnormal pedal behavior. These require brake-system diagnosis, not a reassuring tick beside “pads inspected.” [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

watchFor.title: A caliper supported by its hose
watchFor.body: Independently support a moved-aside caliper. Its weight can damage the flexible hose, turning an inspection into a hydraulic repair. [Front handling](#/document/G1693786), [Rear handling](#/document/G1693756)

watchFor.title: Confusing retaining hardware with mounting hardware
watchFor.body: The 2-piston front guide-pin bolts and standard rear caliper bolts use 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). The 6-piston pad-access pin bolt uses 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). Apply each setting only to the identified fastener; these pad-access branches do not require removing disc-service mounting hardware. [2-piston fasteners](#/document/G1693786), [Rear fasteners](#/document/G1693756), [6-piston fastener](#/document/G1693791)

watchFor.title: Calling a visual check a runout test
watchFor.body: Installed disc runout—the disc’s side-to-side movement as it rotates—has a maximum of 0.002 in (0.05 mm). Looking at a disc does not establish that value. Route persistent pulsation or speed-related vibration to the separate diagnostic inspection. [Runout specification](#/document/G1694687), [Vibration diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

watchFor.title: Treating a thickness limit as machining permission
watchFor.body: Disc machining is a separate repair. Ford prohibits machining cross-drilled friction surfaces and prohibits machining when starting thickness is below the applicable minimum plus 0.6 mm (0.0236 in). Noise alone is not a reason to machine a disc. [Machining restrictions](#/document/G1694691)

watchFor.title: Losing the parking-brake transition
watchFor.body: Release the parking brake for rear pad access only after secure support and wheel blocking are established. Reapply it after rear reassembly and pedal checks, before lowering or final wheel tightening, while maintaining wheel restraints. [Vehicle restraints](#/document/G1693189), [Rear brake completion](#/document/G1693756)

procedures.purpose: Interpret brake symptoms, inspect relevant components and select further diagnosis.
Access and restore pads and clips on the 2-piston front package.
Access and restore pads and retainers on the 4-piston front package.
Access and restore pads and retainers on the 6-piston front package.
Access and restore standard rear pads with correct piston-to-pad alignment.
Identify lifting points and lifting restrictions.
Reference package-specific wear limits and the specified brake fluid.
Remove and reinstall wheels with correct surface preparation and tightening.
Establish service protection, starting precautions and vehicle restraints.

stepGroups.title: Record the concern and reach the brakes
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting, secure the vehicle and remove the wheels.

stepGroups.title: Choose the matching pad-access branch
stepGroups.summary: Follow the fitted front package or standard rear procedure.

stepGroups.title: Inspect pads, discs, hardware and hoses
stepGroups.summary: Record visible findings and distinguish them from dimensional measurements.

stepGroups.title: Restore the disturbed brakes
stepGroups.summary: Reinstall the matching hardware, apply specified torques and complete pedal checks.

stepGroups.title: Refit the wheels and record the result
stepGroups.summary: Restore restraints before lowering, tighten the wheels and route outstanding concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Brief first-morning squeal, intermittent squeal in changing conditions, or low-speed groaning with light braking.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies these patterns as potentially acceptable operating conditions involving temperature, humidity or environmental exposure. [Noise chart](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Record the circumstances and complete the visual inspection. Noise alone does not establish which part needs replacement. [Noise diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Continuous squeal, grinding or moaning.
diagnostics.meaning: Continuous squeal calls for pad inspection. Continuous grinding or moaning requires inspection of pads, discs and attaching hardware, including verification against dimensional specifications. [Noise diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Arrange the necessary dimensional inspection and repair based on its findings. A completed visual checklist alone does not resolve this symptom. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936), [Wear limits](#/document/G1694687)

diagnostics.finding: Visible uneven pad wear, pulling during braking, or locking under light pedal force.
diagnostics.meaning: Pads, discs, calipers, guide pins or flexible hoses can be involved. Pulling can also involve tires, suspension or alignment. [Brake symptom chart](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Have the associated components assessed before treating pad replacement as the whole repair. Route tire or suspension findings to their respective diagnosis. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Leakage, reduced braking, a low or spongy pedal, or a pedal that sinks.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include fluid leakage, air and hydraulic or caliper faults. The appearance of the pads cannot clear these concerns. [Pedal diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Keep the car out of driving use until diagnosed and repaired. Where hydraulic repair requires bleeding, use the matching repair workflow and [Pressure bleeding](#/maintenance/brake-pressure-bleeding). [Hydraulic diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Rattling at a brake assembly.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include guide pins or their bolts, missing or damaged clips or springs, and a loose disc shield. [Rattle diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Identify the affected component and complete its repair. Do not guess a shield-fastener torque or tighten unrelated bolts as a cure. [Rattle diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Brake drag or shudder after pedal release.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford routes this toward drag diagnosis, which can involve parking-brake components, calipers, guide pins, hoses and other hydraulic or actuation components. [Drag diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)
diagnostics.next: Arrange the relevant diagnosis and include the separate parking-brake check. New friction material alone does not establish that the drag is repaired. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: Pedal pulsation with hydraulic-unit noise during heavy braking or on a loose or slippery surface.
