verification.title: Unresolved concerns have a next action
verification.body: A confirmed leak, visible damage or unexplained noise needs the corresponding diagnosis or repair. Submersion needs prompt assessment even if the level is correct. [Axle diagnosis](#/document/G2214741) · [Ford water-exposure guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649140&Uid=G1634877&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

notes: Scope remains the 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Connection and support checks follow the equipment actually fitted.
Shaft removal, exhaust removal, U-joint replacement, runout correction and balancing are follow-up jobs, not routine inspection prerequisites.
guides.title: Driveshaft and U-joints: check movement, noise and mounting
guides.summary: Inspect the installed driveshaft, joints and supports on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Check for damage, binding, unwanted movement and mounting problems, then choose the right diagnostic next step.
guides.introduction: A clunk is a clue, not a parts order. I start by checking what the driveshaft is actually doing before condemning an expensive length of metal. Ford’s diagnosis separates joint wear, support trouble, imbalance and incorrect angles because several different problems can deliver the same damn soundtrack. [Driveshaft diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
guides.why: The driveshaft runs lengthwise between the transmission and rear differential; it is separate from the two rear halfshafts leading toward the wheels. Its joints accommodate changes in alignment along that path. This inspection looks for physical trouble and connects it to the conditions that produce the noise or vibration. A clean-looking shaft alone does not rule out imbalance, excessive runout—wobble as it turns—or an angle problem. [Shaft layout and inspection](#/document/G2214730) [Diagnostic branches](#/document/G2214728)

when.summary: Inspect at each oil-change service. Predominantly towing or car-top-carrier use calls for more frequent inspection and service as needed.
notes: Lubricate only if the fitted joint has the specified grease fitting.

prepare.title: Record the symptom
prepare.detail: Note road speed, acceleration, steady cruise or coast, whether the noise occurs when selecting a gear, and any recent repairs. Keep the original tire pressures and vehicle load unchanged before the baseline vibration road test. [Initial vibration check](#/document/G2214730) [Repair history](#/document/G1693185)

prepare.title: Arrange proper underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a suitably rated twin-post hoist, with an operator who can position and secure the car correctly for inspection and manual shaft rotation. Ford also permits a frame hoist with jackstands and requires the driveshaft angle to remain close to its normal, vehicle-at-rest position. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job. [Inspection support](#/document/G2214730) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Confirm the applicable hoist setup
prepare.detail: Ford specifies NEUTRAL for hoist positioning in each applicable engine’s underbody service procedure: [2.3L setup](#/document/G1688079), [3.7L setup](#/document/G1688092), [5.0L setup](#/document/G1688106). Have the lift operator establish a secure setup that permits hand rotation before anyone works underneath. These setup references do not make exhaust removal part of this inspection.

prepare.title: Gather inspection equipment
prepare.detail: Have a light and a way to record findings; those are practical inspection aids. Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. No joint press, replacement bolts or dial indicator is needed for the installed visual and hand-rotation checks described here. [Protective equipment](#/document/G1693189) [Inspection method](#/document/G2214730)

steps.title: Describe the concern before changing anything
steps.body: Write down exactly when the clunk, shudder or vibration occurs. Include whether it began after other work. Ford calls for verifying the concern and checking obvious causes before pursuing deeper diagnosis; previous repairs can contribute to a new problem. An intermittent noise that is absent during testing is not sufficient grounds to order parts. [Inspection and verification](#/document/G2214728) [Diagnostic approach](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Establish a baseline when investigating vibration
steps.body: First look for obvious damage. If no finding requires correction before driving, reproduce the reported vibration during a road test and record the road speed and driving condition. Do this before making adjustments or changing tire pressure or vehicle load. Note whether the vibration follows road speed or changes with acceleration and deceleration; that distinction helps select the next test. Skip this road test when you are simply performing an inspection without a reported symptom. [Baseline vibration inspection](#/document/G2214730) [Correct obvious causes first](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working underneath. An unexpected start can seriously injure someone working around the driveline. Keep the engine off throughout the underbody inspection and hand-rotation checks. [Unexpected-start precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Lift the car and establish safe working access
steps.body:
Have the hoist operator use the lifting locations identified by the stamped triangles and position the adapters clear of suspension, exhaust, brackets and the rear axle cover. Confirm the hoist has adequate capacity for the car and its contents. Keep the driveshaft close to its normal vehicle-at-rest angle for inspection. Never get underneath a car supported only by a jack. [Lifting locations and clearance](#/document/G1663631) [Capacity and support safety](#/document/G1693189) [Inspection position](#/document/G2214730)

Use the NEUTRAL hoist setup applicable to the engine: [2.3L](#/document/G1688079), [3.7L](#/document/G1688092), [5.0L](#/document/G1688106). If the shaft cannot be turned by hand with the car securely supported, stop the rotation check and have the operator resolve the setup. Do not force the shaft or change the vehicle’s restraint arrangement while underneath.

steps.title: Follow the shaft from front to rear
steps.body: Locate the lengthwise shaft between the transmission and rear differential. Identify its end connections, the joints present, and the center bearing support if fitted. A U-joint has a cross carried in bearing cups between two fork-shaped yokes; other connections may use a constant-velocity joint or flexible coupling. Inspect the arrangement actually fitted rather than assuming every car has the same connections. Leave the shaft and its fasteners installed for these checks. [Shaft layout](#/document/G2214730) [Connection variants](#/document/G2214904) [U-joint construction](#/document/G2214732)

steps.title: Inspect the shaft tube and joint seating
steps.body: Use the light to examine the accessible shaft surfaces for damage, missing balance weights and undercoating on the shaft. Look at the U-joint bearing cups for visibly incorrect seating. Record the location of anything suspicious so it can be checked during rotation. Ford treats these findings as relevant to vibration; a damaged shaft calls for replacement rather than a balancing experiment. [Visual shaft inspection](#/document/G2214730) [Balance-related symptoms](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Check the mounting connections and center support
steps.body:
Look at the rear connection where the shaft meets the differential’s pinion flange—the bolted mating face at the differential input. Check for visibly loose or missing fasteners and an obviously disturbed connection. Inspect the front connection as well for obvious damage or incorrect attachment. Ford identifies loose rear pinion-flange bolts as a possible cause of cruising vibration. Do not loosen fasteners merely to inspect them. [Connection inspection](#/document/G1693185) [Cruising-vibration diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)

If a center bearing is fitted, examine its insulating support for wear or damage. Record a damaged support separately from a damaged shaft tube; they lead to different observations even when both produce vibration. [Center support check](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Inspect the flexible coupling if fitted
steps.body: Examine the visible flexible coupling for cracks. Ford’s replacement decision is direct: a cracked coupling needs replacement. Record the finding and arrange that repair; this inspection does not require disconnecting the coupling to inspect its exposed surfaces. [Flexible coupling inspection](#/document/G2214904)

steps.title: Rotate slowly and feel for joint trouble
steps.body:
With the engine off and the car securely configured for hand rotation, turn the driveshaft slowly by hand. Examine the surfaces that were previously hidden. Feel for binding and end play at the U-joint trunnions—the short bearing journals on the joint’s cross. End play means movement along those journals; binding means the joint resists movement instead of moving smoothly. Note where either occurs. Ford supplies an observational check here, not a numerical play allowance. [Hand-rotation inspection](#/document/G2214730)

Also check for rough operation at the center bearing, if fitted, and inspect the CV joints and U-joints for wear or damage. A smooth hand check does not, by itself, clear every possible cause of vibration. [Bearing and joint checks](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Choose the next action from the findings
steps.body:
Match the observations to the diagnostic decisions below. Correct a confirmed visible cause before moving into more testing. If the installed inspection does not explain a persistent vibration, the next branch may be measured runout, balance or driveline angles—not automatically a replacement shaft. Runout is the amount the shaft wanders as it rotates; angle diagnosis checks the relationship between the transmission, shaft and axle. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G2214728) [Runout escalation](#/document/G2214730) [Angle diagnosis](#/document/G2214729)

A grease fitting creates a separate lubrication requirement. Ford’s owner instructions call for lubrication where fittings exist; do not assume a joint without a fitting needs a homemade lubrication point. Record any fitted lubrication points for service using the correct lubricant and method. This article covers inspection, not an unspecified grease procedure. [Ford owner maintenance instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Close the inspection and verify the outcome
steps.body:
Record which connections, shaft sections, joints and supports you checked, including any area you could not examine. This inspection leaves the assembly installed, so there is no removal sequence to reverse. Collect the light and other inspection items, clear everyone from underneath, and have the lift operator return the car to the ground.

After any corrective work, recheck the original concern at the road-test speed and driving condition that produced it. If the symptom remains, continue diagnosis. [Post-correction verification](#/document/G2214730) [Symptom verification](#/document/G2214728)

watchFor.title: A vibration that began after other work
watchFor.body: Include that work in the investigation. Incorrectly completed repairs can contribute to the current concern; timing is useful evidence, although it does not establish the cause by itself. [Repair history checks](#/document/G1693185)

watchFor.title: Disassembly creeping into an inspection
watchFor.body: Shaft removal, slip-yoke spline inspection and U-joint replacement are separate repair work. Ford requires replacement of removed driveshaft attachment bolts and, during U-joint repair, discarded snap rings. Do not undo them as an exploratory play check. [Shaft removal requirements](#/document/G2214904) [Joint repair requirements](#/document/G2214732)

watchFor.title: A vise offered as a convenient shaft holder
watchFor.body: Never grip the driveshaft assembly in vise jaws or a similar fixture. Local dents or fractures can lead to shaft failure while driving. [Driveshaft handling warning](#/document/G2214732)

watchFor.title: A persistent symptom with no visible damage
watchFor.body: That result calls for a more specific test. It does not prove the assembly is healthy, and it does not prove the shaft needs replacement. [Vibration diagnostic branches](#/document/G2214728)

procedures.purpose: Match the observed noise or vibration to the appropriate diagnostic branch.
Support the installed inspection and provide subsequent runout and balancing procedures when indicated.
Provide the separate angle-measurement procedure when symptoms and joint checks point there.
Provide connection details, coupling inspection and separate shaft removal and installation requirements.
Provide handling precautions and the separate U-joint repair procedure.

stepGroups.summary: Select further diagnosis where needed and verify completion.

diagnostics.finding: A loud clunk when shifting from REVERSE to DRIVE, or a clunk as the car starts moving after a stop.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies worn or damaged CV joints or U-joints; excessive joint play is specifically associated with the moving-off clunk. [Clunk diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Use the joint inspection findings to confirm wear or damage. Arrange the indicated repair or shaft replacement when necessary; the noise alone is not confirmation. [Joint inspection and repair decision](#/document/G2214728)

diagnostics.finding: Binding or end play during slow hand rotation.
diagnostics.meaning: These are abnormal joint observations called out in Ford’s inspection. [Joint movement check](#/document/G2214730)
diagnostics.next: Record the affected joint and arrange component-specific repair assessment. Do not invent a numerical clearance or try to free the joint by force. [Inspection and corrective actions](#/document/G2214730)

diagnostics.finding: Damaged center-bearing insulation or rough bearing operation.
diagnostics.meaning: A worn or damaged center support is a listed cause of cruising vibration. [Center-bearing diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Arrange the repair assessment Ford calls for, including shaft replacement where necessary. [Center support action](#/document/G2214728)

diagnostics.finding: Visibly loose rear flange bolts.
diagnostics.meaning: Loose pinion-flange attachment bolts can cause cruising vibration. [Flange diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Have the attachment corrected to specification before further vibration diagnosis. If bolts are removed, Ford requires new bolts and its seating and tightening procedure. [Attachment repair requirements](#/document/G2214904)

diagnostics.finding: Cracks in a fitted flexible coupling.
diagnostics.meaning: The coupling fails Ford’s inspection criterion. [Coupling inspection](#/document/G2214904)
diagnostics.next: Arrange coupling replacement. [Replacement decision](#/document/G2214904)

diagnostics.finding: Coasting rumble or boom, or shaft damage, missing weights or undercoating.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford associates the noise with possible imbalance and directs inspection for these physical conditions. [Rumble and balance diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Address confirmed damage first. For unresolved vibration, proceed through measured runout and the applicable balancing diagnosis rather than attaching guessed weights. [Runout and balancing sequence](#/document/G2214730)

diagnostics.finding: A similar buzz during cruise and coast, or shudder during acceleration from a stop or low speed.
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect driveline angles are possible. Acceleration shudder can also involve binding or damaged joints. [Buzz and shudder diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Check joint condition first, then arrange angle measurement when indicated. Angle testing requires its own level-surface, unloaded ride-height and tire-pressure setup. [Angle measurement prerequisites](#/document/G2214729)

diagnostics.finding: Cruising vibration remains after the installed inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include shaft or pinion-flange runout, imbalance, incorrect angles and joint or support problems. [Cruising-vibration diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Select the appropriate measurement branch. Shaft runout uses a dial indicator at the front, center and rear of each shaft section; a numerical verdict requires the applicable specifications. [Runout measurement](#/document/G2214730)

verification.title: Document the physical checks
verification.body: Record shaft condition, balance-weight observations, joint seating, joint movement, visible attachments, coupling cracks and center-support condition. Distinguish a completed check from an inaccessible or incomplete one. [Inspection items](#/document/G2214730) [Support checks](#/document/G2214728) [Coupling criterion](#/document/G2214904)

verification.title: Confirm the original symptom after correction
verification.body: Repeat the relevant road-test condition after repairs. A continuing vibration requires further diagnosis even when the visual inspection is satisfactory. [Repair verification](#/document/G2214730)

verification.title: Give the result an honest conclusion
verification.body: For an inspection without a reported symptom, record the observed condition. For a noise or vibration complaint, record whether it was reproduced, whether a cause was confirmed, and what remains to be tested. [Verification sequence](#/document/G2214728)

notes: These inspection steps cover the original 2015 Mustang 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L scope; they do not extend applicability to other years.
Joint grease and differential lubricant serve different locations. A boot finding is not a differential-fluid filling instruction.
guides.title: Halfshaft boots: catch damage before the joint pays for it
guides.summary: Inspect the inner and outer rear halfshaft boots on both sides of your 2015 Mustang, covering the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. Look for damaged covers, displaced attachments and escaping grease, then separate boot concerns from differential-seal leaks.
guides.introduction: I start with the humble flexible covers around the rear halfshaft joints. They’re easy to overlook beside all that suspension hardware, but Ford specifically includes the constant-velocity (CV) joint boots in its visual inspection. A little careful looking beats the hell out of guessing which expensive part deserves replacing. [Halfshaft inspection](#/document/G2214769)
guides.why: The useful result is a clear finding: which boot is damaged, where a leak begins, or which surfaces still need a better view. Ford checks boots, joints, shafts and loose hardware together, then uses the actual symptom to guide further diagnosis. A boot inspection helps narrow the problem; it does not certify the joint’s internal condition. [Inspection and diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

when.summary: Inspect the halfshaft boots at every oil-change service; investigate visible grease loss sooner.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail:
Arrange secure underside access with a hoist rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the triangles stamped into the body structure and position the lift adapters at the corresponding lifting points. Keep the arms clear of suspension parts, stabilizer brackets, steering and exhaust components; incorrect placement can damage parts or let the car shift or fall. [Marked lifting points and restrictions](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

If using a jack for access, work on a hard, level surface, use adequate lifting capacity, set the parking brake and block the wheels remaining on the ground. Support the car on proper stands before going underneath. Never rely on a jack alone, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this inspection. [Jack and stand safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the car. An unexpected start can seriously injure someone inspecting it. [Start prevention](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Bring viewing aids and protection
prepare.detail: A flashlight and inspection mirror are useful viewing aids; a phone can help record locations and findings. Wear eye and ear protection for service work, and protective gloves where you could contact sharp edges. No replacement parts or disassembly tools are needed for the visual inspection described here. [Personal protection](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Keep the job to inspection
prepare.detail: You are examining the installed halfshafts. The knuckle removal, pry bar and seal tools shown in the repair material belong to component replacement; they are not instructions for gaining inspection access. Keep the boots away from sharp edges and hot exhaust parts, which can damage them. [Halfshaft arrangement and handling](#/document/G2214772)

steps.title: Confirm the car is ready to inspect
steps.body: Before reaching underneath, confirm that secure support is already established, the ignition is off, the key is removed and remote start is disabled if equipped. Keep clear of hot exhaust components. If safe access is unavailable, have the inspection performed where the car can be properly supported. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Find both ends of each rear halfshaft
steps.body: Locate the differential between the rear wheels, then follow each halfshaft outward toward its wheel. Identify the flexible boot at the inner joint near the differential and the boot at the outer joint near the wheel. Make a four-location checklist: left inner, left outer, right inner and right outer. The installed arrangement is shown in Ford’s halfshaft illustrations. [Rear halfshaft layout](#/document/G2214772)

steps.title: Inspect the first boot’s folds and attachments
steps.body:
Use your light to examine the visible folds, the spaces between them and both ends where the boot attaches. Look for splits, holes, visibly damaged material, an end that has moved out of place or an attachment that appears displaced. Ford’s visual check includes the boots and surrounding hardware. Use the mirror to improve your view without levering against the shaft or pushing tools into the boot. [Visual inspection](#/document/G2214769)

Work around the visible circumference from different viewing angles. Do not call the boot sound if you have only seen its easiest face; record any area you cannot inspect.

steps.title: Look beyond the boot for escaping grease
steps.body: Examine the boot ends, joint housing and nearby surfaces for greasy deposits or a thrown pattern. Treat these as clues and trace them toward their apparent origin before wiping anything away. Record whether the material leads to a visible opening in the boot, an attachment area or somewhere else. This is a practical way to document Ford’s visual check for boot and joint damage; deposits alone do not establish which component has failed. [Boot and joint inspection](#/document/G2214769)

steps.title: Repeat at the other three locations
steps.body:
Give the other boot on that halfshaft and both boots on the opposite side the same examination. Check the folds, attachment areas and surrounding deposits at each location. Also note obvious shaft damage or visibly loose hardware without disturbing fasteners. Ford includes all of these in the initial inspection. [Inspection checklist](#/document/G2214769)

If a surface remains hidden, record the specific location and arrange a better supported viewing position. Do not remove suspension components for this visual inspection. [Halfshaft repair scope](#/document/G2214772)

steps.title: Separate the differential seal from the joint boot
steps.body:
At each inner joint, distinguish the flexible boot from the separate seal where the halfshaft enters the differential housing. Ford’s seal illustration identifies that housing opening. If wetness appears to begin there rather than at the boot, record a suspected halfshaft-seal leak. If the origin is obscured or uncertain, record that uncertainty instead of naming a failed part from appearance alone. [Halfshaft seal location](#/document/G2214752)

A housing-seal concern needs a different repair assessment from a damaged boot. Neither observation is an instruction to put lubricant into the boot.

steps.title: Choose the next action from the finding
steps.body:
For a damaged boot, displaced attachment or apparent grease escape, arrange assessment of the boot and CV joint rather than assuming a new cover alone settles the matter. Ford’s diagnostic path calls for inspecting joint wear or damage and replacing the rear halfshaft when necessary. [Joint assessment](#/document/G2214769)

Include any existing clunk, acceleration shudder or cruising-speed vibration in the report. Ford assigns different possible causes to those symptoms. Report them without assuming the boot finding explains them, and use the diagnostic decisions below to describe the concern accurately. [Symptom chart](#/document/G2214769)

steps.title: Finish with a complete inspection record
steps.body:
Record each of the four boot locations as either no visible defect found, a specific defect found or incompletely viewed. For a concern, note the exact location, apparent leak origin and any reported driving symptom; photographs are useful for comparison. Remove your viewing aids and confirm that nothing was disturbed or left beneath the vehicle before the lift operator returns the car to the ground.

This inspection removes no components, so there are no boot clamps, suspension fasteners or halfshaft retainers to reinstall. Any repair is a separate job. [Inspection scope](#/document/G2214769)

watchFor.title: Inspection tools becoming damage tools
watchFor.body: Keep sharp tools away from the flexible covers and avoid contact with hot exhaust parts. Ford warns that either can damage the boots. [Boot protection](#/document/G2214772)

watchFor.title: A clean-looking boot beside a driving complaint
watchFor.body: No visible defect does not resolve a clunk, shudder or vibration. Ford directs diagnosis by symptom when the cause is not visually evident. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G2214769)

watchFor.title: Inspection turning into lubrication
watchFor.body: Ford lists halfshaft-boot inspection separately from lubrication of components equipped with grease fittings. Do not interpret that schedule as an instruction to open or fill a boot. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

procedures.purpose: Identify the installed rear halfshaft arrangement and understand the separate component-replacement procedure.
Assess visible halfshaft concerns and route reported clunks, shudder or vibration.
Identify the differential-side halfshaft seal and route a confirmed seal leak to the appropriate repair.
Locate the marked lifting points and establish safe support for underside inspection.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and locate
stepGroups.summary: Establish safe access and identify the four boot locations.

stepGroups.title: Inspect both sides
stepGroups.summary: Examine the boots and trace suspicious deposits.

stepGroups.title: Decide and finish
stepGroups.summary: Choose the appropriate assessment and record what was actually checked.

diagnostics.finding: Split boot, displaced attachment or grease apparently escaping from a boot
diagnostics.meaning: There is a visible boot-area concern; the inspection does not establish the joint’s internal condition.
diagnostics.next: Arrange boot and joint assessment. Ford calls for joint inspection and rear halfshaft replacement when necessary, rather than automatic replacement based on a symptom alone. [Boot and joint diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: Wetness appears to begin where the halfshaft enters the differential
diagnostics.meaning: The separate halfshaft seal may be the source.
diagnostics.next: Have the leak origin confirmed and use the seal repair path if appropriate. [Rear halfshaft seal](#/document/G2214752)

diagnostics.finding: Loud clunk when shifting from reverse to drive
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies worn or damaged CV joints as a possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Have the CV joints inspected for wear or damage; replacement of the rear halfshaft depends on that assessment. [Clunk diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: Clunk as the vehicle starts moving forward after a stop
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies a loose hub nut as a possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Have the hub-nut torque checked against the correct specification. Ford requires a new hub nut if the torque is outside specification; this guide does not provide that repair specification. [Start-off clunk diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: Grunting with acceleration shudder from a stop, or vibration at cruising speed
diagnostics.meaning: Ford associates these symptoms with possible CV-joint binding; cruising vibration can also involve joint damage.
diagnostics.next: Have the outer CV joint’s seating in the hub checked and the concern diagnosed before selecting a repair. [Shudder and vibration diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: No visible damage or leakage
diagnostics.meaning: The inspected surfaces show no obvious defect; hidden surfaces and internal joint condition remain unverified.
diagnostics.next: Record the result. If a driving concern remains, continue symptom-based diagnosis. [Inspection and verification](#/document/G2214769)

verification.title: All four locations accounted for
verification.body: The record includes the left and right inner and outer boots, with any obscured areas explicitly identified. [Halfshaft arrangement](#/document/G2214772)

verification.title: Findings identify a location and next action
verification.body: Every concern distinguishes a boot-area finding, suspected differential-seal leak or unresolved source. Reported symptoms accompany the finding rather than being treated as proof of one failed part. [Diagnostic approach](#/document/G2214769) [Seal location](#/document/G2214752)

verification.title: The inspection ends without creating a repair
verification.body: Viewing aids are removed, nothing has been left underneath and no boot attachments or driveline fasteners have been disturbed. A visual pass is recorded as no visible defect, not a guarantee that the joint is healthy.

notes: Applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.

This installed visual check contributes useful observations to maintenance; it does not represent completion of every steering, ball-joint, suspension and wheel inspection in Ford's broader scheduled service.
Tie-rod replacement, quantitative joint assessment, alignment measurement and suspension repair are follow-on jobs with their own procedures.
guides.title: Steering linkage: installed visual check and symptom routing
guides.summary: For 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine: inspect visible tie rods, boots, clamps and connections, record obscured areas, and decide which concerns need mechanical or electric-assist diagnosis.
guides.introduction: I start with the parts that physically connect the steering gear to the front wheels: an inner and outer tie rod on each side, with ribbed bellows protecting the inner joints. Electric assistance helps move the rack, but the mechanical connections still matter. [Steering layout](#/document/G1686674) This guide teaches an installed visual inspection and symptom routing; it does not certify joint play, alignment or overall steering safety. There is no power-steering-fluid reservoir to check or fill—one less damn bottle on the shopping list. [Ford electric steering care](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1448667&Uid=G1642990&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.why: A useful check produces a location and an observation: a split left bellows, a disturbed outer connection, or a steering warning accompanied by heavier effort. Those findings lead to different next steps. Ford's diagnostic information also lists tires, loading, suspension joints, wheel bearings and alignment among possible contributors to steering complaints, so guessing a steering gear from one symptom can become an expensive pain in the ass. [Mechanical symptom routing](#/document/G1686610) [Electric-assist operation](#/document/G1686674)

when.summary: Inspect steering linkage, ball joints and tie-rod ends at each oil-change service.
notes: The electric-assist system has no power-steering-fluid reservoir, top-up or flush interval.

prepare.title: Bring viewing and recording aids
prepare.detail: Use a flashlight and notes or photographs to record left and right separately. A viewing mirror can help with an awkward sightline. No joint separator, pry bar, replacement clamp or lubricant is needed for this visual check.

prepare.title: Arrange supported viewing access
prepare.detail: Use a properly operated vehicle hoist for the underside portion. Its capacity must cover the car, cargo and modifications. Follow the hoist manufacturer's operating and restraint instructions, using Ford's illustrated lifting locations at the four marked side areas. Locate the stamped triangles on the vehicle before positioning the lifting contacts. Incorrect contact placement can let the car shift or fall. [Mustang lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Keep the inspection installed
prepare.detail: Inspect from beneath the front of the car and through available front-wheel-area sightlines, leaving the wheels, shields, braces, boots and connections installed. Record anything they obscure for follow-up. The removal operations in the tie-rod repair procedures are not automatic visual-inspection prerequisites. [Outer connection layout](#/document/G1686682) [Bellows and access layout](#/document/G1686681)

prepare.title: Prevent starting and protect yourself
prepare.detail: Before working around or underneath the car, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup, switch the ignition off and remove the key. An unexpected start can seriously injure someone working near the vehicle. Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Record the complaint before touching anything
steps.body:
Write down any warning message and describe the change: looseness, stiffness, wandering, pulling, knocking or unusually heavy steering. Include whether it happens over bumps, during turns or under other particular conditions, and note recent repairs or modifications. Do not deliberately road-test a potentially compromised connection. Ford uses the symptom and preliminary observations to direct diagnosis. [Preliminary checks](#/document/G1693185) [Steering-related symptoms](#/document/G1686610)

If selectable steering is fitted, record its setting. Sport deliberately requires more steering effort than Standard; Comfort requires less. A brief feedback bump can occur when selecting a mode. These characteristics can explain a feel change, but they do not dismiss a warning or mechanical concern. [Selectable steering](#/document/G1686674)

steps.title: Check the surrounding clues
steps.body:
While the car is on the ground, note uneven loading, visible tire damage or abnormal wear, and aftermarket steering, suspension, wheel or tire equipment. If checking tire pressures, use a pressure gauge with the tires cold and normal loads aboard, and use the vehicle certification label's specification. Ford warns that its manual specifications do not apply to vehicles with aftermarket equipment. Record modifications for whoever performs further assessment. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686610)

Use the [tire guide](#/maintenance/tires) for tire care and the [suspension guide](#/maintenance/suspension) for the wider chassis check.

steps.title: Shut down and establish safe access
steps.body:
Disable remote start, turn the ignition off, remove the key and apply the parking brake before working around the car. Keep the engine off throughout this check. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

Locate the four lifting areas shown in Ford's illustration: the marked side locations behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Identify their stamped triangles on the actual vehicle. Have the hoist contacts positioned at those locations, with clearance from steering linkage, suspension, exhaust and mounting brackets, then raise and secure the car according to the hoist manufacturer's instructions. Do not use the bumpers as lifting points. [Lifting locations and clearance](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist capacity](#/document/G1693189)

The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job. Never go underneath a car supported only by a jack. If proper supported viewing access is unavailable, arrange the underside check at a suitably equipped shop. [Jack restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Find the linkage on both sides
steps.body:
From beneath the front of the supported car and through available wheel-area openings, locate each outer tie-rod end where it attaches to the wheel spindle, also called the knuckle. Follow its threaded connection inward toward the ribbed bellows at the steering gear. Repeat on the other side. [Outer connection](#/document/G1686682) [Inner tie rod and bellows](#/document/G1686681)

There is one inner rod, outer rod and bellows on each side. The inner joint is beneath the bellows; leave that protection in place. Use the light and viewing aids to inspect the available surfaces, and mark blocked areas as obscured. An intact-looking boot cannot establish the condition of the joint inside. [Component arrangement](#/document/G1686674)

steps.title: Inspect the visible rods and outer connections
steps.body:
On each side, examine the visible rod, threaded connection, jam nut, outer joint boot and attachment at the spindle. Look for obvious bending or other damage, split or displaced joint protection, and an attachment that appears loose, missing or disturbed. Record the side and exact location. Leave fasteners undisturbed; this is not a torque or movement test. Ford's repair illustration identifies these connections and its procedure specifically cautions against damaging the outer boot. [Outer tie-rod end](#/document/G1686682)

As a precaution, if an attachment appears loose or missing, stop the check and have the connection assessed before driving. Do not tighten it by feel or road-test the concern. Ford's diagnostic path calls for checking connections and correcting identified mechanical faults using the applicable specifications. [Connection checks](#/document/G1693185) [Mechanical findings](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Inspect each bellows and both clamped ends
steps.body:
Check the visible folds and edges of each ribbed bellows for tears, damage or displacement. Look at the large end on the gear housing and the small end on the tie rod, including their clamps. Each bellows uses two clamps. Do not loosen either clamp, pull the boot aside or insert a tool beneath its edge. [Boot arrangement](#/document/G1686674) [Bellows installation and sealing](#/document/G1686681)

The bellows must seal airtight. An opening can allow steering movement to draw water and dirt into the gear; water also degrades the inner-joint grease and can lead to joint failure. A torn boot, displaced edge or missing clamp needs assessment of the seal and protected components. Do not patch the connection with zip ties: Ford explicitly excludes them because they cannot provide the required seal. [Contamination precautions](#/document/G1686681)

steps.title: Look over the visible gear and nearby attachments
steps.body:
Inspect exposed steering components and visible attachments for obvious damage, an incorrect connection or missing hardware. Where heavy road deposits hide a surface, have the buildup removed before treating that area as inspected; leave the bellows and clamps intact. Record anything still concealed by shields or braces. Ford's preliminary inspection includes steering components, suspension fasteners and removal of excessive underbody deposits. [Underbody inspection](#/document/G1686610) [Correct connections](#/document/G1693185)

Do not use this view to clear suspension ball joints or wheel bearings. If the complaint involves wandering, binding, knocking or vibration, include those symptoms in the follow-up request because Ford's charts identify several possible systems. [Symptom chart](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Keep lubrication targeted
steps.body:
Ford's maintenance instruction calls for lubrication where grease fittings are fitted. Do not interpret that as permission to coat boots or rubber bushings, or to open a bellows to add grease. If an actual fitting is present, identify the component and obtain its lubricant and servicing instructions before lubricating it. [Ford lubrication instruction](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

The grease application in the inner-tie-rod procedure belongs to boot installation at specified mating surfaces. It is not a routine external treatment for the installed linkage. [Repair lubrication locations](#/document/G1686681)

steps.title: Choose the next diagnostic path
steps.body:
For visible mechanical damage, suspect hardware or persistent looseness and noise, arrange assessment of the identified connection and related suspension or wheel components. An outside view does not locate internal wear. For pulling, tire condition, loading, brakes and alignment may also need investigation; use the [alignment guide](#/maintenance/wheel-alignment) to plan that separate work. [Mechanical diagnostic routing](#/document/G1686610)

For a warning or marked increase in steering effort, arrange electric power-assisted steering diagnosis. The power steering control module can store diagnostic trouble codes. Voltage or temperature concerns can reduce assistance; a critical concern can remove electrical assistance entirely, leaving heavy mechanical steering. Those symptoms do not identify a failed part by themselves. Provide the VIN, exact warning, conditions and visual findings for Ford's guided EPAS routine. The routine requires the VIN and must be followed through its own instructions. [Assist failure modes](#/document/G1686674) [Guided EPAS diagnosis](#/document/G1757488)

steps.title: Finish the check and lower the car
steps.body:
Confirm that no boot, clamp, fastener or connection was disturbed, and remove the light, viewing aids and other loose items from underneath. Keep everyone clear while the hoist operator lowers the vehicle according to the equipment instructions. Keep the parking brake applied during completion. [Protective seals](#/document/G1686681) [Service and lifting precautions](#/document/G1693189)

Finish the record for both sides: no visible concern, a specific concern, or an obscured area requiring follow-up. Assign a next action to every concern. A suspect attachment must be assessed before driving; an unresolved warning, steering symptom or concealed area remains open for the appropriate assessment. [Mechanical next actions](#/document/G1686610) [EPAS diagnosis](#/document/G1757488)

watchFor.title: A loose-looking or missing attachment
watchFor.body: Treat this as a potentially compromised connection. Stop, leave the fastener alone and arrange assessment before driving. Its appearance is a reason to investigate, not a specification for tightening it. [Connection checks](#/document/G1693185) [Mechanical diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

watchFor.title: An opened bellows becoming a bigger problem
watchFor.body: Leave the seal closed during inspection. Inner-tie-rod service requires new bellows and clamps, and an airtight installation; contamination can damage the joint and gear. A replacement tutorial is a separate job. [Bellows requirements](#/document/G1686681)

watchFor.title: Inspection turning into linkage service
watchFor.body: Before any follow-on steering-linkage service, disconnect the battery ground cable through the proper procedure. Ford warns that servicing the linkage with it connected can damage the steering gear badly enough to require replacement. [Linkage service precaution](#/document/G1686682) [Battery procedure](#/document/G1692356)

watchFor.title: Ordering an entire steering gear from one symptom
watchFor.body: Inner rods, outer ends and bellows are separately serviceable. The assist motor, control module and torque sensor are serviced with the gear assembly. Identify the fault before choosing the repair. [Serviceable components](#/document/G1686674)

procedures.purpose: Locate the marked vehicle lifting points and apply lifting restrictions.
Identify the outer connection and route a confirmed outer tie-rod repair.
Explain bellows protection and route inner-tie-rod or bellows service.
Route mechanical steering symptoms among related chassis systems.
Enter the VIN-dependent guided EPAS diagnostic path.
Provide battery isolation instructions if follow-on linkage service is undertaken.

stepGroups.title: Record the concern and establish access
stepGroups.summary: Capture useful clues, prevent unexpected starting and use the marked lifting locations.

stepGroups.title: Inspect the installed linkage
stepGroups.summary: Check both visible connections, bellows and attachments without opening or adjusting them.

stepGroups.title: Route findings and finish safely
stepGroups.summary: Choose mechanical or electric-assist follow-up and close the visual checklist.

diagnostics.finding: A steering attachment appears loose, missing or disturbed
diagnostics.meaning: The mechanical connection may be compromised; appearance alone cannot establish the required correction.
diagnostics.next: Stop the inspection and arrange assessment before driving. Do not tighten by feel or perform a proving road test. [Mechanical connection checks](#/document/G1693185) [Repair routing](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: A bellows is torn, displaced or missing a clamp
diagnostics.meaning: The airtight protective seal may have failed, exposing the gear and inner joint to contamination.
diagnostics.next: Have the protection and protected components assessed. Use the proper repair path, with no zip-tie substitute. [Bellows sealing](#/document/G1686681)

diagnostics.finding: Visible parts look intact, but looseness, knocking or binding remains
diagnostics.meaning: The visual inspection has not identified the cause. Steering, suspension joints, strut bearings or wheel components may require further assessment.
diagnostics.next: Provide the symptom record for a mechanical diagnosis; do not mark the joints as passing a movement test or select replacement parts from the symptom alone. [Mechanical symptom chart](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: The car pulls or wanders
diagnostics.meaning: Loading, tires, alignment, brakes and steering can contribute; a pull does not isolate a tie rod.
diagnostics.next: Record loading and tire observations, then arrange the appropriate tire, suspension and alignment investigation before steering-system diagnosis as needed. [Pull and wander diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Steering becomes markedly heavier or a warning appears
diagnostics.meaning: Electrical assistance may be reduced or absent. The cause still requires diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Avoid a deliberate symptom-reproduction drive and arrange VIN-based EPAS assessment, supplying the warning and operating conditions. [Failure modes](#/document/G1686674) [Guided routine](#/document/G1757488)

diagnostics.finding: Effort changed with a steering-mode selection
diagnostics.meaning: The available modes deliberately alter effort, and selection can produce a brief feedback bump.
diagnostics.next: Record the selected mode. Route any remaining warning or mechanical symptom separately. [Selectable steering](#/document/G1686674)

diagnostics.finding: A shield, wheel or brace blocks the view
diagnostics.meaning: That section has not been visually inspected.
diagnostics.next: Record the location and arrange further access during an appropriate inspection or repair. Do not adopt component-removal disassembly simply to complete this installed checklist. [Installed component and shield layout](#/document/G1686681)

verification.title: Both sides have an explicit result
verification.body: Account for the visible outer rod and connection, outer joint protection, bellows and both clamped ends on each side. Label obscured areas separately. [Component arrangement](#/document/G1686674) [Outer connection](#/document/G1686682)

verification.title: Protection and connections remain intact
verification.body: Confirm that the check has not displaced a boot or clamp, opened a seal or altered a connection. No reassembly is required for this installed visual workflow. [Bellows protection](#/document/G1686681) [Outer boot precaution](#/document/G1686682)

verification.title: Every concern has a next action
verification.body: Record mechanical follow-up, VIN-based EPAS diagnosis or further viewing access as appropriate. Do not drive with a suspect attachment pending assessment. A completed visual checklist does not clear an unresolved symptom or certify joint play. [Mechanical assessment](#/document/G1686610) [EPAS routine](#/document/G1757488)

verification.title: The vehicle is safely back on the ground
verification.body: Confirm that people and equipment are clear, the hoist lowering sequence is complete and the parking brake remains applied before closing the work. [Lifting and restraint precautions](#/document/G1693189)

notes: Applicability remains the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. GT350 and GT350R specifications and other model years are outside this article.
Ford’s front and rear suspension diagnosis pages both refer to the shared suspension-system diagnostic procedure. [Front diagnosis](#/document/G1692530) [Rear diagnosis](#/document/G1686646)

For follow-up, use the related [stabilizer-bushing guide](#/maintenance/stabilizer-bushings), [tire guide](#/maintenance/tires), [steering guide](#/maintenance/steering) or [wheel-alignment guide](#/maintenance/wheel-alignment) as appropriate. Component replacement remains a separate job.
guides.title: Suspension visual checks: wear, leaks and ride height
guides.summary: Inspect the front and rear suspension on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, connect visible findings to symptoms, and measure ride height when needed.
guides.introduction: I start a suspension check with notes before opening a parts catalog. Ford lists several possible causes for the same clunk, pull or rough ride; firing the damn parts cannon is an expensive way to narrow them down. This guide teaches a wheels-on visual inspection, symptom routing and optional ride-height checks. Joint-play tests, damper performance tests, alignment adjustments and repairs remain separate jobs. [Suspension diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)
guides.why: A useful inspection connects what the car does with something you can actually observe. Ford checks loading, tires, suspension, steering and hubs together because a noise or handling change does not identify one failed component. Looking across the system also helps avoid blaming a damper for a loose mounting or a spring for uneven loading. [Inspection and symptom chart](#/document/G1686610)

when.summary: Inspect at each oil-change service. Investigate a new knock, unstable feeling, ride-height change or visible damage sooner.

prepare.title: Inspection supplies
prepare.detail: Have a tire-pressure gauge and access to the vehicle certification label for the specified pressures and tire sizes. A light, inspection mirror and notebook or camera help make the visual inspection specific. Wear eye and ear protection during service, plus protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. [Tire checks](#/document/G1686610) [Service protection](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Raised access with the wheels fitted
prepare.detail: This sequence uses a suitably rated hoist for underbody access. Its capacity must cover the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Have its operating instructions available and understand its adapters, supports and lowering sequence. Ford identifies four lifting locations with stamped triangles, shown near the front and rear ends of the side sills. The vehicle-specific placement is taught in step 5; equipment operation follows the hoist manufacturer’s instructions. [Lifting locations](#/document/G1663631) [Capacity requirements](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Optional ride-height equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use a surface gauge, which records the height of a selected point above a reference surface. Measurements require a flat, level surface, correct tire pressures and a full fuel tank. Comparison with Ford’s limits also requires full service fluids, no passengers and no cargo. Keep the wheels supporting the vehicle during measurement; arrange a suitable wheel-supporting lift if the points cannot be reached safely at ground level. Before driving onto that lift, check for underbody interference and follow its manufacturer’s operating and restraint instructions. [Measuring equipment and setup](#/document/G1686616) [Curb-load definition](#/document/G1686608) [Drive-on lift clearance](#/document/G1663631)

prepare.title: Keep disassembly outside this inspection
prepare.detail: Leave wheels, arms, joints, springs and dampers installed. Ford’s preliminary inspection does not require routine wheel removal. Use the light and mirror for accessible views; record obscured areas for focused follow-up rather than importing the disassembly from a replacement procedure. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Describe the concern and record changes
steps.body: Record whether the car pulls, wanders, leans, bottoms out, rides harshly, sways, vibrates or makes noise. Note the speed, road surface, loading and whether it happens over bumps, during turns, under braking or during acceleration. Include previous repairs and aftermarket changes to steering, suspension, wheels or tires. Ford states that its manual specifications do not apply to vehicles with aftermarket equipment, so flag those changes before comparing measurements. [Symptom history and modifications](#/document/G1686610) [Previous repairs](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Check loading and tires
steps.body: Look for excessive or uneven loading. With normal loads aboard and the tires cold, measure pressure and compare it with the vehicle certification label. Verify tire sizes against the label, then inspect for damage and unusual tread wear. Record findings by corner. Correct pressure and loading problems before attributing the complaint to suspension parts; damaged or unsuitable tires need their own assessment and replacement as necessary. [Loading and tire checks](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Establish the road-test baseline
steps.body: If no observed condition makes driving questionable, check the concern on a smooth road. Describe the behavior without naming a failed part: for example, “pulls right on smooth pavement” or “rear rattle over uneven pavement.” Record vibration separately from noise, because Ford routes vibration through its noise, vibration and harshness diagnosis. Stop the test if damage, looseness or tire condition raises a safety concern. [Road test and diagnostic routing](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Prevent unexpected starting
steps.body: Before working around or beneath the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. These actions prevent a remote command or another person from starting the car while someone is inspecting it, which could cause serious or fatal injury. Set the parking brake and keep it applied throughout this visual inspection. No wheel-spinning test is part of this sequence. [Unexpected-start and movement precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Position and secure the hoist
steps.body:
Confirm the hoist’s capacity before lifting. Locate the stamped triangles at all four lifting locations: a front and rear location along each side of the body, as shown in Ford’s lifting diagram. Position the hoist arm adapters at those designated points. Incorrect placement can let the vehicle shift or fall. [Four lifting locations](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist capacity](#/document/G1693189)

Before raising, check that the arms and adapters clear suspension components, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets, steering linkage, exhaust, axle and rear cover. Do not lift against either bumper. Raise and secure the hoist using its manufacturer’s operating instructions and required supports before anyone goes beneath the vehicle. Leave the wheels fitted and the engine off. [Placement and clearance precautions](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Make the inspection surfaces visible
steps.body: Remove excessive mud, dirt and road deposits that hide the chassis and suspension. Work through one corner at a time, recording the component and observed condition. Include suspension fasteners, arms, bushings, springs, struts, shocks, steering components and hub areas. Mark anything you cannot see as unchecked. [Underbody inspection targets](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Inspect the front suspension
steps.body:
Use the light and mirror to examine visible control arms and ball-joint areas for damage, and bushings for damage or displacement. Inspect spring coils, seats, strut brackets and mountings for damage or parts out of position. Check accessible dust boots and jounce bumpers—the travel-limiting bumpers—for visible damage or displacement. Look for missing hardware and obvious looseness at accessible mountings, and include steering linkage, tie-rod ends and hub areas in the visual pass. [Front inspection targets](#/document/G1686610)

Record suspected joint or bearing wear for mechanical testing. Do not loosen fasteners or improvise a pry-bar test as part of this visual inspection. [Joint and bearing diagnostic routing](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Inspect the rear suspension
steps.body:
Identify the coil spring, shock absorber, stabilizer and links, wheel knuckle, hub assembly, lower-arm vertical link, toe link, lower arm and bushing assembly, and upper arm. Use those names in your notes so a finding can be traced to the correct component. [Rear component identification](#/document/G1697533)

Examine visible arms and joints for damage, bushings for damage or displacement, and springs and their mountings for damage or incorrect seating. Check shock mountings and bushings, stabilizer bushings and links. For rear noise, pay particular attention to the lower control arms, toe-link ball joints and cross-axis joints within the rear linkage. A visible defect warrants follow-up; acceptable internal joint movement requires a separate mechanical test. [Rear inspection and noise checks](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Record damper leaks and damage
steps.body:
Inspect each accessible front strut and rear shock absorber for damage and fluid traces. Check its visible mountings, bushings and protective boots. Record the corner and extent of any wet area before cleaning away the evidence. Ford includes suspension leaks and damage in its owner inspection and identifies dampers and their attachments as possible sources of ride and noise complaints. [Ford owner inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Damper diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

Have suspected leakage assessed. This visual check does not determine damping performance or apply a replacement threshold to an unspecified amount of wetness.

steps.title: Inspect stabilizer parts and keep them dry
steps.body:
Check the front and rear stabilizer bars, links, brackets and bushings for visible damage, displacement and suspected wear. Ford includes these parts among the possible sources of bump-related noises and excessive sway. [Stabilizer inspection](#/document/G1686610)

Do not apply lubricant to either stabilizer bar or its bushings: Ford warns that it can damage the bushings. The owner maintenance instruction to lubricate areas equipped with grease fittings does not authorize coating rubber mountings. [Front lubrication prohibition](#/document/G1692534) [Rear lubrication prohibition](#/document/G1686652) [Ford maintenance instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Return the vehicle to its wheels
steps.body:
Account for tools and inspection materials, then move everyone clear of the underside and lowering path. Confirm that the parking brake remains applied. Release the hoist’s supports and lower it according to the equipment manufacturer’s instructions, keeping arms and adapters correctly positioned until the tires carry the vehicle’s weight. Remove the adapters and move the arms clear only after the vehicle is fully supported on its wheels. [Vehicle support and movement precautions](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting-point requirements](#/document/G1663631)

The inspection leaves suspension parts and wheels connected, so no suspension reassembly or wheel-nut tightening is required. Record any area still obscured as requiring further inspection. [Inspection scope](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Set up the optional ride-height check
steps.body:
Use this check when investigating lean, low stance, front bottoming or a ride-height-related harsh-ride complaint. Place the vehicle on a flat, level surface with correctly inflated tires and a full fuel tank. For comparison with the specifications, have full service fluids, no passengers and no cargo. This is Ford’s curb-load condition; it differs from the normal-load tire-pressure check earlier. [When to measure](#/document/G1686610) [Measurement setup](#/document/G1686616) [Specification loading](#/document/G1686608)

Keep the tires carrying the vehicle’s weight. Use safe access to the measuring points, with the surface gauge referenced to the same flat, level supporting surface. If using a wheel-supporting lift, first check underbody clearance and use the manufacturer’s restraints and supports. Do not measure with the body raised on hoist arms and the suspension hanging. [Measurement method](#/document/G1686616) [Lift clearance](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Measure front ride height on both sides
steps.body:
With the surface gauge on the flat, level reference surface, measure vertically to the center of the rear control arm ball-joint cap. Record this as measurement 2. Measure from that surface to the center of the same arm’s inboard bolt and record measurement 3. Front ride height equals measurement 3 minus measurement 2. Record both readings, their units and the calculated result for each side. [Front measurement method](#/document/G1686616)

“Rear control arm” here names an arm in the front suspension; it does not mean the rear axle. Locate the points without loosening either fastener. [Front-suspension arm naming](#/document/G1692538)

steps.title: Measure rear ride height on both sides
steps.body: Using the same setup and surface gauge, measure from the flat, level surface to the center of the toe-link inboard cam bolt: measurement 2. Measure to the center of the toe-link outboard bolt: measurement 3. Rear ride height equals measurement 2 minus measurement 3. Record the original readings, units and result for each side. The subtraction order differs from the front. Do not substitute wheel-arch measurements or turn the cam bolt. [Rear measurement method](#/document/G1686616)

steps.title: Compare height and side-to-side lean
steps.body:
For the unmodified 2015 Mustang variants within this guide’s 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L scope, use Ford’s specification row excluding GT350 and GT350R. At curb load:

- Front ride height: 48.8 mm (1.921 in) ± 12 mm (0.472 in).
- Rear ride height: 32.1 mm (1.264 in) ± 10 mm (0.394 in).
- Maximum front left-to-right difference: 7.5 mm (0.295 in).
- Maximum rear left-to-right difference: 6.3 mm (0.248 in).

Compare each side’s calculated height with its axle’s specification, then compare the absolute difference between left and right on that axle with the lean limit. [Ride-height and lean specifications](#/document/G1686608)

If a result is outside those limits, recheck loading, pressures, measuring points and subtraction before pursuing spring or suspension diagnosis. An out-of-range height identifies a concern, not automatically a failed spring. Ford lists loading, incorrect or damaged springs and other suspension components among possible causes. Its stock specifications do not apply to aftermarket-equipped vehicles. [Ride-height diagnosis and modifications](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Choose the next job from the findings
steps.body:
Use the diagnostic decisions below to connect symptoms with observations. Correct an obvious cause where appropriate before continuing deeper diagnosis. Suspected joint or bearing wear needs the relevant mechanical test; suspected damper trouble may need assessment beyond appearance. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G1686610)

Record loose or missing fasteners for the exact component procedure. Suspension hardware is critical: Ford requires the specified or equivalent quality of replacement parts and the specified tightening method. Do not apply a torque from a neighboring component. Any repair is a separate job with its own replacement-hardware, alignment and calibration requirements. [Fastener requirements](#/document/G1692532)

steps.title: Close the inspection and verify the complaint
steps.body:
Record each inspected area as having no visible defect, needing assessment or remaining unchecked. Keep ride-height readings with their loading and pressure setup. If a wheel-supporting lift was used for measurement, clear the underside, keep the parking brake applied and return the vehicle to ground level using the lift manufacturer’s lowering sequence before driving. [Support and movement precautions](#/document/G1693189)

After safety-related findings have been resolved and any separate repair is complete, repeat the smooth-road check under comparable conditions. Record whether the original concern remains. If it does, continue focused diagnosis; a visible defect elsewhere does not prove the complaint has been fixed. Do not use a diagnostic replacement instruction when its required symptom is absent during testing. [Road-test basis](#/document/G1686610) [Replacement decisions](#/document/G1693185)

watchFor.title: An unsuitable lifting shortcut
watchFor.body: Use only Ford’s marked lifting locations. Never get beneath a car supported solely by a jack; an unintended drop can cause serious or fatal injury. The jack supplied with the vehicle is intended for emergency flat-tire changes, not this inspection. [Lifting safeguards](#/document/G1663631)

watchFor.title: A visual inspection becoming an all-clear
watchFor.body: No visible damage does not establish acceptable joint play, bearing condition or damper performance. Keep symptom-related concerns open until the relevant mechanical checks are completed. [Wear-related diagnostic checks](#/document/G1686610)

watchFor.title: Tightening everything in sight
watchFor.body: Use the specific component procedure for suspected loose hardware. Some suspension bushing fasteners require the suspension loaded during tightening; treating this as a general retightening exercise can damage bushings or produce incorrect clamp load. [Fastener and loaded-bushing requirements](#/document/G1692532)

watchFor.title: Grease as a noise diagnosis
watchFor.body: A squeak is a clue, not a grease request. Keep lubricant off the front and rear stabilizer bars and bushings because it can damage them. Investigate displacement, damage and the actual source of the noise. [Front dry rule](#/document/G1692534) [Rear dry rule](#/document/G1686652)

watchFor.title: An alignment appointment without a component inspection
watchFor.body: Include suspension damage and looseness when investigating tire wear or an alignment complaint. Alignment measurement does not settle whether a joint, mounting or arm needs attention. [Alignment-related diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

procedures.purpose: Teach preliminary inspection and symptom-based follow-up.
Identify rear suspension components.
Identify marked lifting locations and explain equipment-clearance precautions.
Prevent unexpected starts and vehicle movement during access and lowering.
Teach front and rear surface-gauge ride-height measurements.
Provide curb-load requirements and applicable height and lean limits.
Clarify the front suspension rear-control-arm naming.
Preserve the front stabilizer-bar and bushing lubrication prohibition.
Preserve the rear stabilizer-bar and bushing lubrication prohibition.
Explain critical hardware and loaded-bushing tightening requirements without adding a repair.
Support previous-repair checks and evidence-based replacement decisions.
Confirm the shared front suspension diagnostic route.
Confirm the shared rear suspension diagnostic route.

stepGroups.title: Record the concern and check the basics
stepGroups.summary: Establish symptoms, loading, tire condition and a safe road-test baseline.

stepGroups.title: Inspect the suspension
stepGroups.summary: Secure the vehicle, examine the connected assemblies and return it to its wheels.

stepGroups.title: Measure ride height when needed
stepGroups.summary: Measure both axles at curb load and compare height and lean with the applicable limits.

stepGroups.title: Choose the next action and verify
stepGroups.summary: Separate observations from confirmed faults and document the outcome.

diagnostics.finding: The car pulls or drifts on a smooth road.
diagnostics.meaning: Uneven loading, tire pressure and condition, tire forces, brake drag, alignment or steering may be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Address loading and tire findings first. If the pull remains, arrange Ford’s tire-force isolation, brake-drag and alignment checks in sequence; steering diagnosis follows when alignment is within specification. Wheel swapping and raised-wheel spinning are separate diagnostic work. [Pull diagnostic sequence](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: The car wanders, sways excessively or shimmies.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford lists loading, wheel security, suspension fasteners, joints, bearings, dampers, stabilizer parts and steering or alignment among the possible sources, depending on the symptom.
diagnostics.next: Use the physical findings to select the next test. Have suspected loose wheel or suspension hardware corrected using its exact tightening instructions before further driving. Include stabilizer condition for sway and focused front suspension diagnosis for shimmy, particularly with hard steering during deceleration. [Handling and shimmy chart](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Steering feels sticky, returns poorly or leaves the steering wheel off-center.
diagnostics.meaning: Poor return can involve strut mount bearings, binding ball joints or steering components. An off-center wheel can involve unequal toe settings or steering components.
diagnostics.next: Route sticky steering to joint, strut-bearing and steering assessment. For an off-center wheel, arrange alignment and steering checks. Do not adjust linkage merely to make the steering wheel look straight. [Steering-related symptoms](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: The front sits low, bottoms out or the car leans.
diagnostics.meaning: Loading, incorrect or damaged springs and other suspension damage are possible causes; worn front struts are also listed for front bottoming.
diagnostics.next: Correct loading issues and use steps 12–15 to measure both sides at curb load. Recheck an out-of-range result, then arrange diagnosis of the affected components. A height within limits does not exclude another suspension fault. [Height-related symptoms](#/document/G1686610) [Height and lean limits](#/document/G1686608)

diagnostics.finding: Tread wear is unusual or the ride feels harsh.
diagnostics.meaning: Pressure can contribute to either complaint. Rotation history, driving conditions, alignment and suspension condition can contribute to wear; dampers, springs and damaged components can contribute to harsh ride.
diagnostics.next: Correct cold pressures to the label and assess tire condition. Continue the appropriate symptom path if the concern remains. Record ride height for a spring-related ride complaint instead of selecting a damper solely from tire wear. [Wear and harsh-ride diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: There is a clunk, pop or low-speed rattle over bumps.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include loose hardware, damaged or displaced bushings, dampers, springs or seats and joints. Rear complaints also direct attention to shock bushings, stabilizer links and rear arm joints.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the indicated corner for a matching finding. Arrange mechanical testing where wear is suspected and repair the confirmed cause using its component procedure. [Clunk and rattle checks](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: The front crunches or ratchets while turning.
diagnostics.meaning: The source may be a strut bearing or mounting, spring or seat, stabilizer, steering component, hub or ball joint.
diagnostics.next: Distinguish noise through the steering movement from a confirmed steering-stop noise at full left or right lock. Ford identifies steering-stop noise as normal; that finding needs no repair. Other turning noises require focused inspection. [Turning-noise diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: A whine, roar or groan generally appears above 30 mph and changes with steering input.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford lists loose or damaged wheel bearings as a possible source.
diagnostics.next: Arrange front or rear bearing inspection as appropriate. Speed and sound are clues; they do not confirm which bearing, if any, needs replacement. [Bearing-noise symptom](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Noise occurs mainly during braking, acceleration or driveway transitions.
diagnostics.meaning: Neighboring systems, body structure and subframe movement can produce symptoms that resemble suspension noise.
diagnostics.next: For braking noise, include brakes, hubs, lower arms and powertrain mounts. For acceleration noise, include mounts, exhaust, hubs, body and subframe. For driveway-transition noise, include stabilizer links, body and subframe. Use the correct engine-specific procedure if follow-up reaches the powertrain or subframe. [Condition-related noise checks](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: A damper is wet or visibly damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The inspection has identified a condition needing assessment, but appearance alone has not established damping performance or a leakage replacement threshold.
diagnostics.next: Record the corner and extent of the condition and arrange damper assessment. Keep replacement separate from this inspection. [Damper diagnostic checks](#/document/G1686610) [Ford leak and damage inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: No visible defect explains the complaint, or it cannot be reproduced.
diagnostics.meaning: The visual inspection has not established the cause.
diagnostics.next: Keep the symptom notes and continue focused diagnosis. An electronic listening tool may help locate noise when used according to its manufacturer’s instructions, with connection points selected from Ford’s possible-source chart. Do not replace parts from a diagnostic result that requires an absent symptom. [Further noise diagnosis](#/document/G1686610) [Diagnostic assumptions](#/document/G1693185)

verification.title: Every area has an honest result
verification.body: Account for front and rear arms, visible joint areas, bushings, springs, dampers, mountings, stabilizers, steering and hubs. Identify each finding by corner and component. Keep obscured areas and required mechanical tests open. [Inspection coverage](#/document/G1686610)

verification.title: Any height comparison is valid
verification.body: Retain both original readings for each corner, units and calculated heights. Confirm correct tire pressures and curb load, front subtraction of 3 minus 2, rear subtraction of 2 minus 3, and separate left-to-right comparisons for each axle. Apply only the specifications appropriate to the unmodified vehicle within this guide’s scope. [Measurement method](#/document/G1686616) [Loading and limits](#/document/G1686608) [Aftermarket restriction](#/document/G1686610)

verification.title: The vehicle is secure and clear
verification.body: Before moving the car, confirm that all tools and inspection materials are removed, the vehicle is fully on its tires, and hoist arms or lift equipment are clear. Keep the parking brake applied until ready to move. [Support and movement precautions](#/document/G1693189)

verification.title: The original complaint has an outcome
verification.body: Once any safety-related condition and separate repair are resolved, compare the smooth-road behavior with the original notes. Record the symptom as absent, still present or not reproduced; do not treat completion of the visual checklist as proof of a repair. [Road-test verification](#/document/G1686610) [Diagnostic replacement decisions](#/document/G1693185)
