Switch the engine off and wait one minute to purge large air pockets. Leave the cap closed while hot and keep clear of rotating components. [5.0L initial purge](#/document/G1694583), [fan precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: 5.0L: check the intermediate level
steps.body: Read the level through the reservoir without opening a hot system. At this stage, the target is the top of MAX FILL when warm or the top of MIN FILL LEVEL when cold. For an adjustment, wait until the engine is cold, cover and remove the cap, then add the correct mixture to the top of MIN FILL LEVEL if needed. Reinstall the cap to its hard stop before restarting. The one-minute pause does not override the cooling requirement. [5.0L intermediate level and warning](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: 5.0L: reach the fan-on checkpoint
steps.body: Start the engine and let it idle to normal operating temperature. The cooling fan cycling on at least once is Ford's specified confirmation that the thermostat is fully open for this procedure. Observe from clear of the fan. If the checkpoint is not reached, do not declare the warm-up complete or substitute an invented threshold. Stop if abnormal temperature behavior develops. [5.0L warm-up checkpoint](#/document/G1694583), [fan precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: 5.0L: complete five purge cycles
steps.body: Complete five total cycles: hold 3,500 rpm for 30 seconds, idle for 30 seconds, then switch off for one minute. Restart as necessary for the next cycle. These follow the separate initial purge in step 21. Keep the climate control off, the cap installed and the vehicle restrained. [5.0L repeated bleeding sequence](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: 5.0L: finish the reservoir level
steps.body: After the final cycle, leave the engine off and let it cool before opening the system. Cover and remove the cap, check the reservoir and add the correct mixture to the top of MAX FILL if necessary. Reinstall the pressure-relief cap fully. Continue at step 26. [5.0L final level and closure](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: Pass the final concentration check or correct the fill
steps.body:
After completing the selected filling and bleeding route, let the engine become cold and measure concentration with the refractometer according to its instructions. Compare it with the target chosen in step 2. Retained coolant means the replacement bottle's label alone cannot establish the final system mixture. [2.3L measurement requirements](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L measurement requirements](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L measurement requirements](#/document/G1694583)

If the reading passes, confirm the final level and close the cap. If it does not, the job remains unfinished: use the specified concentrate and/or distilled water to correct the fill through the applicable engine's filling and bleeding workflow. If correction requires draining, repeat the cold access, collection and closure operations. Complete that branch again, including its required running checks, then recheck concentration and final level when cold. Adding concentrate or water to the reservoir and immediately sampling that addition does not establish the system mixture. Do not substitute an invented correction volume or circulation time. [2.3L adjustment and bleeding](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L adjustment and filling options](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L adjustment and bleeding](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: Inspect, record and check again after driving
steps.body:
As a finishing inspection, look for fresh coolant at the drain, reservoir cap and accessible areas disturbed during service. Confirm that the drain is closed, shields are secure, the cap is fitted and all tools and containers are clear. Continuing loss or abnormal temperature behavior needs diagnosis; a coolant change does not repair a leak. Use [cooling-system checks](#/maintenance/cooling-check) or [pressure and leak testing](#/maintenance/cooling-pressure-leak-test) for follow-on work. [2.3L closure](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L closure](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L closure](#/document/G1694583)

Record the date, mileage, engine, coolant specification, final concentration and filling method. Keep removed coolant contained and dispose of it under local requirements. Check the reservoir when cold over the next few drives; normal owner checks use the MIN–MAX range, and additions must not exceed MAX. Repeated topping up calls for investigation. [Ford follow-up checks and disposal](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: Hot coolant remains dangerous during bleeding
watchFor.body: One-minute engine-off periods allow purging; they do not establish safe cap-opening conditions. Let the engine cool before loosening the cap, and cover it with a thick cloth. Pressurized steam and liquid can cause serious burns. [2.3L precautions](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L precautions](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L precautions](#/document/G1694583)

watchFor.title: The system retains old coolant
watchFor.body: Less than 80% of capacity can be recovered with the engine installed. A single drain is neither a complete fluid evacuation nor a chemical flush. This is why final concentration must be measured. [2.3L recovery limit](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L recovery limit](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L recovery limit](#/document/G1694583)

watchFor.title: Required checkpoints stay required
watchFor.body: For the 2.3L, 5.0L and 3.7L non-vacuum branches, complete the initial purge, intermediate level check, fan-on warm-up checkpoint and five subsequent purge cycles. A full reservoir does not replace them. [2.3L sequence](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L non-vacuum sequence](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L sequence](#/document/G1694583)

watchFor.title: Overheating is a stop signal
watchFor.body: During this stationary service, stop the running sequence if abnormal temperature behavior develops and let the engine cool before investigating. On a later drive, an overheating warning or fail-safe operation requires getting safely off the road and seeking repairs; fail-safe cooling is an emergency provision, not permission to keep testing the result. [Ford overheating guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

3.7L coolant selection and draining, separate vacuum and non-vacuum routes, and reservoir-mounted refiller illustration.
5.0L coolant selection, draining, vacuum filling and subsequent running bleed.
Designated lifting points, hoist positioning and support precautions.
Relevant personal protection, starting, fan, hoist and vehicle-restraint requirements.

stepGroups.summary: Shared preparation and draining, with engine-specific shield and drain details.

diagnostics.finding: Orange coolant has become pink or light red but remains clear.
diagnostics.meaning: That color change can occur normally and does not itself establish degradation. [2.3L condition guidance](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L condition guidance](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L condition guidance](#/document/G1694583)
diagnostics.next: Base the service decision on history, contamination and concentration; do not order a flush solely for this color change.

diagnostics.finding: Coolant is dirty, rusty or contaminated.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacement is required, and contaminated coolant must not be reused because it can damage the engine or cooling components. [2.3L contamination guidance](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L contamination guidance](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L contamination guidance](#/document/G1694583)
diagnostics.next: Keep it separate for proper disposal and assess the contamination before treating the job as ordinary scheduled maintenance.

diagnostics.finding: Non-specified coolant was used.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford requires chemical flushing; routine partial draining is insufficient. [2.3L flushing requirement](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L flushing requirement](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L flushing requirement](#/document/G1694583)
diagnostics.next: Arrange the separate documented flushing procedure before completing the replacement fill.

diagnostics.finding: The vacuum refiller fails its manufacturer's checks.
diagnostics.meaning: The equipment-dependent filling route has not passed its operating requirements. Ford directs use of the actual manufacturer's instructions. [2.3L equipment requirement](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L equipment requirement](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L equipment requirement](#/document/G1694583)
diagnostics.next: Stop and resolve the equipment connection, equipment fault or system issue according to those instructions. Resume only when its checks pass.

diagnostics.finding: The fan never cycles during the specified warm-up.
diagnostics.meaning: The thermostat-opening checkpoint for the running-bleed branch has not been established. [2.3L checkpoint](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L checkpoint](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L checkpoint](#/document/G1694583)
diagnostics.next: Verify that fan operation was restored after hands-on work. If the checkpoint remains unmet, stop and arrange diagnosis rather than extending engine operation indefinitely.

diagnostics.finding: Final concentration misses the selected target.
diagnostics.meaning: The intended mixture has not been established, even if the reservoir level looks correct. [2.3L concentration requirements](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L concentration requirements](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L concentration requirements](#/document/G1694583)
diagnostics.next: Correct with the specified concentrate and/or distilled water within the applicable filling and bleeding workflow, then verify concentration and final level again. Do not accept an immediate sample of a reservoir addition as the final system result.

diagnostics.finding: Fresh leakage or repeated level loss appears after service.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement has an unresolved observation; fresh coolant does not establish that the system is sound.
diagnostics.next: Switch off and let the engine cool before inspecting the serviced areas. Continue with [cooling-system checks](#/maintenance/cooling-check) and, where needed, [pressure and leak testing](#/maintenance/cooling-pressure-leak-test).

verification.title: The correct engine branch is complete
verification.body: 2.3L and 5.0L: manufacturer-directed vacuum fill, initial purge, intermediate level check, fan-on checkpoint, five purge cycles and final level check. 3.7L: either the completed manufacturer-directed vacuum route or its full non-vacuum sequence. [2.3L completion](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L completion](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L completion](#/document/G1694583)

verification.title: Concentration passes after the completed workflow
verification.body: The final measured mixture matches the selected climate target—normally 48–50% coolant. Any correction has been followed by the applicable filling and bleeding workflow and renewed measurement, rather than an immediate reservoir sample. [2.3L mixture requirements](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L mixture requirements](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L mixture requirements](#/document/G1694583)

verification.title: Level and closures are correct
verification.body: For the running-bleed branches, the final service target is the top of MAX FILL. The cap is fully installed, the radiator drain is closed, and every removed shield has its fasteners and retainers installed. For the 3.7L vacuum option, finish the equipment-directed closure and confirm the cold reservoir level is within MIN–MAX without overfilling. [2.3L final checks](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L filling routes](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L final checks](#/document/G1694583), [Ford cold-level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: The finishing inspection has no unresolved loss
verification.body: No fresh escaping coolant is visible in the inspected areas, and any abnormal temperature behavior or continuing level loss has been routed for diagnosis. Recheck the level cold over the next few drives. This is a service completion check, not a pressure-test certification. [Ford follow-up checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539654&Uid=G1634794&ProcUid=G1749488&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

notes: Scope: 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L EcoBoost, 3.7L V6 or 5.0L V8. Follow only the matching engine branch.
The existing maintenance schedule remains separate from this procedure. Scheduled plug renewal and diagnosis of a running problem are different decisions.
guides.title: Spark plugs: fresh sparks without the parts-cannon bullshit
guides.summary: Replace the spark plugs on a 2015 Mustang using the separate 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L procedure, including coil access, plug gaps, tightening and reassembly.
guides.introduction: I treat scheduled plug replacement and misfire diagnosis as two different jobs. This guide handles renewal: get access, keep dirt out, fit the correct plugs and put everything back properly. A shopping cart full of ignition parts is a damn expensive diagnostic tool.
guides.why: The plug’s electrode gap and installation torque are engine-specific. So is access: the 3.7L requires upper intake manifold removal to reach the right-hand coils, while the other engines have different cover and tube arrangements. Choose one engine branch and stay with it. [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L coil access](#/document/G1675558), [5.0L coil access](#/document/G1675574)

when.summary: Replace every 100,000 mi (160,000 km) in normal use.
notes: Predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use or extensive idling/low-speed commercial use: 60,000 mi (96,000 km).

prepare.title: Get the correct plugs
prepare.detail: Ford’s 2015 owner information lists four SP-537 / CYFS-12Y-2 plugs for the 2.3L, six SP-520 / CYFS-12F-5 plugs for the 3.7L and eight SP-519 / CYFS-12Y plugs for the 5.0L. Match the replacement to the actual vehicle and follow its handling instructions. The workshop specification’s shared number 12405 does not distinguish these engine-specific choices. [Ford Motorcraft parts](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517147&Uid=G1634835&ProcUid=G1642992&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web), [2.3L quantity](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L quantity](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L quantity](#/document/G1675575)

prepare.title: Prepare hand tools and measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Have hand tools that fit the actual plugs and fasteners, a suitable plug-gap measuring tool, compressed air, and a torque wrench covering the specified low tightening values. The plug illustrations prohibit an impact wrench. The 3.7L and 5.0L also require a way to measure the additional tightening angles. Match socket and fastener sizes on the vehicle rather than guessing. [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L plugs](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L plugs](#/document/G1675575), [3.7L coil tightening](#/document/G1675558), [5.0L coil tightening](#/document/G1675574)

prepare.title: Know the plug gaps before opening the boxes
prepare.detail: 2.3L: 0.0295 in (0.75 mm). 3.7L: 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). 5.0L: 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). Check the replacement plugs against the appropriate specification; follow the replacement manufacturer’s handling instructions rather than bending electrodes by guesswork. [2.3L specifications](#/document/G1673181), [3.7L specifications](#/document/G1675554), [5.0L specifications](#/document/G1675570)

prepare.title: Add the 3.7L access supplies
prepare.detail: For the 3.7L, obtain new upper intake manifold gaskets, a hose clamp remover/installer, and clean blanking plugs for the opened vapor connection. The removed manifold gaskets must be discarded. Have suitable supplies ready to clean the upper and lower manifold sealing surfaces. [Upper intake manifold](#/document/G1681529), [Coupling cleanliness](#/document/G1671536)

prepare.title: Prepare for vapor-tube connections
prepare.detail: The 3.7L manifold access involves an EVAP purge connection; EVAP handles fuel vapor. The 5.0L involves PCV and crankcase ventilation connections. Have clean blanking plugs ready for open connections. These procedures require battery ground disconnection, clean coupling retainers and hand-operated releases. Tools can distort the clips and cause leaks. Fuel-pressure release is specified for liquid-fuel connections; these plug-access steps do not instruct you to open a liquid-fuel line. [3.7L manifold connections](#/document/G1681529), [3.7L couplings](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L coil access](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L couplings](#/document/G1671557)

prepare.title: Recognize the coupling before releasing it
prepare.detail: Keep the release styles separate. On the illustrated side-tab style, release both side tabs first, raise the retainer next, then separate the coupling; reconnect it straight onto the tube and press the retainer fully home. On the lower-release style, press the lower release point before lifting the retainer; reconnect straight onto the tube, then press the retainer down. A single locking-tab style releases by finger pressure; hold that tab released during connection and return it to its locking position afterward. Other illustrated styles use two release points before moving their retainer: complete that sequence before separating them, and restore their retainer after connection. A fitting with separate primary and secondary locks requires the secondary lock released first, the primary tab depressed second, and separation third; reconnect, pull-check it, then secure the secondary lock. Never borrow one style’s latch movement for another. [3.7L coupling actions](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L coupling actions](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: Make the underhood area safe
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup so the engine cannot be started remotely during the job. Wear eye and ear protection, particularly when using compressed air, and protective gloves around sharp edges. Inspect the cooling fan with the ignition off; do not work under the hood with a damaged fan. Fans can operate with the ignition off, so disable them before working nearby. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Wait for the correct engine temperature
steps.body: Remove plugs only when the engine is warm to hand touch after cooling down. Do not remove them from a hot engine or one that is cold soaked: either condition can damage the plug threads or cylinder head. Recheck this immediately before loosening the plugs, especially after the longer 3.7L access work. [2.3L removal precautions](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L removal precautions](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L removal precautions](#/document/G1675575)

steps.title: Disconnect battery power, then choose your branch
steps.body: Remove the battery-cover retainers and cover. Loosen the negative cable clamp nut, remove the negative cable from its terminal and position it aside so it cannot reconnect accidentally. Leave the positive cable connected; negative disconnection is sufficient to interrupt vehicle power. This is required directly by the 2.3L coil procedure and by the coupling procedures used for 3.7L and 5.0L access. Continue with steps 4–9 for the 2.3L, 10–21 for the 3.7L, or 22–27 for the 5.0L. All branches finish at step 28. [Battery disconnection](#/document/G1692356), [2.3L coils](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L couplings](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L couplings](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: 2.3L: remove the appearance cover and release the wiring
steps.body: Remove the engine appearance cover’s retaining nuts, then its retaining bolts, and lift off the cover. Release the wiring harness retainers. If a coil connector has a sliding cover over its locking tab, slide the cover back to expose the tab. Depress the connector locking tab and disconnect each of the four coil connectors. [2.3L coil access](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 2.3L: clean around and remove the coils
steps.body: Use compressed air to clear foreign material from the coils and surrounding area before removing them. Remove the coil mounting bolts. Give each coil a slight twist to release its seal, then remove it. Keep the coils organized by their original positions as a practical way to avoid mixing up observations. [2.3L coil removal](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 2.3L: clear the wells and remove four plugs
steps.body: Confirm the engine is still warm to hand touch. With the plugs still installed, blow foreign material out of each plug well—the recess surrounding the plug—before loosening anything. Remove the four plugs with hand tools. Keep dirt out of the open holes. If any plug is dropped, discard it: hidden internal damage can cause a misfire and subsequent engine damage. [2.3L plug removal](#/document/G1673189)

steps.title: 2.3L: check and install the replacement plugs
steps.body: Confirm a gap of 0.0295 in (0.75 mm). Guide each correct replacement plug into its hole and start its threads by hand; if it will not turn freely, stop and resolve the alignment or thread problem rather than forcing it. Tighten each plug to 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Use hand tools, and follow the replacement plug’s instructions about handling or compounds rather than adding something by habit. [2.3L gap](#/document/G1673181), [2.3L installation and torque](#/document/G1673189)

steps.title: 2.3L: inspect and refit the coils
steps.body: Inspect each coil assembly for cracks, rips or tears, and replace any damaged assembly. Install the coils and their mounting bolts. Tighten the bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). [2.3L coil inspection and installation](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 2.3L: restore the wiring and appearance cover
steps.body: Reconnect all four coil electrical connectors and secure their locking tabs. Reattach the wiring harness retainers. Install the engine appearance cover, then its retaining nuts and bolts; tighten those fasteners to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Continue at step 28. [2.3L reassembly](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the air cleaner outlet pipe
steps.body: The upper intake manifold must come off to reach the right-hand coils; this is established plug access, not optional extra disassembly. Start by disconnecting and positioning aside the brake booster tube and crankcase ventilation tube at the air cleaner outlet pipe. Loosen both pipe clamps and remove the pipe. [Right-hand coil access](#/document/G1675558), [Outlet pipe removal](#/document/G1675695)

steps.title: 3.7L: release the manifold vacuum hose
steps.body: Use the hose clamp remover/installer to disconnect the vacuum hose from the upper intake manifold. Detach the hose retainer at the throttle body, then the retainer at the upper intake manifold, and position the hose clear. [Manifold vacuum hose](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: disconnect the purge valve connection
steps.body: Disconnect the EVAP purge valve electrical connector and detach the associated wiring harness retainers. Before separating its quick-release coupling, use compressed air to clean the retaining-clip area. Release the actual coupling’s hand-operated locks in their proper sequence, then separate it without prying. Fit clean blanking plugs to the open connection. Dirt can damage the connection, and distorted clips can cause leaks. [Purge valve access](#/document/G1681529), [Coupling handling](#/document/G1671536)

steps.title: 3.7L: free the remaining manifold connections
steps.body: Disconnect the PCV tube from the upper intake manifold and position it aside. PCV is the crankcase ventilation connection. Disconnect the throttle body and MAP sensor electrical connectors; MAP means manifold absolute pressure. Detach the wiring harness retainers, then remove the upper intake manifold support bolt. Keep its hardware separate from the manifold mounting bolts. [Remaining manifold connections](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: lift off the manifold and discard its gaskets
steps.body: Remove the upper intake manifold mounting bolts and lift off the manifold. Remove and discard its gaskets. Clean and inspect the sealing surfaces on both the upper and lower intake manifold. Keep debris out of the exposed openings while working; the new gaskets need clean mating surfaces at reassembly. [Manifold removal and sealing surfaces](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the coils on both sides
steps.body: Use compressed air to clean the coils and surrounding areas before removal. Disconnect the coil electrical connectors, remove the mounting bolts, and remove the coils with a slight twisting motion to release their seals. Work through both sides so all six plugs are accessible. Keep each coil associated with its original position as an organizing aid. [3.7L coil removal](#/document/G1675558), [Six-plug quantity](#/document/G1675559)

steps.title: 3.7L: replace all six plugs
steps.body: Confirm the engine is warm to hand touch, neither hot nor cold soaked. Blow foreign material out of the plug wells before removing the plugs. Remove the six plugs using hand tools. Discard any plug that is dropped, because internal damage can cause misfire and engine damage. Check the replacements for a gap of 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). Start each plug by hand without forcing its threads, then tighten to 133 lb.in (15 Nm). Follow the replacement plug’s handling instructions rather than assuming a compound is needed. [3.7L plug handling and torque](#/document/G1675559), [3.7L gap](#/document/G1675554)

steps.title: 3.7L: inspect the boots and install the coils
steps.body: Inspect the coils and replace any rubber boot with cracks, rips or tears. Reinstall the coils and their mounting bolts. Tighten each bolt in two stages: first 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then an additional 50°. The angle is a second tightening movement after reaching the torque value. Reconnect the coil electrical connectors before covering the right-hand side with the manifold. [3.7L coil installation](#/document/G1675558)

steps.title: 3.7L: install new gaskets and tighten the manifold in order
steps.body:
Install new upper intake manifold gaskets, then position the manifold and install its seven mounting bolts. Follow the numbered tightening order for both stages: first 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then an additional 45°.

With the manifold viewed as in Ford’s tightening illustration, throttle body at the left, the order is: 1, lower-edge bolt second from the right; 2, the central upper bolt between the runners; 3, lower-edge middle bolt; 4, lower-edge leftmost bolt; 5, lower-edge rightmost bolt; 6, upper bolt at the right-hand end; 7, left-side bolt beside the throttle-body end. Match those positions to the illustrated sequence before tightening. [Manifold installation and numbered order](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: restore the support and electrical connections
steps.body: Install the upper intake manifold support bolt and tighten it to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Reattach the wiring harness retainers, reconnect the throttle body and MAP sensor electrical connectors, and reconnect the PCV tube to the upper intake manifold. [Manifold support and connections](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: reconnect the purge valve and secure its coupling
steps.body: Remove the temporary blanking plugs and inspect and clean both coupling ends. Push the EVAP purge coupling fully onto its tube and restore its own retaining clip or locking tabs. On the illustrated clip-retained styles, seat the retainer fully; the flush-fitting retainer must have its tabs locked. Pull on the connection to confirm it is retained. Reattach the wiring harness retainers and reconnect the EVAP purge valve electrical connector. [Purge valve reassembly](#/document/G1681529), [Coupling connection and retention](#/document/G1671536)

steps.title: 3.7L: restore the vacuum hose and outlet pipe
steps.body: Reconnect the manifold vacuum hose using the hose clamp remover/installer. Attach its retainer at the throttle body and its retainer at the upper intake manifold. Reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe and tighten both clamps to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Reconnect the brake booster tube and crankcase ventilation tube that were positioned aside. Continue at step 28. [Vacuum hose reassembly](#/document/G1681529), [Outlet pipe installation](#/document/G1675695)

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the appearance cover and move the ventilation tubes
steps.body: Remove the engine appearance cover. Clean the retaining-clip areas of the PCV valve and crankcase ventilation tube quick-release couplings with compressed air. Using the release sequence for each actual fitting, disconnect both couplings by hand and position the tubes aside. Protect open connections with clean blanking plugs. Do not pry the clips: deformation can cause leaks. [5.0L access](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L coupling precautions and releases](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the coil covers and coils
steps.body: Remove the ignition coil covers and disconnect the coil electrical connectors. Use compressed air to clear foreign material from the coils and surrounding area. Remove the coil bolts, then give each coil a slight twist to break its seal and remove it. Keep the coils organized by original position as a practical aid. [5.0L coil removal](#/document/G1675574)

steps.title: 5.0L: replace all eight plugs
steps.body: Confirm the engine is warm to hand touch, neither hot nor cold soaked. Blow foreign material out of the wells before loosening the plugs, then remove all eight with hand tools. Discard any dropped plug; hidden damage can cause misfire and engine damage. Check replacement gaps against 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). Start each replacement by hand without forcing it, then tighten to 133 lb.in (15 Nm). Follow the replacement plug’s handling instructions rather than adding a compound by habit. [5.0L plug handling and torque](#/document/G1675575), [5.0L gap](#/document/G1675570)

steps.title: 5.0L: inspect and reinstall the coils
steps.body: Inspect each coil assembly for cracks, rips or tears and replace any damaged assembly. Install the coils and their bolts. Tighten each bolt first to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then turn it an additional 45°. Reconnect all coil electrical connectors. This angle differs from the 3.7L specification; keep the branches separate. [5.0L coil installation](#/document/G1675574)

steps.title: 5.0L: restore the coil covers and ventilation connections
steps.body: Install the coil covers. Remove the temporary blanking plugs, inspect and clean the mating coupling ends, and reconnect the PCV valve coupling and crankcase ventilation tube coupling. Fully restore each fitting’s own retaining clip or locking mechanism and pull-check the connection. For a fitting with a secondary lock, push it onto the tube, confirm retention, then lock the secondary tab. [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L coupling connection](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: 5.0L: reinstall the appearance cover
steps.body: Check whether the cover’s rubber grommets stayed in the cover during removal. If they did, remove them from the cover and install them on the intake manifold first. Then install the engine appearance cover. Continue at step 28. [5.0L appearance cover installation](#/document/G1675574)

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and close up
steps.body: After completing your engine branch, reconnect the negative battery cable and tighten its clamp nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Reinstall the battery cover and its retainers. Ford notes that battery disconnection can temporarily change driving behavior while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive settings. That is not a reason to ignore a persistent misfire. [Battery connection and relearning](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Check the finished job and record it
steps.body:
Confirm that all coil connectors, harness retainers and covers disturbed in your engine branch are restored. On the 3.7L, also account for the manifold connections and outlet-pipe tubes; on the 5.0L, check both ventilation couplings and the appearance-cover grommets. [2.3L reassembly](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L coils](#/document/G1675558), [3.7L manifold connections](#/document/G1681529), [3.7L outlet pipe](#/document/G1675695), [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675574)

As a practical completion check, make a final visual pass for tools, temporary blanking plugs and any tube left aside before starting. Then start the engine and observe whether it runs normally. If a new rough-running condition appears, switch off and recheck the work before driving. Record the date, mileage, engine and plugs fitted, and retain useful observations from the removed parts. These checks do not replace diagnosis of a continuing misfire.

watchFor.title: Inch-pounds are not foot-pounds
watchFor.body: The plug specifications are 106 lb.in (12 Nm) for the 2.3L and 133 lb.in (15 Nm) for the 3.7L and 5.0L. Read the wrench’s units before tightening. [2.3L torque](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L torque](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L torque](#/document/G1675575)

watchFor.title: A dropped plug goes in the discard pile
watchFor.body: A plug can suffer internal damage without looking broken. Replace a dropped plug rather than installing a possible source of misfire and engine damage. [2.3L handling](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L handling](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L handling](#/document/G1675575)

watchFor.title: Keep the two cleaning stages separate
watchFor.body: Clean around the coils before lifting them out, then clean the plug wells while the plugs still close the holes. The second cleaning is easy to overlook when enthusiasm gets ahead of the air nozzle. [2.3L coils](#/document/G1673188), [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L coils](#/document/G1675558), [3.7L plugs](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L coils](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L plugs](#/document/G1675575)

watchFor.title: Do not reuse the 3.7L manifold gaskets
watchFor.body: The removed upper intake manifold gaskets are discard items. Have the replacements available before beginning this branch. [Manifold gasket replacement](#/document/G1681529)

watchFor.title: Preserve unusual evidence
watchFor.body: As a practical diagnostic aid, photograph unusual damage or contamination and label the removed plug by its original position. Do not assign a cause from appearance alone or automatically replace every coil because the plugs were due.

procedures.purpose: Replace the four 2.3L spark plugs with the specified handling and tightening.
Replace the six 3.7L spark plugs with the specified handling and tightening.
Replace the eight 5.0L spark plugs with the specified handling and tightening.
Access, inspect and reinstall the 2.3L coils and appearance cover.
Access, inspect and reinstall the 3.7L coils.
Access, inspect and reinstall the 5.0L coils, covers and ventilation tubes.
Remove and reinstall the 3.7L upper intake manifold for right-hand coil access.
Remove and reinstall the 3.7L outlet pipe during manifold access.
Handle and verify the 3.7L vapor coupling disturbed for manifold access.
Handle and verify the 5.0L ventilation couplings disturbed for coil access.
Disconnect and reconnect the negative battery cable.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and isolate power
stepGroups.summary: Make the engine safe to work around, establish the required temperature and disconnect the negative battery cable.

stepGroups.title: 2.3L EcoBoost
stepGroups.summary: Use this branch only for the 2.3L; finish at step 28.

stepGroups.title: 3.7L V6
stepGroups.summary: Remove and reinstall the upper intake manifold for right-hand coil access; finish at step 28.

stepGroups.title: 5.0L V8
stepGroups.summary: Restore the ventilation couplings, coil covers and appearance cover; finish at step 28.

stepGroups.title: Reconnect and check
stepGroups.summary: Restore battery power, inspect the completed work and check operation.

diagnostics.finding: A replacement plug has the wrong gap or does not match the engine-specific part.
diagnostics.meaning: It has not passed the basic fit-and-specification check for this job.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the part or gap mismatch before installation. Use 0.0295 in (0.75 mm) for the 2.3L, or 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm) for the 3.7L and 5.0L, following the replacement plug’s handling instructions. [2.3L gap](#/document/G1673181), [3.7L gap](#/document/G1675554), [5.0L gap](#/document/G1675570)

diagnostics.finding: A coil or boot has cracks, rips or tears.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford calls for replacement of the damaged component rather than routine reuse.
diagnostics.next: On the 3.7L, replace damaged rubber boots. On the 2.3L and 5.0L, replace damaged coil assemblies. [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1675558), [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673188), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1675574)

diagnostics.finding: A plug will not start smoothly by hand.
diagnostics.meaning: Its alignment or the condition of the threads needs attention; more force will not establish correct engagement.
diagnostics.next: Stop installation and inspect before proceeding. Do not use the final tightening torque to pull a reluctant plug into place. This is a handling check, not a thread-repair procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A coupling pulls free after reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: Its retaining mechanism has not secured the connection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect and clean the ends, reconnect using that fitting’s own locking sequence, fully seat its retainer and repeat the pull check. Do not proceed with an unsecured connection. [3.7L coupling retention](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L coupling retention](#/document/G1671557)

diagnostics.finding: The engine runs roughly after the work, or the original misfire remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The completion check has failed, or plug replacement has not resolved the original concern.
diagnostics.next: Switch off and recheck the connectors, coils and access components disturbed in the relevant branch. If the concern remains, continue diagnosis rather than repeatedly buying ignition parts. Battery relearning can temporarily affect driving behavior, but it does not establish the cause of a persistent misfire. [Battery relearning note](#/document/G1692356)

verification.title: Confirm the engine-specific tightening
verification.body: Check your recorded values: 2.3L plugs 106 lb.in (12 Nm), coil bolts 89 lb.in (10 Nm), appearance-cover fasteners 80 lb.in (9 Nm). 3.7L plugs 133 lb.in (15 Nm), coil bolts 62 lb.in (7 Nm) plus 50°. 5.0L plugs 133 lb.in (15 Nm), coil bolts 62 lb.in (7 Nm) plus 45°. [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [2.3L coils and cover](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L plugs](#/document/G1675559), [3.7L coils](#/document/G1675558), [5.0L plugs](#/document/G1675575), [5.0L coils](#/document/G1675574)

verification.title: Account for the 3.7L intake work
verification.body: Confirm new gaskets were installed, the seven manifold bolts received 89 lb.in (10 Nm) plus 45° in the numbered order, the support bolt received 89 lb.in (10 Nm), and both outlet-pipe clamps received 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Check the throttle body, MAP sensor, purge valve, PCV tube, vacuum hose, brake booster tube and all disturbed retainers. [Manifold reassembly](#/document/G1681529), [Outlet pipe reassembly](#/document/G1675695)

verification.title: Check retained connections and covers
verification.body: All coil connectors must be connected, the opened couplings retained, and the relevant covers restored. On the 5.0L, confirm the appearance-cover grommets were placed on the intake manifold before the cover was installed. [2.3L reassembly](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L reassembly](#/document/G1675558), [3.7L couplings](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L couplings](#/document/G1671557)

verification.title: Confirm power and operation
verification.body: The negative battery clamp must be secured at 44 lb.in (5 Nm), with the battery cover retained. Complete the visual check before starting, confirm normal running, and record the service mileage. Persistent rough running needs follow-up rather than a completed-job tick. [Battery connection](#/document/G1692356)

3.7L Mustang upper intake manifold spark plug access

notes: Keep the existing belt maintenance schedule separate from these condition decisions. The scheduled belt service does not itself establish a need for new pulleys or a tensioner. [Ford normal maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

Pulley, tensioner, generator and compressor repairs are follow-on jobs when diagnosis identifies a fault. The optional tests here help direct that work without turning routine belt care into an accessory-drive rebuild. [Diagnostic repair decisions](#/document/G1673162)
guides.title: Accessory belts: inspect and replace by engine on your 2015 Mustang
guides.summary: Inspect belt condition and seating, replace the accessory belt using the correct engine branch, and investigate noise without automatically buying every pulley in sight.
guides.introduction: I want a belt inspection to end with a useful answer, not a shopping cart full of guesses. This guide covers the 2015 Mustang’s 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L accessory belts, including the separate A/C belt operation required for 2.3L replacement. The detailed wear limits and tensioner tests below apply specifically to the 2.3L. Separate 3.7L and 5.0L A/C-belt replacement is outside this guide. Choose your engine’s branch and keep its routing drawing handy. [2.3L belt](#/document/G1688219), [2.3L A/C belt](#/document/G1688221), [3.7L belt](#/document/G1688121), [5.0L belt](#/document/G1688132), [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1673162)
guides.why: The belt carries crankshaft rotation around the accessory drive; its path and tensioner arrangement depend on the engine. On the 2.3L, Ford distinguishes belt damage from poor seating, contamination, pulley faults and tensioner trouble. Finding the cause gives the next belt a fair chance—and keeps the damn parts cannon parked. [Engine layouts](#/document/G1688219), [Drive-system diagnosis](#/document/G1673162)

when.summary: Inspect at 100,000 mi (160,000 km), then every other oil change until replacement. Replace the belts at 150,000 mi (240,000 km).
notes: Inspect sooner if there is damage, contamination or a new noise.

prepare.title: Choose one replacement branch
prepare.detail: Use steps 7–10 for the 3.7L, steps 11–14 for the 5.0L, or steps 15–23 for the 2.3L. Replacement requires intake-pipe access on all three engines; the 2.3L also requires removing and refitting its A/C belt. These operations are not automatically necessary for an initial visual inspection. [3.7L method](#/document/G1688121), [5.0L method](#/document/G1688132), [2.3L method](#/document/G1688219), [2.3L A/C access](#/document/G1688221)

prepare.title: Viewing aids and personal protection
prepare.detail: A light and inspection mirror are useful viewing aids. Wear eye and ear protection for service work, plus protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Keep hands and viewing aids clear during any running observation. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Tools and parts for belt replacement
prepare.detail: Have the correct vehicle-specific belt, a tool that fits the actual tensioner operating interface, tools matching the intake clamps and cover fasteners, and an inch-pound torque wrench covering the specifications in your branch. The intake-pipe clamp specification is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Match the actual hardware rather than guessing a socket or screwdriver size. [3.7L belt](#/document/G1688121), [3.7L pipe](#/document/G1675695), [5.0L belt](#/document/G1688132), [5.0L pipe](#/document/G1675684), [2.3L belt](#/document/G1688219), [2.3L pipe](#/document/G1675706)

prepare.title: Additional 2.3L equipment
prepare.detail: For full belt replacement, obtain the flexible stretchy-belt removal tool illustrated as 303-1419, a tool fitting the crankshaft pulley bolt for controlled hand rotation, cable ties at least 3 mm (0.12 in) wide, and a suitable cutter for removing the tie without damaging the belt. Have the correct A/C belt available for installation. The appearance-cover fasteners in this A/C-belt sequence tighten to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). [2.3L stretch-belt method](#/document/G1688221)

prepare.title: Access beneath the car, if needed
prepare.detail: If reaching the work requires lifting, use equipment with adequate capacity on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Locate the stamped triangles identifying the lifting points and support a jacked vehicle on stands before getting underneath. The emergency tire jack is not a service lift. Protect nearby suspension, steering, exhaust and body parts when positioning lifting equipment. [Lifting safety](#/document/G1693189), [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle before hands-on work. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup on the central display. Another person or a remote-start command must not be able to start the engine while you are working beside its rotating parts. [Starting precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Make the fan area safe
steps.body: With the ignition off, inspect the cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation. Stop underhood work if a fan is damaged; it can break apart during operation and needs replacement. Fans can operate with the ignition off, so disable them before working nearby. Keep that protection in place throughout hands-on belt work. [Fan precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Inspect the installed belt and its seating
steps.body: With the engine off, examine the accessible belt surfaces and each visible pulley contact. Compare the path with your engine’s routing drawing. Look for ribs sitting outside their matching grooves, an edge overhanging a pulley, contamination and visible deterioration. A light or mirror can improve the view; record any sections you cannot inspect rather than calling the whole belt checked. Every pulley must have correct belt seating after installation. [3.7L routing and seating](#/document/G1688121), [2.3L routing and seating](#/document/G1688219), [5.0L routing and seating](#/document/G1688132)

steps.title: 2.3L: separate small cracks from failed rubber
steps.body: Inspect the ribbed face—the lengthwise raised strips that engage the grooved pulleys. Small cracks alone do not condemn this belt. Replace it when a crack reaches the bottom of a groove and exposes the internal cord, or when any rubber chunks are missing. Long strips separating from a rib also count as failure. Apply these acceptance criteria to the 2.3L branch. [Cracking and chunking](#/document/G1673162)

steps.title: 2.3L: judge rubber deposits by severity
steps.body: Pilling is worn rubber collecting into little balls between the ribs. Examples 1–2 show small, scattered pills: no action is required. Examples 3–4 show longer pills reaching up to 50% of rib height: replace the belt if noise is apparent. Examples 5–6 show heavy groove deposits: replace the belt because noise and belt stability can be affected. Early pilling may clear during 3,000–5,000 mi (4,800–8,000 km) of normal driving; that observation is not a new service interval or a reason to ignore heavy deposits. [Pilling examples and decisions](#/document/G1673162)

steps.title: 2.3L: look for the cause before ordering parts
steps.body: Check for a damaged or contaminated belt, damaged or contaminated pulleys, an incorrect belt, poor fitment, loose hardware and obvious damage around the generator or A/C compressor. Correct an identifiable cause before continuing diagnosis. If lubricant or another leak has contaminated the belt, repair the leak and replace the belt. Do not apply lubricant or belt dressing: it can damage the belt material. Suspect pulleys also warrant checks for trapped stones and alignment; freedom-of-rotation checks require the belt to be unloaded. [Visual inspection and noise diagnosis](#/document/G1673162)

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the air cleaner outlet pipe
steps.body: Follow steps 7–10 only for the 3.7L. Disconnect the brake booster tube and crankcase ventilation tube from the air cleaner outlet pipe, and position them aside. Loosen the pipe’s two clamps and remove the pipe. Keep track of the original tube connections for reassembly. [3.7L intake access](#/document/G1675695)

steps.title: 3.7L: release tension and remove the belt
steps.body: Use the correctly fitting tool to rotate the accessory-belt tensioner counterclockwise. Hold the spring-loaded tensioner under control, slip the belt off and let the tensioner return under control. Remove the belt from the remaining pulleys. Keep fingers out of the belt-to-pulley pinch points. [3.7L belt removal](#/document/G1688121)

steps.title: 3.7L: route and install the replacement
steps.body: Match the replacement belt to the vehicle and follow the 3.7L routing drawing around the large upper-left pulley, right-hand generator pulley, lower-left crankshaft pulley and central tensioner. Preserve the exact path shown rather than copying another engine’s layout. Rotate the tensioner counterclockwise for clearance, fit the belt and return the tensioner under control. Inspect every pulley contact for complete seating. [3.7L routing and installation](#/document/G1688121)

steps.title: 3.7L: restore the intake
steps.body: Refit the air cleaner outlet pipe and tighten both clamps to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Reconnect the crankcase ventilation tube and brake booster tube to their original connections, then check that each connection is secure. Continue at step 27. [3.7L intake reassembly](#/document/G1675695)

steps.title: 5.0L: clear the air cleaner outlet pipe
steps.body: Follow steps 11–14 only for the 5.0L. Remove the engine appearance cover. Disconnect and position aside both brake booster tubes, the crankcase ventilation tube and the resonator air inlet tube. Loosen the two outlet-pipe clamps and remove the pipe. Match the tools to the actual attachments. [5.0L intake access](#/document/G1675684)

steps.title: 5.0L: release tension and remove the belt
steps.body: Rotate the accessory-belt tensioner counterclockwise using the correctly fitting tool. Hold it under control while slipping the belt off, then let it return under control. Remove the belt from the remaining pulleys. Keep the 5.0L routing drawing available for installation. [5.0L belt removal](#/document/G1688132)

steps.title: 5.0L: install along the V8 path
steps.body: Route the correct replacement belt exactly as the 5.0L drawing shows, including the upper small pulley and central tensioner. Rotate the tensioner counterclockwise to provide installation clearance, fit the belt and return the tensioner under control. Check every pulley contact for correct seating. This operation services the accessory belt shown in the drawing. [5.0L routing and installation](#/document/G1688132)

steps.title: 5.0L: reconnect the tubes and cover
steps.body: Refit the air cleaner outlet pipe and tighten both clamps to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Reconnect the resonator air inlet tube, crankcase ventilation tube and both brake booster tubes. Check the connections, then reinstall and secure the appearance cover using its actual attachments. Continue at step 27. [5.0L intake reassembly](#/document/G1675684)

steps.title: 2.3L replacement: remove the appearance cover
steps.body: Follow steps 15–23 for full 2.3L accessory-belt replacement. Remove the appearance-cover bolts and nuts, then lift off the cover. Keep its hardware together. This branch follows the A/C-belt access sequence, whose cover reassembly specification is 80 lb.in (9 Nm). [2.3L A/C-belt access](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: remove the outlet pipe without admitting debris
steps.body: Keep particles out of every opened intake connection: even small debris can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes. Loosen the clamp securing the CAC bypass valve inlet tube—the short curved tube shown connecting to the outlet pipe—then disconnect it and position it aside. Disconnect and position aside the crankcase ventilation tube. Loosen the three clamps identified in the outlet-pipe removal operation and remove the pipe. Keep the opened intake protected from debris while working. [2.3L pipe removal and debris precaution](#/document/G1675706)

steps.title: 2.3L: remove the A/C belt with the flexible tool
steps.body: Use the strap-style stretchy-belt tool illustrated as 303-1419. Turn the crankshaft pulley bolt clockwise by hand while feeding the tool onto the A/C compressor pulley through approximately 180°, wrapping it around the pulley as shown. At the lower belt departure, fold the flexible tool under the inside of the A/C belt so its free tail hangs downward. Pull the tool downward firmly in one quick motion to remove the belt. The fold and pull peel the belt off the compressor pulley; keep fingers clear of the belt and pulley throughout. [Illustrated A/C-belt removal](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: remove the accessory belt
steps.body: Rotate the accessory-belt tensioner counterclockwise with the correctly fitting tool. Hold it under control, slip the accessory belt off and return the tensioner under control. Remove the belt from the remaining pulleys. Keep the replacement accessory belt off the tensioner and away from the crankshaft pulley while installing the A/C belt in the following steps. [Accessory-belt removal](#/document/G1688219), [A/C installation clearance](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: position the A/C belt and cable tie
steps.body: Fit the A/C belt onto the compressor pulley, then place it over the top of the crankshaft pulley. Feed a cable tie at least 3 mm (0.12 in) wide through a crankshaft-pulley spoke, bring it up and over the belt and tighten it to hold the belt against the pulley. The illustration places this loop at the right-hand side of the crankshaft pulley with the tie tail pointing downward. Keep the accessory belt clear of the crankshaft pulley. [Cable-tie placement](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: roll the A/C belt onto the crankshaft pulley
steps.body: Continue turning the crankshaft clockwise by hand through 180° to install the A/C belt. Use controlled hand rotation; keep hands clear of the moving belt-to-pulley contact. Once the belt is installed, remove the cable tie completely without nicking the belt. [180° installation and tie removal](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: verify A/C-belt seating through a full turn
steps.body: With the cable tie removed, rotate the crankshaft by hand through a further 360°. Check that the A/C belt is correctly seated on both the crankshaft and compressor pulleys. Do not proceed with a rib outside its groove or a belt edge riding over the pulley. [360° seating check](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: install and seat the accessory belt
steps.body: Route the replacement accessory belt along the 2.3L path shown in its drawing. Rotate the tensioner counterclockwise for clearance, fit the belt and return the tensioner under control. Check every accessory-belt pulley contact, then check the A/C belt again. Both belts must be correctly seated before reassembly. [Accessory-belt routing](#/document/G1688219), [Both-belt completion checks](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: 2.3L: restore the intake pipe and appearance cover
steps.body: Inspect the intake components and clean them if needed before reconnecting them, keeping debris out of the system. Refit the outlet pipe and tighten the three clamps specified in its removal operation to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Reconnect the crankcase ventilation tube. Reconnect the CAC bypass valve inlet tube and secure its clamp; no separate tightening value is specified for that clamp. Refit the appearance cover and tighten its bolts and nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) for this A/C-belt sequence. Continue at step 27. [Intake reassembly](#/document/G1675706), [Cover reassembly](#/document/G1688221)

steps.title: Optional 2.3L static test: use the smaller access route
steps.body: Use steps 24–26 only when a concern warrants an unloaded tensioner check and you are not already working through the replacement branch. With the engine secured against starting, remove the appearance-cover fasteners and cover, then remove the outlet pipe using step 16. The tensioner-access drawing identifies three bolts as item 1 and a nut as item 2; retain that distinction for reassembly. This access route allows the accessory belt to be detached at the tensioner without removing the A/C belt. Do not remove the tensioner’s mounting bolts for this test. [Tensioner access](#/document/G1688220), [Static-test scope](#/document/G1673162)

steps.title: Optional 2.3L static test: check movement and the unloaded pulley
steps.body: Inspect around the tensioner for lubricant or other contamination. Repair leaks first; a contaminated tensioner must not be cleaned as a repair because its internal damping mechanism may be damaged. Rotate the tensioner counterclockwise, detach the accessory belt at that pulley and return the tensioner under control. Using the correct tool, move it from its relaxed position through its full stroke and back. Spring resistance must be present, without excessive sticking, grabbing or binding; some damping friction is normal. Turn the unloaded tensioner pulley by hand and check for damage, free rotation and alignment. A failed check calls for tensioner replacement through its separate repair procedure before operational testing. [Static criteria](#/document/G1673162), [Belt detachment](#/document/G1688220)

steps.title: Optional 2.3L static test: restore everything you detached
steps.body: If the tensioner passes, rotate it counterclockwise, refit the accessory belt and return it under control. Verify correct seating on every pulley. Reinstall the outlet pipe, tightening its three specified clamps to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm); reconnect the crankcase ventilation tube and CAC bypass valve inlet tube and secure the bypass-tube clamp. Refit the appearance cover using the torque assignments in the tensioner-access procedure: the three item-1 bolts take 53 lb.in (6 Nm), and the item-2 nut takes 89 lb.in (10 Nm). These assignments belong to this access branch. [Belt and cover restoration](#/document/G1688220), [Pipe restoration](#/document/G1675706)

steps.title: Finish the engine-off checks
steps.body: Inspect the complete installed belt path against your engine’s drawing and confirm seating at every pulley. Check all intake connections disturbed in your branch and confirm their specified clamp torques. On the 2.3L replacement branch, also confirm that the installation tie and stretchy-belt tool are removed and that both belts are seated. Remove all tools and viewing aids, secure the covers and restore anything disabled for safe service before preparing for operation. If the vehicle was raised, retain its parking brake and appropriate wheel restraints while safely returning it to the ground. [3.7L completion](#/document/G1688121), [5.0L completion](#/document/G1688132), [2.3L completion](#/document/G1688221), [Service and lifting safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: 2.3L: interpret remaining noise safely
steps.body: Only perform a running check after complete reassembly. Keep hands, tools and clothing clear of rotating parts. A chirp is an intermittent twittering sound: look for central tracking on flat pulleys, then shut the engine off before checking alignment, excessive pulley end movement or bent flanges. A metallic rattle directs attention to component installation and loose hardware, also checked with the engine off. Ford specifies a stethoscope or listening device to locate unresolved noise, including an idle check for chirp; route close-range listening to someone equipped to perform it safely. Correct the identified cause and retest. [Noise diagnosis](#/document/G1673162), [Rotating-parts precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: 2.3L: interpret tensioner movement after a passing static check
steps.body: The dynamic test follows a satisfactory static test. With the assembled engine running, observe from a safe position: the tensioner should respond to rapid acceleration or A/C clutch cycling, with movement that can be up to 4 mm. This describes its response during those changes, not a universal replacement threshold. Irregular movement under steady conditions can indicate a bent or out-of-round pulley or shaft, or damaged tensioner damping. Uneven belt-groove depth, called belt rideout, can also cause excessive movement; Ford checks that possibility by fitting a new belt. Diagnose the cause, repair as necessary and test normal operation again. Do not reach into the running drive to measure it. [Dynamic tensioner test](#/document/G1673162)

watchFor.title: A new belt over an active leak
watchFor.body: For the 2.3L, contamination requires fixing the leak and replacing the belt. Belt dressing or lubricant can damage the belt rather than repair the cause. [Contamination decisions](#/document/G1673162)

watchFor.title: Debris in the 2.3L intake
watchFor.body: Small particles can damage turbocharger compressor vanes. Keep opened intake connections protected and inspect the components before reconnecting them. [Intake precautions](#/document/G1675706)

watchFor.title: A cable tie left on the pulley
watchFor.body: The 2.3L A/C-belt installation tie comes off after the 180° installation turn and before the subsequent 360° seating check. Account for the entire tie before operation. [Tie removal sequence](#/document/G1688221)

watchFor.title: Cover torque depends on the access procedure
watchFor.body: The 2.3L A/C-belt sequence specifies 80 lb.in (9 Nm) for its cover bolts and nuts. The tensioner-access sequence assigns 53 lb.in (6 Nm) to the three item-1 bolts and 89 lb.in (10 Nm) to the item-2 nut. Keep the hardware identification and its branch together. [A/C access](#/document/G1688221), [Tensioner access](#/document/G1688220)

watchFor.title: Keep the units attached
watchFor.body: The intake-pipe clamp value is 48 pound-inches, or 5.4 Nm. Setting 48 pound-feet would be a very different—and unwelcome—experiment. [2.3L clamps](#/document/G1675706), [3.7L clamps](#/document/G1675695), [5.0L clamps](#/document/G1675684)

watchFor.title: Moving diagnostic limits between engines
watchFor.body: The crack limits, pilling categories and static/dynamic tensioner criteria here belong to the 2.3L diagnosis. Use them within that engine branch. [2.3L diagnostic scope](#/document/G1673162)

stepGroups.title: Set up and inspect
stepGroups.summary: Make hands-on work safe, check seating and apply the 2.3L condition criteria.

stepGroups.title: 3.7L accessory-belt replacement
stepGroups.summary: Remove the intake pipe, replace the belt and reconnect the intake.

stepGroups.title: 5.0L accessory-belt replacement
stepGroups.summary: Use the V8 access, routing and reassembly sequence.

stepGroups.title: 2.3L accessory-belt replacement
stepGroups.summary: Remove the A/C belt, replace the accessory belt and complete the illustrated stretch-belt installation.

stepGroups.title: Optional 2.3L unloaded tensioner check
stepGroups.summary: Use the smaller access route without removing the A/C belt.

stepGroups.title: Verify and follow up
stepGroups.summary: Complete reassembly checks and interpret remaining 2.3L symptoms.

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: small cracks without exposed cord or missing rubber
diagnostics.meaning: Small cracking alone does not meet Ford’s belt-failure criteria.
diagnostics.next: Continue checking seating, contamination and other damage rather than replacing solely for small cracks. [Crack criteria](#/document/G1673162)

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: exposed cord, missing chunks or long strips separating from ribs
diagnostics.meaning: The belt has unacceptable damage.
diagnostics.next: Use the complete 2.3L replacement branch and investigate any associated pulley, fitment or contamination concern. [Damage criteria](#/document/G1673162)

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: rubber pills between the ribs
diagnostics.meaning: The deposit severity determines the action.
diagnostics.next: Leave small scattered pills alone; replace for longer pills up to 50% of rib height when noise is present; replace for heavy groove deposits. [Pilling decisions](#/document/G1673162)

diagnostics.finding: A belt rib sits outside its matching pulley groove
diagnostics.meaning: The installation has not achieved correct seating; on the 2.3L this can also generate noise.
diagnostics.next: Correct fitment through the appropriate engine branch and inspect every pulley before operation. [3.7L seating](#/document/G1688121), [2.3L seating](#/document/G1688219), [5.0L seating](#/document/G1688132), [Noise diagnosis](#/document/G1673162)

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: belt contamination
diagnostics.meaning: A leak or other contamination source needs attention as well as the belt.
diagnostics.next: Correct the source and replace the belt, then test normal operation. [Contamination diagnosis](#/document/G1673162)

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: excessive tensioner binding, absent spring resistance or a damaged or poorly rotating tensioner pulley
diagnostics.meaning: The tensioner fails the static criteria; ordinary damping friction alone is expected.
diagnostics.next: Arrange tensioner replacement through its separate repair procedure before operational testing. [Static-test decisions](#/document/G1673162), [Tensioner repair](#/document/G1688220)

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: chirping or metallic rattling
diagnostics.meaning: Chirping points toward tracking or pulley alignment; rattling points toward loose components or hardware.
diagnostics.next: Use step 28 to direct diagnosis, correct the identified cause and retest. [Symptom chart](#/document/G1673162)

diagnostics.finding: 2.3L: irregular tensioner movement under steady conditions
diagnostics.meaning: Pulley or shaft geometry, tensioner damping and uneven belt-groove depth are possible causes.
diagnostics.next: Follow the static-to-dynamic sequence and investigate the cause before selecting parts. [Dynamic-test decisions](#/document/G1673162)

verification.title: The inspection has a defined result
verification.body: Record your engine, the sections inspected, any inaccessible sections and the findings. For the 2.3L, identify which findings meet the documented replacement criteria. An inspection record should distinguish checked surfaces from hidden ones. [2.3L condition decisions](#/document/G1673162)

verification.title: The installed belt follows the correct path
verification.body: Confirm the engine-specific routing and full seating at every pulley. On the 2.3L replacement branch, confirm that the A/C belt passed the additional 360° hand-rotation seating check and that the cable tie was removed. [3.7L verification](#/document/G1688121), [5.0L verification](#/document/G1688132), [2.3L verification](#/document/G1688221)

verification.title: The intake and cover are restored
verification.body: Confirm every tube removed in your branch is reconnected, the specified intake-pipe clamps are tightened to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), and the appearance cover is secured where removed. For the 2.3L, use the cover torque assignments belonging to the access branch you followed. [3.7L reassembly](#/document/G1675695), [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675684), [2.3L pipe](#/document/G1675706), [2.3L replacement cover](#/document/G1688221), [2.3L static-test access cover](#/document/G1688220)

verification.title: The original 2.3L concern has been retested
verification.body: After correction and full reassembly, check normal operation and whether the original noise or tracking concern remains. Record persistent symptoms for further diagnosis; a new belt does not establish that every driven component is healthy. [Operational verification](#/document/G1673162)

searchTerms: Mustang EcoBoost A/C stretch belt cable tie

notes: The normal-use schedule calls for changing both automatic transmission fluid and filter. A drain-only operation, which does not require filter removal, is a different scope. [Ford schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) · [Drain-only distinction](#/document/G1692052)

For a later level-only inspection, use the level-check procedure and correct the measured level as needed. Do not repeat the post-drain initial fill or air-purge routine simply because you opened the fill plug. [Level check](#/document/G1692053) · [Refill scope](#/document/G1692052)
guides.title: 6R80 automatic transmission fluid and filter service
guides.summary: Remove the pan, replace the filter, inspect the magnets, then refill, purge the cooling circuit and set the level at the specified fluid temperature.
guides.introduction: I treat this as one connected job: pan, filter, refill and a properly measured finish. The little level indicator gets the last word—not the number of empty bottles beside the car. This guide covers the 6R80 automatic in the original 2015 Mustang scope: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. The service requires pan removal and a temperature-controlled refill. [Pan and filter service](#/document/G1692033) · [Drain and refill](#/document/G1692052)
guides.why: The refill procedure circulates fluid through the torque converter and cooling system to clear trapped air. The specified fluid, correct temperature and final level all matter: unsuitable fluid or driving with a low level can cause transmission failure. A guessed capacity is a lousy substitute for the actual reading. [Refill requirements](#/document/G1692052)

when.summary: Change automatic-transmission fluid and filter every 150,000 mi (240,000 km) in normal use.
notes: A leak, contamination concern or diagnosed fault can require service earlier.

prepare.title: Confirm the transmission and plan the whole job
prepare.detail: Verify that the car has the 6R80 automatic. Have the equipment for the hot final check ready before draining anything; this service includes a warm-up drive followed by another hoist access. [Pan service](#/document/G1692033) · [Refill sequence](#/document/G1692052)

prepare.title: Get the specified fluid and matching parts
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft MERCON LV automatic transmission fluid, XT-10-QLVC, specification WSS-M2C938-A. Have the correct vehicle-specific replacement filter and a pan gasket available. For this scheduled fluid-and-filter job, fit a new filter; the repair procedure separately permits filter reuse when excessive contamination is absent. An undamaged pan gasket may be reused. [Fluid, filter and gasket](#/document/G1692033)

prepare.title: Gather dispensing, measuring and hand tools
prepare.detail: Have a universal fluid dispenser, a fluid suction gun for correcting overfill, and a diagnostic scan tool that displays transmission fluid temperature. Ford recommends a pressurized dispenser with 8–12 qt capacity, such as the Mityvac MITMV6412; that is equipment capacity, not the prescribed service fill. Also gather a drain container, clean wiping materials, tools matching the actual fasteners, and torque wrenches capable of 80 lb.in (9 Nm) and 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). [Refill equipment](#/document/G1692052) · [Pan torque](#/document/G1692033)

prepare.title: Arrange suitable lifting access
prepare.detail: The procedure uses a hoist. Confirm its capacity covers the car and any cargo or modifications. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points and position the lift adapters without contacting vulnerable suspension, exhaust, steering or underbody parts. The emergency tire jack is unsuitable for this job; never work beneath a car supported only by a jack. [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) · [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Prevent unintended starts and protect yourself
prepare.detail: If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or beneath the car. Keep the key under your control during engine-off work; start the engine deliberately only when the refill instructions require it. Wear eye and ear protection, use protective gloves around sharp edges, and consult the fluid's safety information before handling it. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Raise the car for pan access
steps.body: With the engine off and the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the car on the hoist. Use the triangle-marked lifting locations and check lift-arm clearance before raising it. The supported access route goes directly to the transmission fill assembly and pan. [Pan removal setup](#/document/G1692033) · [Lifting locations](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Remove the fill plug and short level indicator
steps.body: Locate the fill-plug assembly on the transmission case just above the pan flange, as shown in the procedure. Remove the assembly and separate the short level indicator from the plug for checking later. Keep both clean and protected from dirt. This is the indicator used for the refill—not an underhood dipstick. [Fill assembly](#/document/G1692033) · [Separate the indicator](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Remove the pan and collect the fluid
steps.body: Place the drain container beneath the pan before releasing it. Support the pan as you remove its bolts, then lower it while allowing the fluid to drain into the container. The illustration identifies 21 pan bolts. Pan removal is the specified draining method; removing the filter is a separate part of the combined service. [Pan removal](#/document/G1692033) · [Draining method](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Remove the gasket and filter
steps.body: Lift the pan gasket away and inspect it for damage. Remove the transmission fluid filter from beneath the transmission, keeping the drain container in place. Set the old filter aside for inspection before discarding it. Although the repair procedure allows an uncontaminated filter to be reused, this guide's scheduled service includes changing it. [Gasket and filter removal](#/document/G1692033) · [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Clean and inspect the pan and magnets
steps.body: Before moving the magnets, note their locations. Clean and inspect the pan and its magnet or magnets. For the late-build arrangement illustrated in the procedure, keep track of both magnets, labeled 1 and 2, so they return to their corresponding locations. Assess contamination before wiping away the evidence. The procedure supplies no numerical contamination limit. Conspicuous debris warrants diagnosis; fresh fluid does not establish that the cause has been repaired. [Pan and magnet inspection](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Check the filter socket for a retained seal
steps.body: Inspect the transmission pump bore—the opening that receives the filter's sealed neck. The old filter seal may remain inside after the filter comes out. If it has, carefully remove it without scratching the bore. Confirm the old seal is out before fitting the replacement filter. [Filter seal inspection](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Lubricate the seal and install the new filter
steps.body: Match the replacement filter to the vehicle and removed component. Make sure its seal is on the filter, lubricate that seal with the specified MERCON LV fluid, and install the filter in its proper position. The seal belongs on the filter during installation; leaving the old one in the pump bore is not part of the plan. [Filter installation](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Return the magnets and fit the gasket
steps.body: Place the magnet or magnets back in their original pan locations; the late-build illustration shows the two corresponding positions. Refit the pan gasket if it is undamaged, or install the correct replacement gasket if needed. Check that it follows the pan flange and its bolt holes before offering the pan up to the transmission. [Magnets and gasket installation](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Install and torque the pan
steps.body: Position the pan against the transmission and install its bolts. Tighten them in a crisscross pattern to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Move between opposing areas around the pan rather than tightening consecutively around the perimeter. Check the torque wrench's units: this specification is inch-pounds. [Pan installation and torque](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Add the initial engine-start fill
steps.body: With the engine still off, use the fluid dispenser through the fill opening to add 3.3 L (3.5 qt) of the specified MERCON LV fluid. That is the initial quantity after pan or filter removal, allowing the engine to be started; it is not the finished service level. Additional fluid is determined by the following readings. [Initial service fill](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Establish the cold level before driving
steps.body: Connect the scan tool and monitor transmission fluid temperature. Start the engine, select PARK and let it idle at 600–750 rpm. Use the short level indicator in the fill opening to check the fluid. Add fluid until the reading reaches the indicated area below the crosshatch, shown in the refill procedure's cold-fill illustration. Do not begin the warm-up drive before reaching this level: driving low can damage the transmission. [Cold running check](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Close the fill opening before the warm-up drive
steps.body: Return the level indicator to the fill-plug assembly, install the assembly and tighten the fill plug to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). Lower the car using the hoist's operating procedure before driving. [Fill plug installation](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Drive to purge the cooling circuit
steps.body: Drive safely for the conditions and obey traffic laws while monitoring transmission fluid temperature with the scan tool. Reach 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). This drive circulates fluid through the torque converter and transmission cooling system to eliminate trapped air. It is a required part of this refill after pan service; it is not an instruction to repeat the initial fill during an ordinary level-only check. [Refill air purge](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Return to the hoist and cycle the selector
steps.body: With the engine idling at 600–750 rpm in PARK, confirm the fluid is within 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), then raise the car on the hoist.
