For the final level check, with the engine running, move the selector through every gear position, holding each for approximately 5 seconds, then return it to PARK. All drive wheels must be elevated before selecting a drive position on the hoist; otherwise the car can move unexpectedly. [Hot refill setup](#/document/G1692052) · [Selector sequence](#/document/G1692053) · [Hoist running safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Read the hot level in the dotted area
steps.body: Remove the fill plug and separate the indicator from it. With the engine idling in PARK, check the level using the indicator and verify the fluid temperature remains within 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). The final target is the upper level of the dotted area marked B, not the crosshatched area A. If the fluid is hotter than the specified window, allow it to cool into range before judging the reading. [Hot level target](#/document/G1692053) · [Idle speed](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Correct the level and close the assembly
steps.body: If the hot reading is below the upper level of dotted area B, add the specified fluid with the dispenser. If it is above that level, withdraw fluid with the suction gun. Recheck the reading and scan-tool temperature until both meet the specification. Return the indicator to the plug assembly, install it and tighten the fill plug to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). [Level correction and closure](#/document/G1692052) · [Final level check](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Inspect the serviced areas and finish
steps.body: As a completion check, look for fresh leakage around the pan flange and fill plug before lowering the car. Confirm that the pan received its crisscross tightening and that the fill assembly is installed. Record the fluid specification, filter replacement, gasket decision, final temperature and level. If slipping, slow shifts or leakage remains, check the level and diagnose the cause; the service alone does not establish that a fault has been repaired. [Pan closure](#/document/G1692033) · [Fluid-related symptoms](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: The initial fill is only the beginning
watchFor.body: The 3.3 L (3.5 qt) quantity follows pan or filter removal. The separate 11.35 L (12 qt) initial quantity in the source applies to an overhauled transmission, not this service. Finish by measured level. [Refill quantities](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: Cold and hot readings use different targets
watchFor.body: Before driving, use the illustrated area below the crosshatch. At 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), use the upper level of dotted area B. Mixing those instructions makes the little indicator a pain in the ass for entirely avoidable reasons. [Cold and hot targets](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: Low level means no driving
watchFor.body: Do not use a road test to see whether a low transmission will sort itself out. Establish the required level first; driving low can cause internal failure. [Low-fluid warning](#/document/G1692053)

watchFor.title: A seal left behind
watchFor.body: Inspect the pump bore after removing the filter. Remove any retained old seal carefully, without scoring the bore, before installing the lubricated filter seal. [Seal handling](#/document/G1692033)

watchFor.title: Fluid specification matters
watchFor.body: Use MERCON LV meeting WSS-M2C938-A. Other fluid can cause abnormal operation or transmission failure. Keep this job to the specified pan, filter and refill service rather than substituting a generic flush or additive routine. [Specified fluid](#/document/G1692052)

procedures.purpose: Remove, inspect and reinstall the transmission pan, gasket, filter and magnets.
Perform the initial refill, cold running check, cooling-system air purge and level correction.
Cycle the selector and verify the temperature-controlled final fluid level.
Identify lifting points and avoid unsafe vehicle support or underbody damage.
Apply relevant remote-start, personal-protection and hoist-running precautions.

stepGroups.title: Access and drain
stepGroups.summary: Raise the car, open the fill assembly and remove the pan and filter.

stepGroups.title: Inspect and reassemble
stepGroups.summary: Check contamination and the filter seal, then reinstall the filter, magnets, gasket and pan.

stepGroups.title: Establish the initial level
stepGroups.summary: Add the engine-start quantity and establish the running cold level before driving.

stepGroups.title: Purge and set the hot level
stepGroups.summary: Warm the cooling circuit, cycle the selector and adjust to the dotted B target.

stepGroups.title: Check the finished service
stepGroups.summary: Inspect for leakage and record the result.

diagnostics.finding: Excessive contamination in the removed filter, pan or magnets
diagnostics.meaning: The repair procedure's condition for filter reuse is not met. It provides no numerical debris threshold or diagnosis from appearance alone. [Inspection criteria](#/document/G1692033)
diagnostics.next: Fit the new filter for this service, retain useful observations of the debris and arrange diagnosis of the contamination rather than assuming the fluid change resolves its cause.

diagnostics.finding: The old filter comes out without its seal
diagnostics.meaning: The seal may still be in the pump bore. [Retained seal check](#/document/G1692033)
diagnostics.next: Inspect the bore and carefully remove the retained seal without scratching it. Confirm the replacement filter carries its lubricated seal before installation.

diagnostics.finding: The final hot reading is below dotted area B's upper level
diagnostics.meaning: The level is low if measured at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F) under the specified running conditions. [Hot reading](#/document/G1692052)
diagnostics.next: Add the specified fluid with the dispenser and recheck temperature and level. Do not drive with a low level.

diagnostics.finding: The final hot reading is above dotted area B's upper level
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission is overfilled under the specified checking conditions. [Overfill correction](#/document/G1692052)
diagnostics.next: Remove fluid with the suction gun, then repeat the temperature and level check.

diagnostics.finding: The temperature is outside the checking window
diagnostics.meaning: The reading does not establish the specified final level. Extended high-speed driving, traffic, hot weather or towing may leave the fluid too hot. [Temperature requirements](#/document/G1692053)
diagnostics.next: Bring the fluid into 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), allowing cooling when needed, and repeat the running level check.

diagnostics.finding: Slipping, slow shifts or leakage continues
diagnostics.meaning: These symptoms call for a fluid-level check; a fluid and filter change does not identify their underlying cause. [Symptom guidance](#/document/G1692052)
diagnostics.next: Verify the level correctly, inspect any leakage and obtain further diagnosis if symptoms remain.

verification.title: Pan and filter assembly is complete
verification.body: Confirm the filter seal was checked and lubricated, the filter installed, magnets returned, gasket assessed and pan bolts tightened crisscross to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). [Assembly requirements](#/document/G1692033)

verification.title: The refill and air purge were completed
verification.body: Confirm the cold running level was established before driving and the warm-up drive reached 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). [Refill sequence](#/document/G1692052)

verification.title: Final level was measured under the right conditions
verification.body: After holding each selector position for approximately 5 seconds, return to PARK. Confirm the final reading reaches the upper level of dotted area B at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), with the engine idling at 600–750 rpm. [Selector and target](#/document/G1692053) · [Idle requirement](#/document/G1692052)

verification.title: The transmission is closed and checked
verification.body: Confirm the indicator is back in the fill assembly and the plug is tightened to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). Inspect the pan and plug for fresh leakage and address any continuing symptoms before considering the work complete. [Fill plug torque](#/document/G1692052)

notes: Keep the existing maintenance schedule separate from this procedure. Do not transfer these MT82 fluid instructions or its schedule to the 3160 or an automatic transmission.
guides.title: MT82 manual transmission fluid: drain, refill and set the level
guides.summary: Change the fluid in a 2015 Mustang’s MT82 manual gearbox using the correct lubricant, a level vehicle and the specified fluid depth.
guides.introduction: I start this job by reading the fluid specification, because “transmission fluid” is a category, not a shopping instruction. The MT82 calls for Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, specification WSS-M2C200-D2. Yes, the bottle says dual clutch and your Mustang has a clutch pedal. The specification gets the final damn word. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)
guides.why: This service renews the lubricant used by the manual gearbox. Getting the product and final level right matters more than simply pouring in a stated quantity: Ford supplies both a capacity and a separate level-check illustration. Fresh fluid also does not establish that an existing shifting problem has been repaired. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

when.summary: Every 150,000 mi (240,000 km) in normal use.
notes: Predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use: 60,000 mi (96,000 km).
Predominantly dusty or sandy driving: 50,000 mi (80,000 km).

prepare.title: Confirm the application
prepare.detail: This guide covers the MT82 in the original 2015 Mustang scope: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. Confirm that the installed gearbox is an MT82 before choosing fluid or starting work. These instructions do not cover the 3160 or an automatic transmission. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

prepare.title: Get the correct fluid
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, meeting WSS-M2C200-D2, available for the listed 2.7 qt (2.6 L) capacity. XL-18 additive is required only after synchronizer replacement; it is not part of this routine fluid change. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

prepare.title: Gather filling, draining and measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Ford specifies a fluid suction gun—a hand-operated tool for transferring fluid into or out of the gearbox. Also gather a drain container, tools that fit the actual plugs, a torque wrench capable of 26 lb-ft (35 Nm), clean wiping materials and a clean measuring aid for checking fluid depth below the fill opening. Match the tools to the actual fasteners rather than guessing a drive size. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

prepare.title: Arrange level underbody access
prepare.detail: Use lifting and support equipment rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. The car must remain level for filling and checking. Ford identifies lifting locations with triangle stamps in the body or frame; the supplied lifting illustration shows the four locations along the sides. The emergency tire jack is not suitable for this service. [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

prepare.title: Protect yourself
prepare.detail: Have eye and ear protection available, use protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts, and read the fluid’s safety information before handling it. Improper chemical handling and sharp components can cause injury. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If remote start is equipped, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working underneath. An unexpected start during service can cause serious injury or death. Put on the required protection before beginning. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Raise and support the Mustang level
steps.body:
Work on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block any wheels that remain on the ground. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points before raising the car. If using a jack, support the vehicle on stands before going underneath; a jack alone can lower unexpectedly and crush someone beneath it. Do not lift against either bumper. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631)

If using a hoist, use equipment of adequate capacity and position its arms at the specified lifting locations. Check that adapters and arms do not bear against or interfere with the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets, axle or rear cover. For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving aboard. Keep the vehicle level for the fluid service. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

steps.title: Identify both service plugs
steps.body: Locate the drain plug on the underside of the transmission and the separate fill plug on the side of the housing. The close-up of the fill opening shows the cast-in FILL marking. Confirm that you can reach both plugs with the appropriate tools before draining. The documented service accesses these plugs directly; it does not call for wheel removal or transmission disassembly. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Drain the old fluid
steps.body: Position the drain container beneath the drain plug, remove the plug and let the transmission fluid drain into the container. Keep the removed plug where it will stay clean and remain identifiable. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

steps.title: Close the drain and open the fill port
steps.body: Reinstall the drain plug after draining and tighten it to 26 lb-ft (35 Nm). Then remove the separate fill plug to open the filling port. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

steps.title: Pump in the specified lubricant
steps.body: Use the fluid suction gun to add XT-11-QDC fluid meeting WSS-M2C200-D2 through the fill opening. Ford lists capacity as 2.7 qt (2.6 L); use that figure to plan the supply, then establish the final amount by checking the level. Do not add XL-18 for an ordinary drain and refill—it is specified only after synchronizer replacement. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

steps.title: Set the fluid surface below the opening
steps.body:
Keep the vehicle level. Check the vertical distance from the lower edge of the fill opening to the fluid surface. Ford’s level illustration specifies 10 ± 3 mm below that edge, giving an acceptable distance of 7–13 mm. The target is below the opening, so fluid spilling from the hole is not the prescribed finished level. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

If the surface is more than 13 mm below the edge, add fluid with the suction gun. If it is less than 7 mm below the edge, withdraw fluid. Remove the gun from the opening and check again after each adjustment until the surface is within the specified range. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Install the fill plug
steps.body: Once the level is correct, reinstall the fill plug and tighten it to 26 lb-ft (35 Nm). Confirm that both the drain and fill plugs have been installed and tightened before moving on. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Check the closures for leakage
steps.body: As a practical completion check, wipe away spilled fluid around both plugs, then look for fresh wetness. Cleaning first helps distinguish a spill from fluid continuing to escape. If fresh fluid appears, resolve the leak and repeat the level check before calling the service finished. The level check still requires a level vehicle and the same fill-plug torque afterward. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Clear the work area and finish
steps.body:
Remove the drain container, suction gun and loose tools from beneath the vehicle. Return the car to the ground using the lifting equipment’s operating instructions, keeping everyone clear while the supports are changed. Keep the vehicle secured against movement during this process. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

Record the date, mileage and lubricant used. Record any remaining leak or shifting complaint so it receives diagnosis.

watchFor.title: The product name can mislead
watchFor.body: Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, specification WSS-M2C200-D2, is the listed MT82 lubricant. Shop by that requirement rather than a generic manual-transmission, automatic-transmission or axle-oil label. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

watchFor.title: Capacity does not replace the level check
watchFor.body: The listed 2.7 qt (2.6 L) capacity and the illustrated 10 ± 3 mm fluid depth serve different purposes. Finish by measuring the level with the vehicle level, rather than stopping solely because a measured quantity has gone in. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

watchFor.title: A top-up is not a leak repair
watchFor.body: Recurring wetness or a level that repeatedly drops needs investigation. Repeatedly adding fluid can conceal the unresolved problem.

procedures.purpose: Identify the drain plug and perform the MT82 drain, refill and plug-tightening operations.
Identify the fill opening and establish the illustrated fluid depth.
Select the lubricant, plan fluid quantity and distinguish routine service from the additive requirement after synchronizer replacement.
Identify lifting locations and protect the vehicle during underbody access.
Prevent unexpected starting and establish safe lifting, support and personal protection.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and reach the plugs
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting, support the car level and identify the two service plugs.

stepGroups.title: Drain the gearbox
stepGroups.summary: Collect the old fluid and reinstall the drain plug before filling.

stepGroups.title: Refill and establish the level
stepGroups.summary: Use the specified fluid, adjust its depth and tighten the fill plug.

stepGroups.title: Check and finish
stepGroups.summary: Inspect for leakage, clear the equipment and record the service.

diagnostics.finding: The fluid surface is more than 13 mm below the lower edge of the fill opening.
diagnostics.meaning: The level is below the illustrated acceptable range, provided the vehicle is level.
diagnostics.next: Add the specified fluid with the suction gun, remeasure and stop within 7–13 mm below the opening. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328) [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

diagnostics.finding: The fluid surface is less than 7 mm below the lower edge of the fill opening.
diagnostics.meaning: The level is above the illustrated acceptable range, provided the vehicle is level.
diagnostics.next: Withdraw fluid with the suction gun and remeasure. Reinstall the fill plug at 26 lb-ft (35 Nm) once the level is correct. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

diagnostics.finding: Fresh wetness returns after the plug areas have been wiped clean.
diagnostics.meaning: Residual spillage alone no longer explains the observation; a leak needs investigation.
diagnostics.next: Locate and resolve the source, then repeat the level check before returning the car to use. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

diagnostics.finding: A shifting complaint remains after the service.
diagnostics.meaning: The fluid change has not established the cause or repaired the complaint.
diagnostics.next: Arrange diagnosis of the shifting problem. Do not treat extra fluid or routine XL-18 dosing as the next repair; XL-18 is specified only after synchronizer replacement. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

verification.title: Correct lubricant and measured level
verification.body: Confirm XT-11-QDC / WSS-M2C200-D2 was used and the fluid surface was checked at 10 ± 3 mm below the fill opening’s lower edge while the vehicle was level. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

verification.title: Both plugs secured
verification.body: Confirm the drain plug and fill plug were each tightened to 26 lb-ft (35 Nm). [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

verification.title: No fresh leakage and equipment cleared
verification.body: Check the wiped plug areas for fresh fluid, account for the tools and fluid-transfer equipment, and record any unresolved observation with the service details.

notes: Confirm the vehicle-specific instruction before booking routine axle-fluid replacement. Suspected leakage or submersion needs attention regardless of the odometer.
guides.title: Rear axle fluid: confirm the schedule and the differential type
guides.summary: Understand Ford’s 150,000-mile normal-schedule entry and the separately stated axle exception before choosing a service deadline.
guides.introduction: Rear axle lubricant protects the gears and bearings inside the differential. Choosing the right service requires two pieces of information: the fitted differential and the maintenance instruction that applies to the car’s use. The drain/fill procedure also has branches for different equipment, including whether a drain plug or cooler is fitted.
guides.why: A gear-oil choice, friction-modifier instruction or filling method from another axle can be wrong for this one. Confirming the assembly first avoids turning a routine fluid job into an experiment.

when.summary: The normal schedule lists rear axle fluid replacement at 150,000 mi (240,000 km); read the axle exception before treating that as an unconditional deadline.
notes: Ford’s special-conditions page separately says axle fluid checks or changes are not required unless leakage is suspected or the assembly has been submerged. These online instructions need to be reconciled for the vehicle’s applicable schedule.
Suspected leakage or submersion needs prompt assessment regardless of mileage.

prepare.title: Identify the axle and equipment
prepare.detail: Confirm the differential type and whether a cooler is fitted.

prepare.title: Confirm the applicable service plan
prepare.detail: Review the normal entry together with the exception and the vehicle’s original maintenance information; obtain a vehicle-specific recommendation if they differ.

steps.title: Resolve the service scope
steps.body: Decide whether this is routine replacement, a leak repair or contamination after water exposure.

steps.title: Use the correct equipment branch
steps.body: Follow the draining/filling procedure for the actual axle, with its specified lubricant and any applicable additive.

steps.title: Finish with the correct level
steps.body: Complete the specified fill, closure and leak checks, and record what fluid and service were used.

watchFor.title: Water exposure or leaking seals
watchFor.body: Do not delay assessment because a mileage milestone is far away.

watchFor.title: Additive used by habit
watchFor.body: A limited-slip label alone is not a substitute for the exact application instructions.

procedures.purpose: Use the axle-equipment branches for draining and filling.
Check differential fluid level.
Confirm the axle lubricant specifications.

notes: Applicability remains the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.
Clean, sound connections can complete this maintenance task without battery removal, tray removal, charging or drain testing.
Battery replacement and repairs to damaged cables, clamps or mounting components are separate operations.
guides.title: Battery connections: inspect, clean and reconnect
guides.summary: Check the connections on your 2015 Mustang, clean corrosion when needed, and complete the reconnection checks before blaming the battery.
guides.introduction: I start a weak-start investigation with the damn connections. This guide covers connection inspection and cleaning on the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, including safe disconnection, reconnection and the applicable window and engine relearning steps. Battery replacement, charging and electrical testing remain separate jobs.
guides.why: Starting needs a sound electrical path as well as a battery that can do its job. Ford lists connection maintenance and battery-performance inspection separately, so clean terminals earn you a completed maintenance task—not a battery-health certificate. That distinction can save a perfectly unnecessary parts purchase. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

when.summary: Check battery connections every six months and clean as needed. Battery performance is part of the recommended multi-point inspection.

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Keep the vehicle stationary with the parking brake applied. Begin with the ignition off and the key removed. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup so someone cannot start the engine during your work. The window-initialization branch briefly requires powered window operation; keep the engine stopped during that cable work. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189), [parking brake](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web), [window initialization](#/document/G1957566)

prepare.title: Protect against gas, acid and lead
prepare.detail: Work with adequate ventilation. Keep flames, sparks and smoking materials away: battery gases can explode. Shield your face and protect your eyes against acid splashes; avoid acid contact with skin or clothing. Keep children away and wash your hands after handling terminals because they contain lead compounds. If acid contacts skin or eyes, flush immediately with water for at least 15 minutes and obtain prompt medical attention. If swallowed, contact a physician immediately. [Ford battery precautions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Gather the inspection and cleaning kit
prepare.detail: Have a light, a container for the cover retainers, a tool matching the actual retainers, and a wrench or socket matching the terminal-clamp nuts. Cleaning needs a wire brush; Ford also permits baking soda mixed with water to neutralize acid. Have a torque wrench capable of 44 lb.in (5 Nm) for reconnection. Keep tools from bridging terminals or contacting other conductive parts while touching a terminal. [Terminal access and torque](#/document/G1692356), [Ford cleaning method](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Keep the underhood work contained
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Review the safety information for any materials used. With the ignition off, inspect the cooling fans for visible damage; do not continue underhood work with a cracked or separating fan. Fans can operate with the ignition off. Stay outside their operating area; work nearby requires disabling them first. This connection service leaves the battery, hold-down and tray installed. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189), [battery mounting](#/document/G1692362)

prepare.title: Plan for windows if you disconnect
prepare.detail: If one-touch-up windows are fitted, read steps 6, 10 and 13 before removing a cable. Ford requires an existing window motor to be de-initialized by interrupting its power while the glass is moving before initialization. A helper makes the battery-cable method practical. Convertible models do not have one-touch-up or bounce-back features, so that branch does not apply to them. [Window initialization](#/document/G1957566)

steps.title: Record what brought you here
steps.body: Note the starting symptom, any battery-related message and whether the Mustang has been parked for an extended period. Normal electrical loads with the ignition off can discharge a battery during storage; that history helps explain the complaint without making replacement the automatic answer. [Discharge background](#/document/G1692355)

steps.title: Open and support the hood
steps.body: Pull the hood-release handle under the left side of the instrument panel. Slightly lift the hood, push the secondary release lever toward your left, then open the hood and support it with its strut. Confirm the support is engaged before reaching underneath. [Ford hood access](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539650&Uid=G1634784&ProcUid=G1642930&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Uncover the battery
steps.body: Remove the battery cover’s three retainers, then lift the cover away. Keep the retainers together. Leave both terminal-clamp nuts untouched while making the initial inspection. [Battery-cover access](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Inspect the connections, cables and mounting
steps.body:
Identify positive and negative from the battery markings. Move the positive cable’s protective cover aside to see its connection. [Terminal access](#/document/G1692356)

My visual checklist is simple: look around both posts and clamps for crusty deposits, a visibly displaced clamp, missing or damaged hardware, or cracks. Follow the accessible cables with your light and look for split insulation, exposed strands and damaged cable ends. Also look for case damage, unexplained wetness and a missing or displaced hold-down. These are observations to investigate, not electrical test results.

Leave the battery and hold-down installed. Removing the mounting hardware is part of battery extraction, not connection inspection or routine terminal cleaning. [Battery mounting](#/document/G1692362)

steps.title: Choose the safe branch
steps.body:
If the connections are clean, correctly positioned and show no visible concern, leave them connected and continue at step 11. Ford calls for cleaning when necessary; disconnection is not a compulsory souvenir of every inspection. [Ford connection checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

If corrosion needs cleaning and the components otherwise appear sound, continue through the service steps. Ford’s cleaning method requires removing the cables from the terminals first. [Ford battery cleaning](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

As a conservative handling rule, stop manipulation if you find suspected leakage, a damaged case, exposed conductors or unsafe connection hardware. Unexplained wetness is not automatically battery acid, but it needs assessment before cleaning or a starting check. Record the location and arrange repair assessment; extra wrench force is not a repair.

steps.title: Disconnect negative first
steps.body:
For ordinary disconnection, keep the ignition off. Loosen the negative terminal-clamp nut, lift the connection from its post and position the cable aside so it cannot return to the post. Disconnecting negative alone interrupts vehicle power on the normal single-battery installation; positive need not be removed merely to interrupt power. Cleaning both connections does require the positive cable removed next. [Negative-cable procedure](#/document/G1692356)

If equipped with one-touch-up windows, an existing motor must first be de-initialized by losing power while its glass is moving. With the engine stopped, coordinate with a helper operating the affected window so negative-cable removal interrupts power during movement. Keep everyone and everything clear of the glass. Once the cable is aside, switch the ignition off and remove the key again. Any applicable motor that was not moving at that interruption is addressed in step 10. [Existing-motor preparation](#/document/G1957566), [accidental-start precautions](#/document/G1693189)

If the vehicle has additional batteries, disconnecting only one does not isolate its electrical system. All batteries must be disconnected to remove vehicle power; have an added or unfamiliar installation assessed before proceeding. [Ford isolation warning](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Disconnect positive for cleaning
steps.body: With negative already disconnected and positioned aside, move the positive cable cover aside, loosen the positive terminal-clamp nut and lift the cable connection from its post. Position it clear of the post. Keep the disconnected ends from slipping back onto their terminals, and keep conductive tools under control. [Positive-cable procedure](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Clean and inspect the exposed connections
steps.body:
With both cables removed, use a wire brush to remove corrosion from the battery terminals and the mating surfaces of the cable clamps. Ford permits a baking-soda-and-water solution to neutralize acid. Keep your face and eyes protected throughout the work. [Ford cleaning method and precautions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Remove the loosened residue and leave the battery top clean and dry. Inspect the now-visible contact surfaces for cracks, broken hardware or other damage previously hidden by deposits. If cleaning exposes a defect, stop and obtain repair assessment before reconnecting or starting. The aim is a usable connection, not a shiny disguise for a broken clamp.

steps.title: Reconnect positive, then negative
steps.body:
After cleaning is complete and no unsafe condition remains, refit the positive cable connection to its post. Tighten its clamp nut to **44 lb.in (5 Nm)** and restore its protective cover. Refit negative last and tighten its clamp nut to **44 lb.in (5 Nm)**. These are inch-pounds, not foot-pounds. [Terminal reconnection](#/document/G1692356)

If only negative was disconnected for another supported part of this workflow, reconnect only negative; leave an untouched positive connection alone. Do not try to compensate for damaged hardware by exceeding the specified torque. [Disconnect/connect sequence](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Finish preparation for any remaining window motor
steps.body:
Skip this step if no one-touch-up window requires initialization, or if all applicable existing motors lost power while their glass was moving in step 6. Convertible models skip this branch. [Window applicability and preparation](#/document/G1957566)

For an existing motor that still needs de-initializing, keep the engine stopped and have your helper operate that window. Interrupt its movement by disconnecting negative only, using step 6. Switch the ignition off, then reconnect negative and tighten its clamp nut to **44 lb.in (5 Nm)** using step 9. Repeat for another applicable motor only if necessary. Positive stays connected during these negative-only interruptions. Complete all cable work before starting the engine. [Motor de-initialization](#/document/G1957566), [negative-only interruption and torque](#/document/G1692356)

The actual window-learning sequence follows in step 13, after the battery area is reassembled.

steps.title: Restore the covers and close the hood
steps.body:
Confirm the positive cable cover is in place. Restore any battery vent tube or shield displaced during cleaning. Refit the battery cover and its three retainers, making sure the cover is seated and retained. [Cover installation](#/document/G1692356), [Ford post-cleaning restoration](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Account for tools, the brush and your light. Remove the hood support from its catch and secure it correctly. Lower the hood and let it drop under its own weight through the final **8–12 in (20–30 cm)**. Confirm it is latched. [Ford hood closing](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539650&Uid=G1634784&ProcUid=G1642930&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

If no cable was disconnected, skip the relearning steps and continue at step 15. If an unsafe condition remains unresolved, defer starting and driving.

steps.title: Begin the post-disconnection relearn
steps.body: Proceed only after the connection work is complete, the hood is latched and no unresolved damage or suspected leak remains. Keep the parking brake applied. Select **Park (P)** for an automatic or **Neutral (N)** for a manual transmission, switch off accessories, press the brake pedal and start the vehicle. Run the engine until it reaches normal operating temperature. During warm-up, reset the clock and radio presets as needed and complete the applicable window reset in step 13. [Ford post-disconnection sequence](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Initialize the applicable one-touch windows
steps.body:
For each applicable motor prepared in steps 6 or 10, keep the door **closed** throughout initialization. Keep hands, body parts and objects completely clear of the glass: during this procedure the window closes with high force and cannot detect an obstruction. Never use a hand or object to test protection during initialization. Convertible models do not have the one-touch-up or bounce-back features covered by this branch. [Window initialization and warning](#/document/G1957566)

Start with the window fully open. Hold the window switch upward at the **second detent**—the full switch position used for one-touch operation—until the glass reaches the upper stop, then continue holding for **at least 2 seconds**. Release the switch. Hold it downward at the second detent until the glass reaches the bottom, then continue holding for **at least 2 seconds**. Cycle the glass up and down once more to establish its lower soft stop. Finally, check one-touch up and one-touch down operation. Repeat for each applicable window. [Complete learning sequence](#/document/G1957566)

If the functional check fails, do not record the reset as complete; arrange window-system assessment.

steps.title: Complete the engine relearn
steps.body:
After the engine reaches normal operating temperature, allow it to idle for **at least one minute**. Then, when ready to drive, release the parking brake and drive at least **10 mi (16 km)** to complete the idle- and fuel-trim relearn. Ford notes that incomplete learning can affect idle quality. [Ford relearning instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Some drive behavior can change while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive settings. Record persistent or concerning symptoms instead of dismissing everything as relearning. [Adaptive-strategy note](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Assess the result and choose the next job
steps.body:
If no unsafe condition remains, observe the starting behavior after reassembly. Record what you found, whether you cleaned the connections, and whether the original symptom changed. A better start is useful evidence; it does not measure battery capacity or charging performance. Ford treats battery performance as a separate inspection item. [Ford battery-performance check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

If starting remains poor, continue with [battery testing and charging](#/maintenance/battery-testing-charging). If a charged battery repeatedly goes flat, use [battery-drain diagnosis](#/maintenance/battery-drain-diagnosis). Ford requires a fully charged, assessed battery before drain testing; active low-battery warnings must be addressed first. [Drain-test prerequisites](#/document/G1692357)

watchFor.title: Wetness or damage changes the plan
watchFor.body: Treat suspected leakage, case damage, exposed conductors or unsafe clamps as a reason to stop manipulation and defer starting until assessed. Cleaning is appropriate for otherwise sound connections; it cannot repair damaged parts.

watchFor.title: A short idle is not a recharge
watchFor.body: Ford says a deeply discharged battery will not return near full charge through a short idle such as 15 minutes. Use the separate external-charging workflow. The post-disconnection idle relearn is not a charging treatment, however convenient that bullshit would be. [Charging guidance](#/document/G1692355)

watchFor.title: A protection message is not a replacement verdict
watchFor.body: The battery management system can temporarily switch off electrical features to protect battery charge. Ford says the associated notification does not, by itself, establish an electrical fault or a need for a new battery. [Ford battery-management explanation](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: Connection service is not a new-battery reset
watchFor.body: Ford requires a scan-tool Battery Monitoring System reset when installing a new battery. Reconnecting the existing battery after cleaning is a different job; do not substitute an invented reset ritual. [New-battery requirement](#/document/G1692362)

procedures.purpose: Battery-cover access, cable disconnection order, explicit reconnection order and terminal-clamp torque.
Accidental-start prevention, remote-start disabling, personal protection and relevant underhood precautions.
Existing-window-motor de-initialization, applicable initialization sequence, glass hazard and functional checks.
Distinguish connection maintenance from battery extraction and the new-battery BMS reset.
Explain storage discharge and distinguish external charging from a brief idle.
Retain the applicable post-reconnection window requirement and route repeat discharge to a properly prepared drain investigation.

stepGroups.title: Open and inspect
stepGroups.summary: Expose the connections and decide whether cleaning is appropriate.

stepGroups.title: Disconnect, clean and reconnect
stepGroups.summary: Service sound connections in the correct order and prepare applicable windows for initialization.

stepGroups.title: Reassemble and restore operation
stepGroups.summary: Secure the battery area and hood, then complete the applicable window and engine relearning steps.

stepGroups.title: Check the outcome
stepGroups.summary: Record the maintenance result and route any remaining starting or discharge concern.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion on otherwise sound terminals or clamps
diagnostics.meaning: Connection cleaning is needed, but appearance does not establish battery performance.
diagnostics.next: Disconnect negative first, then positive; wire-brush the connections, inspect the cleaned surfaces and reconnect positive before negative. Follow the applicable relearning steps afterward. [Terminal sequence](#/document/G1692356), [Ford cleaning method](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

diagnostics.finding: Suspected leakage, a damaged case, exposed conductors or unsafe hardware
diagnostics.meaning: There is a physical concern that cleaning or additional tightening may not resolve.
diagnostics.next: Stop manipulation, record the affected area and arrange assessment. Defer starting and driving verification until the concern has been assessed and corrected.

diagnostics.finding: Clean connections, but poor starting remains
diagnostics.meaning: The connection maintenance has not established the cause of the starting complaint.
diagnostics.next: Continue with battery-performance and related-system assessment before deciding on replacement. [Ford performance inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: The battery repeatedly discharges after charging
diagnostics.meaning: A separate key-off drain investigation may be appropriate.
diagnostics.next: Have the battery fully charged and assessed first, and address low-battery warnings before beginning the drain procedure. [Battery-drain prerequisites](#/document/G1692357)

diagnostics.finding: One-touch operation fails after initialization
diagnostics.meaning: The required window functional check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the door was closed and the full learning sequence was completed. If correct one-touch up and down operation is still absent, arrange window-system assessment. [Window initialization](#/document/G1957566)

verification.title: Connections restored correctly
verification.body: For connections disturbed during service, confirm positive was reconnected before negative and each terminal-clamp nut was tightened to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Confirm the positive protective cover is restored. [Reconnection requirements](#/document/G1692356)

verification.title: Battery area and hood secured
verification.body: Confirm the battery cover and all three retainers are installed, any displaced vent tube or shield is restored, all tools are removed and the hood is latched. [Battery cover](#/document/G1692356), [post-cleaning restoration](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web), [hood closure](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539650&Uid=G1634784&ProcUid=G1642930&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Applicable reconnection follow-up completed
verification.body: After disconnection, confirm the engine warm-up, at least one-minute idle and at least 10 mi (16 km) relearn drive are complete. For applicable one-touch-up windows, confirm initialization and successful one-touch up/down checks. Record an unfinished or failed follow-up explicitly. [Engine relearn](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405408&Uid=G1634800&ProcUid=G1611704&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web), [window checks](#/document/G1957566)

verification.title: The result is accurately recorded
verification.body: Record the visible findings, cleaning performed and starting observation. If damage or suspected leakage remains unresolved, record that starting verification was deferred. Keep a connection-service result separate from a battery-performance result. [Ford inspection distinction](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

notes: Applicability remains 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines. No engine-specific disassembly is needed for this operating inspection.
This article teaches inspection and initial fault sorting. Bulb, assembly, switch and module repairs remain separate procedures.
guides.title: Lighting checks: see, be seen, and catch the dead lamp
guides.summary: Check interior and exterior lights, record exactly what fails, and choose the right diagnostic path before buying parts.
guides.introduction: I work through lighting one function at a time. A Mustang looking damn good under a streetlight does not prove its brake lamps work. This check covers 2015 cars with the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines; check the equipment actually fitted to yours.
guides.why: Headlamps help you see, signaling lamps tell others what you intend to do, and cabin lights make the interior usable. A dark headlamp can involve its bulb, wiring, ballast—the HID lamp’s operating electronics—or body control module. I want a useful fault description before the parts cannon starts firing. [Headlamp diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)

when.summary: Check interior and exterior light operation monthly; include hazard-warning and horn operation in the recommended service inspection.

prepare.title: A safe place and a helper
prepare.detail: Choose a level parking spot away from traffic, secure the car against movement, and arrange a helper to operate controls while you observe. For brake and reversing lamps, keep a driver at the controls and the observer outside the vehicle’s path.

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Before walking around the car, disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup in the central display. An unexpected remote start can injure someone working around the vehicle. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Simple checking supplies
prepare.detail: Bring a phone or notepad for a lamp checklist and fault notes. The operating check needs no dismantling or electrical test equipment. Use the car’s marked controls; include optional lamps only where fitted.

steps.title: Set up the check
steps.body: Keep the engine off for the walkaround. Set the parking brake and disable remote start before beginning. Have the helper tell you before changing a control or selecting a gear; nobody should be surprised by vehicle movement. Ford requires remote start to be disabled for inspections around the vehicle. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Look before switching anything on
steps.body: Walk around the car and note damaged lamp housings or lenses. Look at the headlamp switch and steering-column lighting stalk for visible damage without removing trim. Record any recent lighting or body repair that might help explain a fault. Ford’s preliminary checks specifically include damage and previous repairs. [Headlamp pre-checks](#/document/G1694228) · [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Check the position and rear lighting
steps.body: Select the parking-lamp function using the marked control. Walk around and check the corresponding front position lamps, rear tail lamps, side markers and license-plate lighting where fitted. Record each location as working, faulty or not checked. This is a practical walkaround checklist for Ford’s requirement to check all exterior lights. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Select low beams directly
steps.body: Turn the ignition on and select HEADLAMPS ON rather than relying on an automatic-light setting. Observe both low beams and record whether the left, right or both fail. This is Ford’s starting operating check for an inoperative low beam. Also check any other fitted exterior lighting through its normal control; record the selected mode if operation is uncertain. [Low-beam operating check](#/document/G1694228)

steps.title: Separate high beams from flash-to-pass
steps.body: With the ignition on and HEADLAMPS selected, move the lighting stalk to high beam and then back to low beam, observing both sides in each position. Separately operate the stalk’s flash-to-pass function and release it. Record whether ordinary high beams work when flash-to-pass does not; Ford diagnoses those symptoms through different paths. A dashboard indication alone does not complete the exterior observation. [High-beam and flash-to-pass checks](#/document/G1694228)

steps.title: Check each turn direction, then the hazards
steps.body: Operate the left turn signal and observe the fitted front, rear and side signaling lamps. Cancel it, repeat on the right, then operate the hazard switch and check the signaling lamps around the car. Note a dark lamp, incomplete illuminated area or intermittent behavior without assuming the bulb is responsible. Switch the hazards off afterward. Ford includes all exterior lighting and hazard-system operation in its checks. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Observe the brake lamps
steps.body: With the car secured and the helper in the driver’s seat, have them press and release the brake pedal. Observe the rear stop lamps, including the high-mounted lamp, and confirm that each responds to the pedal. Check the change in illumination rather than merely noticing that the tail lamps are already lit. Record any lamp that fails to illuminate or remains on after release. This observation forms part of the all-exterior-lights check. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Check reversing lamps without standing behind the car
steps.body: Keep the engine off. The driver should remain seated, hold the foot brake, keep the parking brake applied and select reverse using the vehicle’s normal controls with the ignition state needed for lamp operation. Observe from beside the vehicle, outside its travel path. Confirm the reversing lamps illuminate and then go out when reverse is deselected. Return the transmission to its normal secured parking state before anyone leaves the controls. If you cannot establish these conditions safely, mark the reversing lamps untested and arrange that check separately. [All exterior lights](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Work through the interior
steps.body: Operate the fitted cabin and reading lights individually. Check door-operated courtesy lighting and any fitted luggage-compartment, glovebox or vanity lighting by opening the relevant door or cover. Include instrument and control illumination through the normal lighting controls. Record the function and control setting for anything that stays dark or will not switch off. This is a practical checklist for Ford’s all-interior-lights check; safety warning lamps have their own inspection routine. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Include the horn during a service inspection
steps.body: If you are doing the wider service inspection, briefly operate the horn where it will not create a hazard or disturb someone nearby. Record whether it sounds. Ford lists horn operation alongside the hazard-warning system in its recommended multipoint inspection. [Ford service inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Turn a vague complaint into a useful finding
steps.body: Write down the side, exact lamp function, selected control position and whether the failure is constant or intermittent. For example: “Right low beam dark with ignition on and HEADLAMPS selected; left low beam works.” Include which related functions still work. If the problem disappears, record that too: Ford’s diagnostic replacement decisions assume the named fault is present during testing. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Choose diagnosis before choosing parts
steps.body: Use the findings below to select the matching headlamp diagnostic branch. Keep the inspection at the controls and visible lamps: do not apply power or ground to lamp or module circuits as an improvised test, because a direct connection can damage components. Several failures together deserve investigation for a common supply, ground or connection fault. Bulb replacement, assembly removal and aim adjustment are separate jobs; none is a prerequisite for this operating check. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185) · [Headlamp diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)

steps.title: Repeat the questionable function and close up
steps.body: Repeat any failed or uncertain check under the same control conditions and update the record. After any repair, repeat the affected function and its related modes to confirm normal operation. Return the lighting controls to the intended setting, switch the ignition off, and close the doors, lamp covers and luggage compartment opened for inspection. No component reassembly is required for this walkaround. [Post-repair operating checks](#/document/G1694228)

watchFor.title: Several failures at once
watchFor.body: A shared electrical fault can affect several functions. Check for a common cause before buying several lamps; that particular shopping trip can become a pain in the ass. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

watchFor.title: A working lamp with a misplaced beam
watchFor.body: Illumination does not establish correct aim. Ford’s aim procedure requires level ground, correct tire inflation, normal loading, clean working headlamps and a measured screen setup. Horizontal aim is not adjustable. Treat suspected misalignment as a separate check. [Headlamp aim](#/document/G1694148)

watchFor.title: Intermittent success
watchFor.body: A lamp working today does not explain yesterday’s failure. Preserve the conditions and symptoms in your notes; do not replace a component using a fault-present diagnostic decision while the fault is absent. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

procedures.purpose: Select the diagnostic branch matching the observed headlamp symptom and vehicle market.
Separate bulb-service procedure after diagnosis identifies that repair.
Separate assembly-service procedure when diagnosis requires assembly access or replacement.
Separate measured headlamp-aim check and adjustment.

stepGroups.title: Set up and inspect
stepGroups.summary: Secure the car and look for visible damage.

stepGroups.title: Check the functions
stepGroups.summary: Observe exterior lights, interior lights and the service-inspection horn check.

stepGroups.title: Record, route and finish
stepGroups.summary: Describe faults precisely, choose the next diagnostic action and restore the controls.

diagnostics.finding: One or both low beams fail with HEADLAMPS ON.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include fuses, wiring, connections, bulb, ballast, assembly or body control module; darkness alone does not identify the failed part. [Low-beam diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Record one-side versus both-side failure. Use Pinpoint Test A for vehicles except China, or Test B for China-market vehicles. Have circuit diagnosis completed before ordering a bulb or ballast. [Low-beam diagnostic branches](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: High beams fail.
diagnostics.meaning: The next diagnostic decision depends on whether low beams work and whether one or both high beams fail. [High-beam diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: If low beams also fail, address their diagnostic branch first. If low beams work, use Test C; both-high-beam failure leads first to checking the stalk input with a suitable diagnostic scan tool. [Test C](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: Ordinary high beams work, but flash-to-pass does not.
diagnostics.meaning: The flash-to-pass input needs separate investigation; successful ordinary high beams are useful evidence. [Flash-to-pass diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Use Test G, which checks the steering-column control module’s recorded flash-to-pass switch input before further module diagnosis. [Test G](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: A headlamp remains on when the corresponding function is deselected.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford treats continuously illuminated low or high beams as distinct symptoms involving control inputs, wiring or modules. [Continuous-illumination diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Record the ignition and switch positions and which side remains on. Low beams use Test D except China or Test E for China; high beams use Test F. [Symptom routes](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: A diagnostic report shows U1000:00 or U3000:49.
diagnostics.meaning: U1000:00 indicates temporary output protection after excessive current; U3000:49 indicates an output has been permanently disabled. The body control module is the BCM. [BCM fault descriptions](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Correct the underlying excessive-current fault and address other related codes first. For U1000:00, clear codes and successfully repeat the self-test after repair to restore the output. U3000:49 requires the VIN-specific guided BCM routine; correct the cause before installing a replacement module. [BCM recovery requirements](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: A signaling, stop, reversing or interior lamp fails.
diagnostics.meaning: The operating check identifies the failed function; the supplied headlamp diagnostic chart does not establish the cause for these other lamps.
diagnostics.next: Keep the side, function and control-condition notes and arrange diagnosis for that specific lighting circuit. Avoid treating a headlamp test or replacement procedure as interchangeable with another lamp.

verification.title: Every fitted function has a result
verification.body: Confirm your record covers exterior position lighting, low and high beams, flash-to-pass, turn signals, hazards, stop lamps, reversing lamps, other fitted exterior lights and interior lighting. Mark any untested item explicitly; it is not a pass. [Ford all-lamp check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

verification.title: The original symptom is checked after repair
verification.body: Repeat the original control sequence and confirm the affected lamp now responds correctly. Complete any required BCM code clearing and self-test after correcting an output-protection fault. [Repair verification](#/document/G1694228)

verification.title: Headlamp service includes aim afterward
verification.body: If subsequent work removes a headlamp assembly or replaces its bulb using these Ford procedures, headlamp adjustment is part of completing that repair. A lamp lighting up is only the operating check. [Assembly completion](#/document/G1694118) · [Bulb completion](#/document/G1694119)

notes: Applicability is limited to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Rain-sensitive checks apply only when equipped.
This stationary care check does not certify every feature in the system overview, including speed-dependent behavior. [System features](#/document/G1694644)
Routine blade care does not require removing the motor or linkage. Use the motor procedure only after diagnosis establishes that repair is needed. [Motor repair](#/document/G1694635)
guides.title: Washers and wipers: check fluid, spray and blades
guides.summary: Check and top up washer fluid, inspect and clean the blades, observe spray and wiping, and replace blades when cleaning does not solve the problem.
guides.introduction: I start with fluid, glass and rubber before giving the expensive bits a suspicious look. A damn bug stuck to a blade does not justify a new motor. This guide covers routine washer and wiper care for the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, including stationary rain-sensitive checks when equipped. Ford starts blade-performance diagnosis with cleaning and a retest. Pump, motor, linkage, sensor and arm-alignment repairs remain separate jobs. [Blade-performance diagnosis](#/document/G1694646)
guides.why: Spray delivery and wipe quality need separate observations. Fluid reaching the glass does not establish that the blades clean it properly; streaking does not identify a failed motor. Ford’s diagnosis considers the fluid path, controls, glass and blade condition. Keeping those findings separate makes parts-guessing a less expensive hobby. [Washer and wiper diagnosis](#/document/G1694646)

when.summary: Check washer-fluid level monthly. Check spray and wiper operation every six months; clean or replace blades as needed.

prepare.title: Washer fluid suitable for the weather
prepare.detail: Use fluid meeting Ford specification WSS-M14P19-A; the reservoir procedure lists Motorcraft Premium Windshield Wash Concentrate with Bitterant ZC-32-B2. Prepare concentrate according to its container instructions. [Fluid specification](#/document/G1694630) Below 40°F (5°C), use washer fluid with antifreeze protection: freezing fluid can impair visibility and increase accident risk. Follow local restrictions on methanol; any alternative must protect against freezing without damaging paint, blades or the washer system. [Ford washer-fluid guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539658&Uid=G1634797&ProcUid=G1547160&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Cleaning and test supplies
prepare.detail: Gather clean, lint-free cloths, a soft sponge or cloth, water for wet-glass checks, blade-cleaning washer fluid such as Motorcraft ZC-32M20-EG or equivalent, and glass cleaner such as Motorcraft ZC-23 or equivalent. Have isopropyl alcohol swabs available for the additional rain-sensor-area cleaning check. [Cleaning materials and wet-glass checks](#/document/G1694646)

prepare.title: Access and a helper
prepare.detail: The work takes place at the windshield and the underhood washer filler. Use the engine-specific identification in step 2. Routine filling uses the filler from above; the splash-shield removal in the reservoir procedure is for reservoir repair. A helper is useful for the pump-listening observation near the vehicle’s right front. [Filler and reservoir access](#/document/G1694630) [Pump listening check](#/document/G1694646)

prepare.title: Personal and chemical protection
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and read the safety information for the fluid and cleaners. Keep solvents away from flames, sparks and other ignition sources because they can ignite or explode and cause serious injury. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Replacement blades, if needed
prepare.detail: Ford lists WW-2201-PF for the driver side and WW-2001-PF for the passenger side across these three engines. Confirm the replacement’s fit for the actual vehicle and follow its attachment instructions. [Ford blade listings](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517147&Uid=G1634835&ProcUid=G1642992&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Prevent unexpected operation
steps.body:
If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the car. Switch the ignition off and remove the key during inspection, filling, cleaning and blade handling so another person cannot start the vehicle. Restore ignition power only for the operating observations, with everyone clear of the blades. [Unexpected-start precautions](#/document/G1693189)

Before underhood work, inspect the cooling fans with the ignition off for visible cracks, damage or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; it can come apart during operation and cause serious injury. Fans can also run with the ignition off. Keep clear and have them disabled before work that requires being nearby. [Cooling-fan precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Find the washer filler for your engine
steps.body:
Open the hood and identify the washer reservoir using the overview for the engine actually fitted. Each of these illustrations labels it G, toward the front of the engine compartment, ahead of the electrical box marked H.

For the 2.3L EcoBoost, use G in the [2.3L underhood overview](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539651&Uid=G1642504&ProcUid=G1642531&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web).

For the 3.7L, use G in the [3.7L underhood overview](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539651&Uid=G1634788&ProcUid=G1642507&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web).

For the 5.0L, use G in the [5.0L underhood overview](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539651&Uid=G1634789&ProcUid=G1642508&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web).

Use the filler from above. Leave the splash shield, hoses, pump connection and reservoir fasteners installed for this care task. Their removal belongs to reservoir repair. [Reservoir procedure](#/document/G1694630)

steps.title: Check the supply and top up if low
steps.body:
With the ignition off, open the identified washer cap and look into the filler to assess the visible fluid supply. Ford directs filling the reservoir when the level is low. Add the correctly prepared washer fluid slowly, pausing to let it settle and to observe the rising level. As fluid approaches the filler opening, use small additions and stop before it overflows. This ordinary top-up does not require a measured quantity or an assumed MAX mark. Refit the cap securely and wipe away any spilled fluid. [Ford washer-fluid check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539658&Uid=G1634797&ProcUid=G1547160&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Fill an empty reservoir before operating the washer pump; running it before filling can cause premature failure. If fluid escapes as you add it or the reservoir will not retain a supply, stop the washer test and arrange leak diagnosis. You can still use externally applied water for the blade checks. [Pump protection](#/document/G1694630) [Leak inspection](#/document/G1693185)

If fluid repeatedly disappears without enough washer use to explain it, look over accessible hoses for wetness, leaks, kinks or damage. Record what you actually see. Unexplained loss deserves investigation even when no leak is visible. [Preliminary hose inspection](#/document/G1693185) [Washer hose checks](#/document/G1694646)

steps.title: Inspect the rubber and windshield
steps.body:
Keep the ignition off. Inspect both blades for dirt, ice, debris and visible damage. Gently run your fingertips along each rubber wiping edge to feel for roughness. Note which blade and which part of the glass show the complaint. [Ford blade inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405324&Uid=G1634804&ProcUid=G1448670&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Inspect the windshield for contamination and visible damage, including cracks or pits. Record glass damage separately so a missed patch does not automatically become a shopping list for rubber. [Blade and glass inspection](#/document/G1694646)

steps.title: Clean before condemning the blades
steps.body:
With the ignition off, wipe the suspect blades with a clean, lint-free cloth moistened with windshield washer fluid, Motorcraft ZC-32M20-EG or equivalent. Clean the affected glass with a separate clean, lint-free cloth and glass cleaner, Motorcraft ZC-23 or equivalent. Ford calls for cleaning and retesting before replacing blades for poor cleaning, streaking or chatter. [Clean-before-replacement check](#/document/G1694646)

For routine blade cleaning, water or washer fluid applied with a soft sponge or cloth is also supported. Return any lifted blades gently to the glass before operating them. [Ford blade care](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405324&Uid=G1634804&ProcUid=G1448670&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Set up conventional intermittent operation
steps.body:
Establish whether the car has rain-sensitive wipers. If equipped, note your current preference. With everyone clear of the blades, turn the ignition on and use the steering-wheel controls to access vehicle settings in the message center. Disable the rain-sensitive feature for the conventional intermittent check; this activates conventional intermittent operation. [Intermittent setup, Test E](#/document/G1694646)

There are six intermittent/sensitivity selections. Automatic response gets its own observation in step 9. [Available functions](#/document/G1694644)

steps.title: Check wiping on wet glass and watch the parked position
steps.body:
Apply water to the windshield and keep it wet during the checks. With hands and supplies clear and the ignition on, select low speed. Watch each blade’s cleared area for streaks, missed patches and chatter—the skipping or juddering across the glass. Select off after observing it. Check high speed, mist and each conventional intermittent selection, recording which mode fails or behaves incorrectly. These are stationary observations; no exact intermittent delay is being measured. [Wet-glass and speed checks](#/document/G1694646) [Wiper functions](#/document/G1694644)

Select off and let the blades finish parking. Compare their resting positions with the installation marks on the windshield: the blades should sit inside those marks. If you cannot identify the marks, record alignment as unchecked rather than inventing a distance from the cowl. Blades outside the marks need parking/alignment diagnosis. [Windshield alignment reference](#/document/G1694632) [Parking diagnosis](#/document/G1694646)

steps.title: Observe spray delivery and pump sound
steps.body:
Proceed with the washer check after establishing fluid supply in step 3. In below-freezing conditions, confirm that the fluid is suitable for the temperature. If unsuitable fluid is present, Ford directs warming the vehicle to room temperature, then draining and refilling with the correct fluid as separate corrective work. Do not run the pump to empty the reservoir. [Cold-weather diagnosis](#/document/G1694646) [Pump protection](#/document/G1694630)

With the ignition on and everyone clear of the blades, momentarily activate the wash function using the wiper/washer switch. Observe whether each jet delivers fluid to the windshield. Record weak, absent or one-sided delivery and any visible escaping fluid. Release the command and observe whether washing stops. [Washer checks, Tests H and I](#/document/G1694646)

If spray is absent, have a helper briefly activate the washer while you listen near the vehicle’s right front. Switch the ignition off before examining accessible hoses for kinks, damage or leaks. An audible pump establishes that it activates audibly; it does not establish satisfactory delivery or identify the failed part. Route continuing faults to Test H. [Pump and hose checks H4–H8](#/document/G1694646) [Leak inspection](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Observe rain-sensitive response, if equipped
steps.body:
With the ignition off, inspect the windshield near the rain sensor for cracks, pits or other visible damage. From outside, look through the glass at the sensor’s contact area. It should appear black, without bubbles, air pockets or contamination. Keep the sensor and its clips attached during this care check; disturbing the assembly can damage or contaminate its gel lens. [Sensor-area inspection F5/F10](#/document/G1694646)

If streaking remains across the sensor area, clean the glass with glass cleaner and wipe the entire length of the blades with isopropyl alcohol swabs. Keep the ignition off while cleaning. Clear everyone away, turn the ignition on and repeat the low-speed check while applying water, watching the sensor area in particular. [Sensor-area cleaning F6–F7](#/document/G1694646)

Enable rain-sensitive operation in the message center. Select auto/intermittent setting 5—the setting Ford identifies as most sensitive to moisture in Test F8—and apply water to the windshield above the rain sensor. Observe whether wiping starts, then select off. Record no response, erratic response or visible glass/contact-area defects for Test F diagnosis. This observation does not complete the full sensor diagnostic test. [Feature setting and water response F3/F8](#/document/G1694646)

steps.title: Replace affected blades if cleaning did not help
steps.body:
If cleaning restores satisfactory wiping, keep the blades in service. If poor cleaning, streaking or chatter remains, Ford directs replacing the affected blade or blades. [Replacement decision, Test J](#/document/G1694646)
