Switch the ignition off. For the original button-lock attachment, lift the blade and arm away from the glass, press the locking buttons together, then rotate and remove the blade. Support the arm while the blade is detached so it cannot fall against the glass. Attach the correct new blade to the arm and snap it into place. Check that it is secure, then lower it gently onto the windshield. Repeat on the other side if needed. If the replacement has a different adapter, follow its attachment instructions and confirm vehicle fit. [Ford blade-changing instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405325&Uid=G1660533&ProcUid=G1660534&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Retest, restore your settings and close up
steps.body:
Repeat the wet-glass check after blade replacement. Confirm whether both blades clear their areas and whether the original streaking or chatter has disappeared. If a spray fault prompted the work, repeat a brief washer check with fluid in the reservoir and record the result for each jet. [Blade retest and washer checks](#/document/G1694646) [Pump prerequisite](#/document/G1694630)

Restore your intended rain-sensitive preference if you changed it. Select the wiper switch off, let the blades park and compare their positions with the windshield marks again. Switch the ignition off before final handling. [Feature settings](#/document/G1694646) [Parking reference](#/document/G1694632)

Check that the washer cap is secure, remove the cleaning supplies and close the hood. Record fluid top-up, blade condition, spray delivery and the modes observed. Give every remaining fault or unchecked item a next action. I want a useful checklist; a fictional pass is bullshit.

watchFor.title: Cold-weather fluid choice
watchFor.body: Below 40°F (5°C), washer fluid needs antifreeze protection. Fluid freezing on the windshield can impair vision and increase accident risk. [Ford cold-weather warning](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539658&Uid=G1634797&ProcUid=G1547160&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: An empty reservoir
watchFor.body: Fill before activating the washer pump. Stop repeated activation when delivery is absent; operating the pump before filling can cause premature failure. [Pump protection](#/document/G1694630)

watchFor.title: Wipers that ignore the off setting
watchFor.body: Keep hands clear and stop blade handling if wiping continues with the switch off. Test D covers continuous wiping, including operation with the ignition off; Test I covers a washer that stays on. [Continuous-operation diagnosis](#/document/G1694646)

watchFor.title: Rain-sensor bubbles or damage
watchFor.body: Record the defect and arrange diagnosis without releasing the sensor clips. Its gel lens can be damaged or contaminated during disturbance. [Rain-sensor handling](#/document/G1694646)

watchFor.title: A symptom that disappears during the check
watchFor.body: Record the conditions under which it occurred. Ford’s component-replacement decisions generally require the named fault to be present during testing; an intermittent complaint does not justify buying a module on suspicion. [Diagnostic assumptions](#/document/G1693185)

procedures.purpose: Identify the wiper and washer functions relevant to stationary operating observations.
Support cleaning, observable operating checks and routing persistent faults to the appropriate pinpoint test.
Support filler access, the fluid specification and pump protection; reservoir removal remains separate.
Provide the windshield-mark reference for observing parked blade alignment.
Route diagnosed motor replacement to its separate repair procedure.

stepGroups.title: Set up and check the fluid
stepGroups.summary: Prevent unexpected operation, find the correct filler and top up the supply.

stepGroups.title: Inspect, clean and check wiping
stepGroups.summary: Assess rubber and glass, conventional modes and parked position.

stepGroups.title: Observe spray and automatic response
stepGroups.summary: Check washer delivery and rain-sensitive operation when equipped.

stepGroups.title: Replace affected blades and finish
stepGroups.summary: Secure replacement blades, retest and restore your settings.

diagnostics.finding: Cleaning restores satisfactory wiping.
diagnostics.meaning: The observed performance complaint was caused by contamination on the blades or glass.
diagnostics.next: Keep the blades in service and finish the remaining observations. [Test J](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: Poor cleaning, streaks or chatter remain after cleaning.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford’s blade-performance check directs replacement of the affected blades.
diagnostics.next: Use step 10 and retest on wet glass. If the complaint remains, have blade fit and glass condition reassessed. [Test J](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: Fluid repeatedly disappears without a visible leak.
diagnostics.meaning: The loss is unexplained; it does not establish a visible defect or identify a failed component.
diagnostics.next: Record washer use and the recurring loss, inspect accessible hoses and arrange fluid-path diagnosis if it continues. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1693185) [Washer Test H](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: An accessible hose is visibly leaking, kinked or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: There is an observed fluid-path defect requiring attention.
diagnostics.next: Record its location and arrange the appropriate hose repair and delivery retest. [Hose inspection](#/document/G1693185) [Test H5](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: Spray is weak, absent or one-sided while the pump is audible.
diagnostics.meaning: The pump activates audibly, but delivery remains faulty.
diagnostics.next: Check temperature suitability and accessible hose condition, then arrange Test H diagnosis. A limited visual check does not establish that the entire fluid path is sound. [Test H](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: No spray and no audible pump operation.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch input, electrical supply, ground or pump requires targeted testing.
diagnostics.next: Arrange Test H diagnosis and report the silent-pump observation. [Test H](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: All modes fail, a particular mode fails, or wiping continues with the switch off.
diagnostics.meaning: These operating faults need diagnosis beyond blade cleaning.
diagnostics.next: Route all modes dead to Test A, low/intermittent failure to B, high-speed failure to C, continuous wiping to D, and incorrect conventional intermittent behavior to E. [Symptom chart](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: Rain-sensitive wiping is absent or erratic after enabling the feature.
diagnostics.meaning: Automatic operation needs further diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Arrange Test F, reporting the setting-5 water response, wipe quality and any visible glass or sensor-contact defects. [Test F](#/document/G1694646)

diagnostics.finding: Parked blades sit outside the windshield installation marks.
diagnostics.meaning: Parking or arm alignment needs attention.
diagnostics.next: Arrange Test G and the appropriate arm-alignment repair. Leave the arms on their shafts during routine blade care. [Parking diagnosis](#/document/G1694646) [Arm alignment](#/document/G1694632)

diagnostics.finding: The washer continues after releasing the wash command.
diagnostics.meaning: The washer has a continuous-operation fault.
diagnostics.next: Stop repeated spray checks and arrange Test I diagnosis. [Test I](#/document/G1694646)

verification.title: Fluid supply checked and cap secured
verification.body: Confirm that the correct reservoir was checked, low fluid was topped up with the appropriate product, and the cap is secure. Record unexplained loss or observed leakage separately from spray performance. [Ford fluid check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539658&Uid=G1634797&ProcUid=G1547160&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Leak inspection](#/document/G1693185)

verification.title: Blades attached and wipe quality retested
verification.body: Any replacement blade is snapped securely onto its arm and returned to the glass. On wet glass, record whether both blades clear their areas and whether the original streaking or chatter has disappeared. [Blade attachment](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1405325&Uid=G1660533&ProcUid=G1660534&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Blade retest](#/document/G1694646)

verification.title: Delivery, modes and final settings recorded
verification.body: Record delivery from each jet, conventional modes tested and rain-sensitive response when equipped. Confirm that washing stops after release and the blades park inside the windshield marks after selecting off. Restore the intended rain-sensitive preference and assign next actions to remaining concerns. [Operating checks](#/document/G1694646) [Parking marks](#/document/G1694632)

notes: Applies to the original 2015 Mustang scope with 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines; this inspection has no engine-specific branch.
Door removal, alignment adjustment, convertible roof-seal service and corrosion-treatment application are separate jobs.

For protection concerns after body work, see [corrosion protection](#/maintenance/corrosion-protection). For abnormal latch or door operation, see [hinges, latches and locks](#/maintenance/latches-locks).
guides.title: Body drains and weather seals: an accessible condition inspection
guides.summary: Inspect exposed door weatherstrips and door fit, check confirmed accessible drains, and record anything needing identification or further service.
guides.introduction: I start with observation before buying parts: where is the debris, what does the seal look like, and does the door close normally? A damp carpet is a clue, not a damn shopping list. This guide covers a ground-level inspection of exposed areas and removal of loose debris at confirmed drain mouths. Concealed passages, seal replacement, lubrication and alignment repairs are separate work. Ford calls for drain-obstruction and weatherstrip-wear checks, with cleaning or lubrication when necessary. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.why: Door drains let moisture escape; Ford specifically requires them to remain clear to prevent moisture buildup. Weatherstrips deserve their own condition check, while the way the window glass engages the seal belongs to the glass-fit assessment. Keeping those observations separate helps avoid treating every water concern with another handful of rubber parts. [Door drainage](#/document/G1687508), [coupe glass engagement](#/document/G1697266), [convertible glass engagement](#/document/G1725016)

when.summary: Every six months: check body and door drains for obstruction and door weatherstrips for wear; clean or lubricate as appropriate.
notes: Use the correct care product and application instructions for the specific seal.

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Switch the ignition off and remove the key. If remote start is equipped, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before inspecting around the car. An unexpected start can seriously injure someone working nearby. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Gather simple inspection aids
prepare.detail: Have a light and a way to record findings; a small mirror may help you see an exposed lower edge without reaching underneath. These are observation aids, not tools for probing drain passages. Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the car, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. [Personal protection](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Keep access simple
prepare.detail: Use the open doors to inspect exposed edges and seals, with the car remaining on the ground. Leave door wiring, check arms, hinges and trim attached. Ford’s front-door removal procedure concerns removing the complete assembly; its disassembly steps are not prerequisites for this visible check. [Front door](#/document/G1810502)

prepare.title: Keep care products conditional
prepare.detail: No chemical is needed for the visual inspection. If later care calls for a product, first confirm that Ford approves it for the particular seal and obtain its application instructions. Read the product safety information and use the protection it requires; incorrect chemical handling can cause serious injury. [Ford chemical guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259), [chemical precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Open one door and survey the exposed area
steps.body:
Open one front door. Illuminate its accessible lower edge and the exposed body opening, then look for loose debris, visible damage and material covering an opening. Work on one side at a time and describe locations as front, rear, upper or lower so your notes remain useful.

An exposed hole is not automatically a drain. If the intended outlets have not been confirmed for this car, record “drain identification pending” and continue with the seal inspection. Have those outlets identified before attempting drain cleaning. Ford requires obstruction checks, but its generic corrosion-treatment illustrations are not a Mustang drain locator. [Ford drain checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259), [corrosion reference views](#/document/G1687508)

steps.title: Check confirmed accessible drain mouths
steps.body:
Where an opening has been positively identified as a drain and is directly visible and reachable, inspect its mouth for debris or product bridging the opening. Remove only loose surface debris that comes away without scraping the finish, enlarging the opening or pushing material inward. Recheck the mouth afterward. This is a conservative surface-cleaning limit for Ford’s instruction to clean obstructed drains when necessary. [Ford drain checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

Stop if debris resists removal, disappears into a concealed passage or requires dismantling to reach. Leave coatings out of the opening: Ford requires door drain holes to stay clear so moisture does not accumulate inside. [Door drain protection](#/document/G1687508)

steps.title: Follow each exposed weatherstrip
steps.body:
Weatherstrip is the flexible seal around the opening or glass contact area. Follow each accessible section along its visible length without pulling it out of its mounting. As a practical way to carry out Ford’s wear check, look for splits, worn-through patches, loose sections, folds and obvious displacement. Record the side and exact area of each finding. [Ford weatherstrip checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

Comparing the corresponding area on the other side can help you describe an unusual appearance; it does not establish a factory fit specification. I want a useful observation here, before parts-guessing becomes a hobby.

steps.title: Observe closure and visible fit
steps.body:
Move your hands, light and other inspection items clear, then carefully close the door. Observe whether an exposed seal becomes folded or trapped, whether the door closes normally, and whether door or glass fit looks obviously uneven. Record the location; do not loosen the striker or hinges or force the door against abnormal contact. Ford’s alignment assessment checks door-to-body dimensions and front-window alignment together. [Front door alignment](#/document/G1693219)

Route glass-contact concerns by body style. A coupe uses the coupe window-glass procedure. On a convertible being assessed for wind noise or water entry, Ford requires the rear quarter-window alignment to be checked before front-window adjustment. Neither route is an extra adjustment step for this inspection. [Coupe glass](#/document/G1697266), [convertible glass](#/document/G1725016)

steps.title: Decide whether separate seal care is needed
steps.body:
Record a torn, worn or displaced seal for condition or fit assessment. Lubrication is a separate decision, not a substitute for addressing that finding. Ford calls for weatherstrip lubrication only when necessary and advises against unapproved maintenance chemicals. If lubrication is indicated, obtain the approved product and application instructions for that seal before applying anything. [Ford seal care and chemical guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

The cavity wax, undercoating and metal-preparation wipes in Ford’s corrosion procedure serve metal protection. That procedure does not authorize them as rubber-seal care products. [Corrosion prevention](#/document/G1687508)

steps.title: Repeat, close up and record the result
steps.body:
Repeat the inspection on the other side. Remove inspection items and collected debris, check that you have not left a seal folded or trapped, and close both doors normally. No components were removed during this check, so there is no hardware or trim to reinstall.

For each drain location, record one result: visibly clear, loose debris removed, still obstructed, inaccessible or identification pending. For each exposed seal, record either no visible defect or the defect and location. A visibly open drain mouth does not prove that its concealed passage is clear. Keep unchecked locations and pending care separate from the inspection actually performed. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

If dampness continues, make a simple observation log: where moisture first becomes visible and whether it follows rain or washing. Use that record to request water-path diagnosis before choosing replacement seals.

watchFor.title: Coating covering an outlet
watchFor.body: Record the location and arrange correction without enlarging the opening. Door corrosion protection must preserve clear drains to prevent moisture buildup. [Door drain protection](#/document/G1687508)

watchFor.title: Poor fit beside a damaged seal
watchFor.body: Record both conditions together. Door dimensions and glass alignment belong in the follow-up assessment before deciding which component needs attention. [Front door alignment](#/document/G1693219)

watchFor.title: A door that meets abnormal resistance
watchFor.body: Stop the closure check instead of forcing it shut. Keep hands clear and arrange a fit assessment if the door cannot close normally. [Door-fit assessment](#/document/G1693219)

procedures.purpose: Distinguish complete door removal from access for this exposed-area inspection.
Preserve clear door drains and distinguish corrosion products from seal care.
Route abnormal door fit to a separate alignment assessment.
Route coupe glass-contact concerns to the correct procedure.
Route convertible glass-contact concerns, retaining the quarter-window prerequisite for leak or wind-noise diagnosis.

stepGroups.title: Survey accessible drainage
stepGroups.summary: Establish the visible inspection area and check only confirmed outlets.

stepGroups.title: Inspect seals and fit
stepGroups.summary: Record visible wear, observe closure and decide what needs separate care.

stepGroups.title: Finish and record
stepGroups.summary: Repeat on the other side and distinguish findings from completed cleaning.

diagnostics.finding: An opening cannot be confirmed as a drain.
diagnostics.meaning: Its drainage function has not been established, so cleaning it would be guesswork.
diagnostics.next: Record the location and have the intended drain openings identified for this Mustang before cleaning. Continue the independent weatherstrip check. Ford’s corrosion illustrations are generic reference views. [Corrosion prevention](#/document/G1687508)

diagnostics.finding: Loose debris comes away and a confirmed drain mouth is visibly open.
diagnostics.meaning: The accessible surface obstruction has been removed; concealed flow remains unverified.
diagnostics.next: Record the work performed. Seek further diagnosis if moisture concerns continue. [Ford drain checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: A confirmed outlet remains obstructed.
diagnostics.meaning: Cleaning is incomplete at that location.
diagnostics.next: Arrange cleaning using the correct vehicle-specific access method rather than probing or dismantling by guesswork. Door outlets must remain clear to prevent moisture accumulation. [Door drainage](#/document/G1687508)

diagnostics.finding: A weatherstrip is split, worn through, loose or displaced.
diagnostics.meaning: A visible condition concern has been found; lubrication alone does not assess its fit or damage.
diagnostics.next: Record the location for seal assessment, adding a door-fit assessment if closure or alignment also looks abnormal. [Ford weatherstrip checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259), [door alignment](#/document/G1693219)

diagnostics.finding: Exposed seals appear intact, but glass contact looks uneven or water entry continues.
diagnostics.meaning: The visual seal check has not identified the cause.
diagnostics.next: Request diagnosis using the correct body-style route. For convertible wind-noise or water-leak concerns, rear quarter-window alignment must be checked before front-glass adjustment. [Coupe glass](#/document/G1697266), [convertible glass](#/document/G1725016)

verification.title: Recheck every outlet touched
verification.body: Confirm that no loosened debris or product remains across a confirmed drain mouth. Retain a separate entry for any outlet still blocked or not inspected. [Door drain requirement](#/document/G1687508)

verification.title: Check the final seal and door condition
verification.body: Confirm that inspection items are removed, exposed seals have not been left folded or trapped, and both doors close normally. Route an abnormal fit finding to the door-alignment assessment. [Front door alignment](#/document/G1693219)

verification.title: Record exactly what was completed
verification.body: Separate the exposed-seal inspection, confirmed drain-mouth checks and loose-debris removal from drain identification, concealed cleaning or lubrication still needed. Do not record the entire body-drain system as clear from this visual pass. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

notes: Scope remains the 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. This guide covers operation checks, installed door-latch lubrication and the accessible binding exterior key-cylinder lubrication branch.
A lubrication procedure does not mean the complete latch assembly needs replacement. Replacement follows the applicable diagnostic result. [Latch diagnosis](#/document/G1695898)
guides.title: Hinges, latches and locks: check operation, then lubricate the right place
guides.summary: Check door movement, handle release and locking operation, then use the correct lubrication sequence for a sticky latch or accessible binding key cylinder.
guides.introduction: My first move with a stubborn door is to find out which part is being a pain in the ass. Hinges let the door swing; the latch holds it closed against the striker, its mating catch on the body. Extra opening or closing effort can come from insufficient lubrication, door alignment or striker adjustment. Spraying everything nearby skips the useful part: finding the cause. [Door operation diagnosis](#/document/G1695898)
guides.why: A latch should engage securely and release easily from either handle. Targeted lubrication can restore a dry latch, but excessive grease can damage its internal lock motor. The exterior key cylinder has its own lubrication-and-retest sequence. I want smooth operation without turning a small maintenance job into an expensive one. [Latch and cylinder checks](#/document/G1695898) [Lubrication precautions](#/document/G1695899)

when.summary: Check operation every six months and lubricate where needed using the applicable procedure.
notes: Address failure to latch or release promptly.

prepare.title: Latch tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver suited to the latch opening, Motorcraft Multi-Purpose Grease Spray XL-5-A meeting ESB-M1C93-B, and a clean cloth for removing excess grease. The screwdriver operates the latch while the door remains open. [Door-latch lubrication](#/document/G1695899)

prepare.title: Optional key-cylinder materials
prepare.detail: For an accessible exterior key cylinder that binds, have the correct key and a lock lubricant such as Motorcraft XL-1. If that restores locking and unlocking, the cylinder procedure then calls for multi-purpose grease such as Motorcraft XL-5 for lasting lubrication. Keep these cylinder instructions separate from the latch’s product specification and application time. [Cylinder lubrication, G5](#/document/G1695898)

prepare.title: Access
prepare.detail: Open the door to reach the latch opening on its trailing edge. Lubrication uses the installed latch. Window-glass, trim and handle removal belong to the separate latch-replacement procedure. For the key-cylinder branch, establish the vehicle’s normal key access before starting. [Lubrication access](#/document/G1695899) [Separate latch replacement](#/document/G1695904)

prepare.title: Personal and chemical protection
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp edges. Read each product’s safety information before use. Keep solvents away from flames and other ignition sources; incorrect handling can cause injury or fire. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the car. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle, keeping it under your control for the lock checks. An unexpected engine start during service can cause serious injury. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Observe the door as it swings
steps.body:
Move the door through its normal opening and closing travel, keeping fingers clear of the hinges and latch. Notice where resistance or noise occurs: during the swing, or only as the door meets the body. This is an observation, not an alignment measurement. Ford identifies hinges, door alignment, striker adjustment and the latch as possible causes of extra effort. [Mechanical diagnosis, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

Leave hinge and striker fasteners secured during this check. If the latch later passes its open-door test but the door remains difficult to close, have striker adjustment and door alignment assessed before deciding the hinges need lubrication. That is Ford’s diagnostic order. [Mechanical diagnosis, A2–A5](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Compare both door handles
steps.body:
With the door unlocked, check opening from the exterior handle and then the interior handle. Observe whether each handle releases the door easily and returns after being released. If a handle fails, stop closing the door for repeated trials. [Handle checks, Tests A–E](#/document/G1695898)

A problem affecting only one handle follows a different diagnostic route from a door that is difficult from both handles. Record which handle sticks, needs extra effort or fails to release; that detail helps identify the appropriate next test. [Handle diagnosis, Tests B–E](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Separate locking trouble from opening trouble
steps.body:
Press lock and unlock on the driver’s door control switch, then repeat from the passenger’s switch while observing which locks respond. Record whether the failure affects one door, both doors, only one direction or only one switch. These patterns lead to different electrical tests; they do not establish that the latch needs grease. Finish with the door unlocked. [Power-lock checks, Tests H–K](#/document/G1695898)

For an exterior key cylinder whose normal key access is established, insert the correct key and check both locking and unlocking. If it works normally, skip the cylinder service in step 5. If it rotates freely without operating the lock, arrange the linkage/free-spin diagnostic route in Test G2–G4. A binding cylinder follows the lubrication branch in step 5. [Manual-lock check, G1–G5](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Service an accessible binding key cylinder
steps.body:
Use this branch only for a symptomatic, binding exterior key cylinder with normal key access already established. Spray a lock lubricant, such as Motorcraft XL-1, into the cylinder opening for a couple of seconds. Operate the cylinder with the key and check whether it now locks and unlocks the door. [Cylinder lubrication test, G5](#/document/G1695898)

If locking and unlocking return, apply multi-purpose grease, such as Motorcraft XL-5, into the cylinder opening for a couple of seconds to provide lasting lubrication. Operate the key again and verify both functions. The cylinder application is a couple of seconds, separate from the latch’s approximately five-second application. [Cylinder lubrication and result, G5](#/document/G1695898)

If locking and unlocking do not return, stop this basic cylinder service and arrange removal-based diagnosis of the cylinder and linkage. Do not assume the latch is responsible. Finish with the door unlocked before continuing the latch checks. [Further cylinder diagnosis, G6–G7](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Test the latch with the door open
steps.body:
Open the door and identify the latch opening on its trailing edge. Keep fingers out of the moving mechanism to avoid a pinch injury. Use the flat-bladed screwdriver to move the latch into its fully latched position: two clicks. The door stays open throughout this operation. [Latch positioning](#/document/G1695899)

Remove the screwdriver and pull a door handle to check whether the latch releases easily. Repeat the two-click setup to check release from the other handle. Always return the latch to its released position before moving the door closed. [Open-door latch test, A2](#/document/G1695898)

If both handles release it easily, skip latch lubrication and proceed to step 11; use the diagnostic decisions below for any remaining movement complaint. If both releases are stiff, continue with lubrication. If only one handle fails, stop here and arrange the corresponding handle/cable diagnosis. [Diagnostic branches, A1–A3 and Tests B–C](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Lubricate the latch opening
steps.body:
For a latch needing lubrication, leave the door open and use the screwdriver to set the latch fully closed again, through two clicks. Remove the screwdriver. Spray Motorcraft Multi-Purpose Grease Spray XL-5-A, specification ESB-M1C93-B, into the latch opening for approximately 5 seconds. [Application sequence and material](#/document/G1695899)

Use the specified approximately five-second application. Excessive grease can damage the internal lock motor. [Over-lubrication precaution](#/document/G1695899)

steps.title: Release the latch before closing the door
steps.body:
Operate the exterior door handle to release the latch. Ford notes that exterior handles may operate mechanically or electronically; use the handle’s normal operation. Confirm that the latch has returned to its open position before closing the door. [Exterior-handle release](#/document/G1695899)

If the latch will not release, keep the door open and stop the cycling sequence. Arrange diagnosis rather than trying to close the door against an already closed latch. [Release check, A3](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Distribute the lubricant and clean up
steps.body: Once the latch is released, open and close the door several times to circulate the lubricant inside it. Then open the door and wipe away excess grease from the exposed latch area. Keep fingers clear of the moving mechanism. [Distribution and cleanup](#/document/G1695899)

steps.title: Retest the serviced latch
steps.body:
After lubrication, repeat the open-door test: use the screwdriver to close the latch through two clicks, remove the tool, and check easy release with each handle, resetting the latch between trials. Leave it released when finished. [Post-lubrication test, A3](#/document/G1695898)

Easy release after the original stiffness indicates insufficient latch lubrication caused that concern. If release remains difficult in the both-handles diagnostic branch, Ford directs latch replacement. Arrange that separate repair instead of adding more spray. [Result and repair decision, A3](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Confirm complete door operation
steps.body:
With the screwdriver and cloth clear and the latch released, close the door normally. Confirm that it engages securely, then unlock and open it using each handle in separate trials. Persistent extra closing effort calls for striker and door-alignment assessment even if the latch itself releases easily. [Door operation checks, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

Repeat the lock/unlock checks from both door switches and note any remaining fault. If you serviced the accessible key cylinder, confirm that the key still locks and unlocks correctly after its final lubrication. Finish unlocked. [Power-lock checks, Tests H–K](#/document/G1695898) [Cylinder result, G5](#/document/G1695898)

watchFor.title: A door that needs slamming
watchFor.body: Extra force can involve the striker, door alignment, hinges or latch. Have the cause assessed instead of accepting a harder slam as routine operation. [Possible causes, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

watchFor.title: A handle that stays pulled out
watchFor.body: Binding linkage or a failed return spring can cause a sticking handle. Arrange the appropriate handle diagnosis. [Sticking-handle diagnosis, Tests D–E](#/document/G1695898)

watchFor.title: A latch left closed while the door is open
watchFor.body: The screwdriver test deliberately closes the latch without closing the door. Release it with the handle before every actual door-closing attempt. Keep fingers out of its moving parts. [Latch setup and release sequence](#/document/G1695899)

watchFor.title: Persistent rattles
watchFor.body: Ford’s noise diagnosis checks for loose internal components, striker adjustment and door alignment before judging the result of latch lubrication. A rattle alone does not prove the latch needs replacement. [Noise diagnosis, Test F](#/document/G1695898)

procedures.purpose: Installed door-latch positioning, specified grease, application, release, cycling and cleanup.
Operation checks, accessible binding-cylinder lubrication and symptom-based decisions for door movement, handles and locks.
Separate latch-replacement reference when diagnosis requires repair; its removal operations are not lubrication prerequisites.
Task-relevant starting, personal-protection and chemical precautions.
Avoid replacement decisions based on a fault that is not present during testing.

stepGroups.title: Set up, identify the symptom and check locks
stepGroups.summary: Separate door movement, handle release and electrical locking complaints; service an accessible binding key cylinder when appropriate.

stepGroups.title: Check and lubricate the latch
stepGroups.summary: Use the two-click setup, controlled application, exterior-handle release and cleanup sequence.

stepGroups.title: Retest and finish
stepGroups.summary: Verify the latch result and complete door and lock operation.

diagnostics.finding: The latch was stiff from both handles and releases easily after lubrication.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies insufficient latch lubrication as the cause in this diagnostic branch.
diagnostics.next: Complete the normal door and locking checks, then wipe away any remaining excess. [A3 result](#/document/G1695898) [Cleanup](#/document/G1695899)

diagnostics.finding: The latch releases easily with the door open, but closing the door still takes unusual effort.
diagnostics.meaning: The open-door test has not established a latch lubrication fault.
diagnostics.next: Have striker adjustment checked, followed by door alignment. Ford calls for hinge lubrication after those checks pass. [A4–A5 sequence](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: Only the interior or exterior handle has trouble releasing the door.
diagnostics.meaning: The affected handle, cable or linkage needs isolation before condemning the latch.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the corresponding interior- or exterior-handle diagnosis. [Tests B–C](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: The latch remains difficult to release after the specified lubrication in the both-handles branch.
diagnostics.meaning: The lubrication test has failed.
diagnostics.next: Arrange latch replacement as a separate repair. [A3 replacement decision](#/document/G1695898) [Front-door latch repair](#/document/G1695904)

diagnostics.finding: The exterior key cylinder rotates freely without locking or unlocking.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford routes this symptom through checks of the cylinder-to-latch connections and the cylinder’s free-spin operation.
diagnostics.next: Arrange Test G2–G4 diagnosis. Skip the binding-cylinder lubrication branch. [Free-spin diagnosis](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: An accessible binding key cylinder locks and unlocks after the initial lock lubricant.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies insufficient cylinder lubrication as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Complete step 5’s couple-second multi-purpose grease application, then verify key-operated locking and unlocking again. [Cylinder lubrication result, G5](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: The binding key cylinder still does not lock and unlock after the initial lubricant.
diagnostics.meaning: The basic lubrication test has not resolved the fault.
diagnostics.next: Stop cylinder service and arrange removal-based cylinder and linkage diagnosis. [Cylinder diagnosis, G6–G7](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: Power locking remains intermittent or fails from particular switches or in one direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom needs electrical diagnosis; lubrication alone does not identify its cause.
diagnostics.next: Provide the observed door, switch and direction pattern for Tests H–K. An intermittent fault that is absent during testing is not grounds for guessing at replacement components. [Electrical symptom routes](#/document/G1695898) [Diagnostic assumptions](#/document/G1693185)

verification.title: Latch released and tools clear
verification.body: Before the final closure, confirm that the latch is open and the screwdriver has been removed. [Lubrication release sequence](#/document/G1695899)

verification.title: Engagement and release restored
verification.body: Confirm that the door engages securely and opens easily from both handles when unlocked. Persistent difficulty requires the appropriate diagnostic branch. If it will not latch securely or release reliably, stop using the car until the fault is corrected. [Door operation checks, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

verification.title: Locking checked separately
verification.body: Check both door switches in both directions and record any remaining failure. If the accessible key cylinder was serviced, verify that it locks and unlocks after the final grease application. [Lock checks, Tests G–K](#/document/G1695898)

verification.title: Excess removed
verification.body: Wipe away excess grease from the exposed latch area after cycling the door. [Final lubrication step](#/document/G1695899)

notes: Applies to the original 2015 Mustang scope: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. The inspection has no engine-specific branch.
Select seat-control and folding-backrest steps by fitted equipment; do not assume the coupe and convertible have identical rear-seat mechanisms.

Ford documents separate automatic-locking and road-test procedures. They remain follow-on diagnosis or repair verification, rather than universal requirements for this routine checklist. [Functional-test branches](#/document/G1883856)
guides.title: Seatbelts and seat latches: a hands-on wear-and-function check
guides.summary: Inspect every belt, check stationary buckle and retractor operation, exercise the fitted seat controls, and confirm that moved seats latch securely. Includes cleaning precautions and clear repair routes.
guides.introduction: I like a satisfying buckle click, but it is a damn short inspection report. This guide takes you through belt condition, stationary buckle and retractor checks, and the normal release-and-return checks for your fitted seats. It also explains Ford’s cleaning requirements. It covers the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine; select the seat checks by equipment. This routine check does not provide collision clearance or prove vehicle-sensitive locking performance. [Seatbelt maintenance](#/document/G1692224) [Stationary belt checks](#/document/G1883856)
guides.why: The webbing is the fabric belt, the tongue is the metal piece that enters the buckle, and the retractor draws the belt back into storage. Their condition and operation matter together. The seat also needs to remain secured in its intended position. A working buckle cannot cancel out damaged webbing, and a backrest resting upright has not necessarily latched. [Belt inspection](#/document/G1883856) [Ford seat-latch checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

when.summary: Check seatbelts and seat latches for wear and proper function every six months.
notes: Collision repair requires the separate inspection of all seatbelt components.

prepare.title: Make room for every seating position
prepare.detail: Park with the engine off and keep the ignition off during the belt checks. Clear belongings from the seat tracks, belt paths and behind the backrests. Never adjust the driver’s seat while moving; unexpected seat movement can cause loss of control. Keep objects out from behind a backrest before returning it. [Manual seat precautions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Gather viewing aids, not removal tools
prepare.detail: A light and somewhere to record findings are useful. These checks use accessible belts and normal seat controls; no jack, drill or trim removal is needed. Leave anchors, restraint connectors and pretensioners assembled. Front retractor/pretensioner removal requires a separate SRS depowering procedure, and incorrect restraint work can trigger deployment and serious injury. Do not probe, power or dismantle a pretensioner. [Front restraint service](#/document/G1692230) [SRS safety](#/document/G1696297)

prepare.title: Plan access around child restraints
prepare.detail: If a child restraint prevents access, follow its manufacturer’s removal and installation instructions before disturbing it. Keep any required refitting separate from the belt checklist so it cannot be forgotten. Ford directs owners to the child-restraint manufacturer for its specific inspection and maintenance requirements. [Restraint maintenance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517116&Uid=G1634902&ProcUid=G1517132&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Have the correct cleaning instructions if cleaning is needed
prepare.detail: Identify the solution recommended in the vehicle’s owner literature and have that product’s instructions available. Ford requires full belt extraction before cleaning and prohibits bleaching or re-dyeing because either can weaken the webbing and increase crash-injury risk. No chemical is needed simply to inspect the belt. [Cleaning requirements](#/document/G1692223)

steps.title: Separate routine checking from collision follow-up
steps.body:
Establish whether the car has been in a crash or a belt has experienced severe stress. Severe stress deserves particular attention during inspection. After any crash, arrange an authorized-dealer check of belt function, including automatic locking operation at passenger positions; this checklist cannot clear the restraints for continued service. All seatbelt components must be inspected and corrected during collision repair. [Seatbelt maintenance](#/document/G1692224) [Collision requirements](#/document/G1692225) [Owner collision instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Ford recommends replacement of assemblies that were in use during a crash. Its owner instructions allow a minor-crash exception only when an authorized dealer finds no damage and correct operation. Assemblies not in use also need inspection and replacement if damaged or operating incorrectly. The workshop procedure specifically requires new belts at positions where deployment occurred and the belts were used. [Owner replacement guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517116&Uid=G1634902&ProcUid=G1517132&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Collision procedure](#/document/G1692225)

steps.title: Inspect both faces and edges of each belt
steps.body:
Work through every seating position, including the rarely used rear belts. Draw the webbing out slowly as you inspect its accessible length. Look for nicks, tears, cuts, fraying or stretching, examining both faces and edges. Record the seating position and where the defect appears. Do not decide that a small cut is harmless because the buckle still works. Ford’s preliminary inspection specifically includes webbing integrity, the buckle and the tongue. [Belt inspection](#/document/G1883856) [Owner condition checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517116&Uid=G1634902&ProcUid=G1517132&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

If the webbing will not come out, continue with the slow-extraction guidance in step 4 rather than forcing access.

steps.title: Inspect hardware and the visible belt path
steps.body:
Look at each accessible buckle, tongue, guide and attachment area for visible damage or displacement. Note cracked, bent or distorted parts and webbing caught against trim or seating. Keep mounting hardware tight and untouched during this inspection. A damaged retaining area requires assessment as part of restraint repair. [Assembly condition](#/document/G1692224) [Buckle and tongue inspection](#/document/G1883856)

At the front seats, check the belt’s normal route across the occupant. Ford provides an outboard web guide; use it if the shoulder belt otherwise misses the middle of the shoulder. Match the guide to the fitted seat rather than assuming every Mustang seat uses the same arrangement. [Belt routing and guides](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Record an apparent twist instead of rotating an installed anchor to flatten it. The coupe’s front-belt installation has a prescribed 180-degree anchor orientation, so an anchor adjustment is a separate service operation. [Coupe installation detail](#/document/G1692230)

steps.title: Check retractor travel and return
steps.body:
At each position, slowly extend the belt to full extension, then allow it to return to its stowed position. Watch for excessive effort, binding or webbing that fails to retract. Ford’s stationary retractor check covers travel between these two positions. If it binds or fails to return, record the concern and arrange diagnosis; do not pull trim away to investigate. [Retractor check](#/document/G1883856)

A belt pulled too quickly can lock normally. Let it retract slightly, then draw it out again slowly and steadily. Full extension can also engage automatic locking mode on the front passenger and rear belts; the driver’s belt does not have that mode. Unbuckle if necessary and let the belt retract completely to restore normal operation, then check slow extraction and return again. [Locking modes and reset](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

If it remains locked, stop this position’s check and use the separate locked-retractor service route. A locked belt can have a normal cause, but the repair procedure can progress to anchor removal; that is beyond this inspection. [Locked retractor procedure](#/document/G1883858)

steps.title: Check buckle engagement, retention and release
steps.body:
With the seatback upright, insert the tongue into its proper buckle—the buckle nearest the direction from which that tongue comes. It should enter without excessive effort, click and feel latched. Keep the lap belt low and snug across the hips, with the shoulder portion across the chest. [Fastening and fit](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

For Ford’s stationary buckle check, pull forcefully on the webbing after latching to verify that the tongue stays retained. Fully press the release button: it should operate without excessive effort, the tongue should come out easily, and the belt should release and retract. Repeat the complete latching, retention-pull and release sequence three times. This checks buckle retention; it does not establish a calibrated load capacity or vehicle-sensitive locking result. [Buckle and tongue check](#/document/G1883856)

If engagement, retention or release is unreliable, stop using that position pending assessment. Ford directs replacement of the buckle or retractor as required when this test identifies a concern; identifying the correct component belongs to diagnosis. [Buckle test decisions](#/document/G1883856)

steps.title: Clean only when needed, using the specified method
steps.body:
For a soiled belt, first establish the cleaning solution recommended by the vehicle’s owner literature. Fully extract the belt before applying it, then carry out the product manufacturer’s application and completion instructions. Do not substitute bleach, dye or an improvised chemical treatment: weakened webbing can increase the risk of serious injury in a crash. [Seatbelt cleaning](#/document/G1692223)

Once the product’s instructions are complete, examine the belt again and repeat the extraction-and-return check. Cleaning does not resolve a cut, fraying or a mechanical operating fault. If you have not identified the recommended solution, leave cleaning for later; you can still finish the condition and operation inspection. [Condition requirements](#/document/G1692224) [Retractor check](#/document/G1883856)

steps.title: Check front-seat movement using the fitted controls
steps.body:
Look at the accessible seat controls and latch areas for visible wear or damage, then check each front seat using its normal controls. Keep the car stationary and the movement path clear. [Owner wear-and-function check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

Manual seat: use the front bar, identified as A in Ford’s control illustration, to move the seat backward and forward. Release the bar at the intended position, then rock the seat backward and forward to confirm it has fully locked. If fitted, lever B adjusts seat height. Return the seat to its intended position and repeat the track-lock check after movement. [Manual seat controls and locking check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Power seat: use the switch on the outboard side. Move it in the indicated direction to check forward/backward movement and the fitted cushion raising/lowering functions. Release the switch, return the seat to its intended position and note any failure to move, stop or remain positioned during ordinary use. This is an operating observation, not a manual-track latch test. [Power seat controls](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539512&Uid=G1634988&ProcUid=G1638641&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Check the fitted backrest-angle control
steps.body:
Where the manual recline lever is fitted, use lever C to change the backrest angle, then return the backrest upright and release the control. Observe whether it remains in the selected position during normal use. Report a control that will not release or a backrest that will not hold its position; do not improvise a force test. Keep the space behind the backrest clear while returning it. [Backrest control](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Leave the backrest upright for occupancy. Excessive recline can let an occupant slide beneath the belt during a crash and suffer severe injury. [Seating precaution](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Check front-seat folding for rear access
steps.body:
For the fitted rear-access mechanism on either body style, use the release handle on the upper back of the front seat and fold the front backrest forward. Return it to its original position. Ford specifies that the backrest remembers that position and locks automatically there. Confirm that it has returned and remains secured without holding the release handle; if engagement is uncertain, keep that seat out of use pending assessment. Repeat for the other front seat. [Front backrest release and return](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539514&Uid=G1634990&ProcUid=G1638642&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Keep objects clear behind the backrest before returning it. A bag wedged in the mechanism is a pain in the ass, not a latch diagnosis. [Return-path precaution](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Check split-folding rear backrests, if fitted
steps.body:
On a car equipped with split-folding rear backrests, check each section individually. Pull its release strap and fold the backrest down. Raise it again and listen for the latch to engage, then pull down on the backrest to confirm it has latched. A click without secure retention does not complete the check. [Rear backrest operation and engagement check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539514&Uid=G1634990&ProcUid=G1638642&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Skip this folding check where the feature is absent, including a convertible without folding rear backrests. Do not remove the convertible backrest or loadspace trim to create access for a routine check. Those are separate removal operations. A confirmed coupe rear-backrest latch fault likewise belongs to latch repair, not upholstery removal during this inspection. [Convertible service access](#/document/G1692610) [Rear latch repair](#/document/G1692167)

steps.title: Restore every seat and belt you moved
steps.body:
Return front seats to their intended positions. Rock each manually adjusted seat backward and forward to confirm track locking. Make sure front backrests returned through the rear-access release have automatically locked in their original positions. For each folding rear section, confirm engagement again with the specified downward pull. Leave backrests upright for occupancy. [Manual seat locking](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Backrest engagement](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539514&Uid=G1634990&ProcUid=G1638642&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Make sure no belt or buckle was trapped by the returning seats. Leave them accessible to occupants, and allow belts extended during the check to stow completely. Recheck the front shoulder-belt route after restoring the seat position. [Belt accessibility](#/document/G1692230) [Belt routing and full-stow reset](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Record the outcome and route any fault
steps.body:
Record which positions you checked and any visible defect, sticking, failed retention, poor retraction or uncertain seat engagement. As an owner precaution, keep an affected seating position out of use until assessed. Describe the actual symptom rather than ordering a part by guesswork. Ford’s symptom chart distinguishes locking modes, routing, trim interference and internal retractor faults. [Belt diagnosis](#/document/G1883856)

If nothing concerning was found, the routine condition and stationary-operation checklist is finished. Replacement work has additional requirements: inspect retaining areas, restore damaged attachment structure as required, install the correct assembly using its procedure, and carry out the appropriate Functional Test at all seating positions. Those post-replacement requirements do not make every routine owner check a full workshop test. [Maintenance and replacement requirements](#/document/G1692224)

watchFor.title: Normal locking mistaken for a failed retractor
watchFor.body: Fast extraction can lock a belt; passenger and rear belts can also enter automatic locking mode after full extension. Use the documented slow-extraction or full-stow reset before describing the symptom. Persistent locking still needs assessment. [Owner locking-mode instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: Cleaning that hides damage
watchFor.body: Bleach and dye can weaken webbing. Cleaning is for soiling; a damaged belt needs assessment rather than a cosmetic rescue mission. [Cleaning safety](#/document/G1692223) [Condition inspection](#/document/G1692224)

watchFor.title: A seat that merely looks back in place
watchFor.body: Use the actual engagement check: rock a manually adjusted seat backward and forward, and pull down on a raised folding rear backrest after hearing it latch. Uncertain engagement means the position is not ready for use. [Manual seat check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Rear backrest check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539514&Uid=G1634990&ProcUid=G1638642&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: Warning-lamp or chime concerns
watchFor.body: A missing seatbelt reminder is a separate diagnostic concern, not proof of a mechanical belt fault. Ford routes diagnosis differently when the airbag warning indicator is illuminated. Record the warning behavior and use [Warning lamps](#/maintenance/warning-lamps) for the related owner check. [Warning symptom routes](#/document/G1883856)

procedures.purpose: Routine condition inspection and the separate retaining-area and functional-test requirements after replacement.
Preliminary inspection, stationary buckle/retractor checks and symptom-based diagnostic routing.
Full-extraction cleaning prerequisite, recommended-solution requirement and chemical precautions.
Collision inspection, correction and replacement requirements.
Belt accessibility, coupe anchor-orientation distinction and restraint-removal boundary.
Safety basis for leaving pretensioner and SRS service outside the inspection.
Separate service destination for a persistently locked retractor.
Distinguish convertible backrest/trim service access from routine owner inspection.
Separate repair destination for a confirmed coupe rear-backrest latch fault.

stepGroups.title: Check history and visible condition
stepGroups.summary: Separate collision follow-up from routine care and examine every accessible belt assembly.

stepGroups.title: Check stationary belt operation
stepGroups.summary: Check extraction, return, buckle retention and release, then clean only if needed.

stepGroups.title: Exercise the fitted seats
stepGroups.summary: Check manual or power movement, front backrest return and fitted rear folding latches.

stepGroups.title: Restore and finish
stepGroups.summary: Confirm seat engagement, leave belts accessible and record any required follow-up.

diagnostics.finding: Webbing is nicked, cut, torn, frayed or stretched
diagnostics.meaning: The belt has a condition concern even if it latches and retracts. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1883856)
diagnostics.next: Record the position and defect; keep that position out of use pending assessment and any required replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Tongue is hard to insert, does not stay retained, or is difficult to release
diagnostics.meaning: The stationary buckle-and-tongue check has identified a fault. Ford calls for a new buckle or retractor as required. [Buckle check](#/document/G1883856)
diagnostics.next: Arrange diagnosis and the correct restraint repair. Do not treat repeated attempts that occasionally work as a pass.

diagnostics.finding: Belt binds, remains slack or will not extract after the normal reset
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include routing, trim interference, a locking condition or internal retractor binding; the symptom alone does not identify the part. [Retractor symptom chart](#/document/G1883856) [Locked-belt service](#/document/G1883858)
diagnostics.next: Record when it happens and arrange the appropriate diagnosis. Leave anchor removal and internal investigation to the separate service procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Manual seat moves after its control is released, or a backrest fails to engage
diagnostics.meaning: The seat has not met its normal locking or engagement check. [Manual seat locking](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Backrest engagement](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539514&Uid=G1634990&ProcUid=G1638642&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)
diagnostics.next: Keep the affected seat out of use and report the precise mechanism and failed action. Route a confirmed coupe rear-backrest latch fault to [Latch repair](#/document/G1692167).

diagnostics.finding: Crash history without completed restraint inspection
diagnostics.meaning: Routine checks cannot satisfy the required collision inspection and correction. Skipping that work can leave incorrect restraint operation and increase crash-injury risk. [Collision inspection](#/document/G1692225)
diagnostics.next: Arrange authorized-dealer inspection of all belt functions and the applicable collision repair requirements before treating the restraints as cleared.

diagnostics.finding: No damage or operating concern found
diagnostics.meaning: The routine visual and stationary checks found no concern within this guide’s scope. [Maintenance inspection](#/document/G1692224)
diagnostics.next: Record completion and leave every seat secured and every belt accessible. No additional repair test is required by this checklist solely because you performed the owner check.

verification.title: Every belt position completed
verification.body: Confirm that each accessible belt was inspected, extended and returned, and checked for buckle engagement, retention and easy release. Any position you could not check remains recorded as incomplete rather than assumed satisfactory. [Stationary inspection and checks](#/document/G1883856)

verification.title: Every moved seat secured
verification.body: Confirm manual track locking by rocking backward and forward, front rear-access backrests returned to their original locked positions, and each fitted folding rear section latched and checked with a downward pull. [Manual seats](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539511&Uid=G1634986&ProcUid=G1638640&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Backrest return checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539514&Uid=G1634990&ProcUid=G1638642&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Cabin ready for occupants
verification.body: Make sure belts and buckles are accessible, none were caught by seat movement, and any fully extended passenger or rear belt has returned completely to stow. Complete any child-restraint refitting according to its manufacturer’s instructions before using it. [Belt accessibility](#/document/G1692230) [Locking-mode reset](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G910645&Uid=G1634896&ProcUid=G1638636&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) [Child-restraint instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517116&Uid=G1634902&ProcUid=G1517132&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

verification.title: Findings have a next action
verification.body: Record any unresolved fault and affected position. If replacement or collision work follows, confirm that its separate retaining-area inspection and appropriate all-position Functional Test are included in that work. This article does not record those repairs or tests as performed. [Replacement checks](#/document/G1692224) [Collision checks](#/document/G1692225)

notes: Respond to an active warning when it occurs; do not wait for the next routine check.
This cabin check does not require lifting the vehicle, removing the cluster, disconnecting the battery or entering engineering test mode.

MyKey notices can describe an active restriction rather than a fault. For example, Buckle Up to Unmute Audio is a belt reminder associated with MyKey. [MyKey message meanings](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1642765&Uid=G1634747&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.title: Warning lamps: an owner’s start-up check and response guide
guides.summary: Check the warning lamps on your 2015 Mustang, distinguish normal start-up behavior from an active warning, and choose the right next action.
guides.introduction: A dashboard full of lights at start-up can be perfectly normal. One stubborn light afterward can deserve your immediate attention. I’ll walk you through the stationary owner check for a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, then explain the important warning responses. This covers observation and owner action; circuit tests, pressure measurements and repairs are separate jobs. The goal is to understand what the damn car is saying before buying parts.
guides.why: The instrument panel cluster, or IPC, displays information supplied by several vehicle modules. Brake, airbag, engine and other warnings can originate outside the cluster, so an illuminated symbol does not automatically mean the display needs replacing. A normal lamp check confirms the observed display behavior; it does not certify the entire monitored system. [Cluster operation](#/document/G1693931)

when.summary: Check operation of brake, ABS, airbag and seatbelt warning lamps every six months.
notes: Respond to an active warning when it occurs; do not wait for the routine check.

prepare.title: Set up a stationary check
prepare.detail: Park somewhere safe and level, apply the parking brake and begin with the engine and ignition off. Stay in the driver’s seat for the check. The brake lamp is expected to illuminate with the ignition on and parking brake applied. [Brake-lamp behavior](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539493&Uid=G1801494&ProcUid=G1642762&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Have a way to record what happens
prepare.detail: No service tools or replacement materials are needed for this cabin check. A clock or timer helps compare the short lamp checks. A notebook or phone can preserve the exact message, whether a lamp flashed or stayed on, and whether the engine was running. Take photographs only while safely parked.

prepare.title: Match the fitted equipment
prepare.detail: Identify the ABS, brake, airbag and seatbelt symbols before switching on. Check additional indicators only where fitted. Some warnings appear in the information display and do not illuminate during start-up; an absent start-up appearance is not automatically a fault for every symbol. [Ford warning-lamp guide](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539493&Uid=G1801494&ProcUid=G1642762&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Deal with an existing urgent warning first
prepare.detail: If you are responding to a warning that appeared while driving, read step 6 before attempting another start. An oil-pressure, overheating or brake-system warning takes priority over finishing a routine checklist. [Required message responses](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1642765&Uid=G1634747&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Switch on and watch the actual lamp check
steps.body:
While stationary, leave the driver’s belt unbuckled briefly and switch the ignition to ON/RUN without starting the engine. Watch from the moment you switch on. Ford calls this a prove-out: a short display check before normal indications take over.

Use these expected durations:

- ABS: 3 seconds.
- Airbag: 6 seconds.
- Brake: 3 seconds for the prove-out; it can remain illuminated because the parking brake is applied.
- Seatbelt: 65 seconds with the belt unbuckled, or until you buckle it.
- Stability/traction control, stability control OFF and tire-pressure warning: 3 seconds each.
- LED low-beam malfunction indicator: 3 seconds, where applicable.

The analog gauges also sweep and then return to the indication commanded by their inputs. Record any expected lamp that never appears, continues flashing or remains illuminated beyond its normal check without an explained operating condition. [Start-up and prove-out details](#/document/G1693931)

steps.title: Check the belt response and separate the parking-brake indication
steps.body:
Fasten the driver’s belt and confirm that the seatbelt indicator goes out. Do not count its timed disappearance while unbuckled as a successful buckle-response check. If the reminder does not respond correctly, record the behavior and arrange diagnosis; the [seatbelt and latch guide](#/maintenance/seatbelts-latches) covers the separate physical inspection. [Seatbelt indicator operation](#/document/G1693931)

For the brake lamp, keep the vehicle stationary with the foot brake firmly applied. Briefly release the parking brake and observe the lamp after the initial prove-out. If it remains on, do not dismiss it as a parking-brake reminder: low fluid or a brake-system malfunction can also illuminate it. Arrange immediate assessment. Reapply the parking brake before continuing or leaving the seat. Do not drive to try to make the light disappear. [Brake warning meaning and urgency](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539493&Uid=G1801494&ProcUid=G1642762&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Recognize the engine light’s pre-start behavior
steps.body:
The engine-shaped Service Engine Soon lamp, also called the malfunction indicator lamp or MIL, normally illuminates with the ignition on before the engine starts. That alone is not an engine fault. If, after 15 seconds with the engine still off, it blinks eight times, Ford identifies that pattern as not ready for Inspection/Maintenance emissions testing. That is different from a blinking lamp with the engine running.

Parking-lamp, high-beam, fog-lamp and turn-signal indicators have no timed prove-out in the cluster table; they normally follow the corresponding controls. Do not mark them faulty merely because they stayed dark during this check. [MIL behavior](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539493&Uid=G1801494&ProcUid=G1642762&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web) · [Indicator prove-out table](#/document/G1693931)

steps.title: Observe what remains after a normal start
steps.body:
If there is no unresolved warning requiring the engine to remain off, fasten the belt and start the car using its normal starting procedure in a suitable open-air location. Keep the car stationary and the parking brake applied. No road test or deliberate ABS or traction-control activation is needed for this owner check.

Observe which warnings remain after the start-up sequence. The Service Engine Soon lamp normally goes out after cranking when no malfunction is present. The brake lamp can remain on with the parking brake applied. Treat any other continuing warning according to its specific meaning below, rather than expecting every symbol to behave identically. An airbag lamp that never illuminated, keeps flashing or stays on requires service. [After-start warning behavior](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539493&Uid=G1801494&ProcUid=G1642762&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Read and record the message before pressing OK
steps.body:
Write down the exact wording, accompanying symbols, steady or flashing behavior, and whether the warning appeared before starting, with the engine running or during an earlier drive. Include other warnings that appeared at the same time.

The steering-wheel OK button acknowledges and removes some messages; others disappear automatically. Certain messages must be acknowledged before menus become available. Wording may be shortened, and available messages depend on equipment and cluster type. Acknowledging a message changes what is displayed—it does not establish that the underlying condition has been corrected. [Information-display messages and controls](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1642765&Uid=G1634747&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Give stop warnings their proper priority
steps.body:
For an active warning, follow the matching response immediately:
