prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system on a level platform, a steering-wheel holding device and the equipment manufacturer’s instructions. Arrange safe underbody access at the facility for inspection and adjustment. A tire-pressure gauge is needed for the preliminary checks; a surface gauge is needed only for the ride-height branch. Alignment measurement does not itself require wheel removal. [Alignment setup](#/document/G2361401) [Tire checks](#/document/G1686610) [Ride-height equipment](#/document/G1686616)

prepare.title: Prepare only for the work selected
prepare.detail: For toe or rear-camber adjustment, the facility needs tools matching the actual fasteners and torque equipment covering the specified values. Rear toe requires mild cleaning liquids. After rear toe adjustment, an LDW-equipped car requires a scan tool capable of the IPMA camera-alignment routine. If wheels must come off, have Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 and wheel-torque equipment available. [Rear toe requirements](#/document/G2361401) [Rear camber requirements](#/document/G2361400) [Front toe requirements](#/document/G2361399) [Wheel installation materials](#/document/G1686507)

prepare.title: Prevent unexpected starting and protect yourself
prepare.detail: Before service around or beneath the car, disable remote start if fitted through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup, and remove the key so another person cannot start it. Wear eye and ear protection during service and gloves when handling sharp parts. Follow the safety information for cleaning materials and keep flammable solvents away from ignition sources. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Use proper lifting equipment when a branch needs it
prepare.detail: The lift or jack must support the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo or modifications. Locate the lifting points by the stamped triangles and position lift adapters without contacting vulnerable suspension, steering or exhaust parts. Check clearance before driving onto a platform. For jack lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake, block wheels remaining on the ground and support the car on stands before going underneath. A jack alone can lower unexpectedly and cause a crushing injury. The supplied emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire, not this service. [Lifting points and precautions](#/document/G1663631) [Lifting safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Describe the symptom before changing anything
steps.body: If the car is safe to drive, confirm the complaint on a smooth road. Record whether it pulls, wanders, vibrates or has an off-center steering wheel. Ford routes vibration through separate noise-and-vibration diagnosis; vibration alone does not establish an alignment fault. Note recent repairs because an incorrectly completed repair can contribute to the concern. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686610) [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Check cold pressures, tire sizes and wear
steps.body: With the tires cold and the car carrying its normal loads, check pressures and sizes against the vehicle certification label. Inspect every tire for damage and abnormal wear. Record center wear, wear on both shoulders and wear along one edge. Incorrect pressure can cause rapid center or both-edge wear; excessive toe or camber can cause inner- or outer-edge wear. The pattern is a clue, not a confession from one particular bolt. Correct pressure and arrange replacement of damaged tires as necessary before proceeding. [Tire inspection and wear causes](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Inspect the car that will produce the readings
steps.body:
Check for uneven or excessive loading and aftermarket equipment. With safe access, have the chassis and underbody inspected for excessive mud or road deposits, damaged suspension components, loose fasteners, incorrect or damaged springs, worn shocks or struts, damaged bushings, steering faults and wheel-bearing or hub problems. Remove excessive deposits and correct an obvious cause before continuing. Record what was found and what needs separate repair. [Chassis inspection](#/document/G1686610)

When checking movement between suspension components, use hand force only. Do not lever the wheel or suspension with tools: that can damage parts and create movement that would not appear during the prescribed hand-force check. [Movement-check precaution](#/document/G2361401)

steps.title: Use this wheel routine only if wheels must come off
steps.body:
For a diagnostic exchange, the facility positions the car on a suitable hoist with the transmission in Neutral, following the lifting precautions. Remove the wheel nuts and wheel assembly. Never heat a seized wheel nut; heat can damage the wheel and bearing. [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1663631)

Before each installation, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel and hub/disc mounting faces. Ensure rotor-retaining fasteners do not prevent flat seating. Contamination or interference can allow the wheel to loosen and detach in use. Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft XL-2 only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Keep it off the flat mounting faces, studs, nuts and brake surfaces. Position the wheel and install the nuts finger-tight. [Wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

Before lowering, set the parking brake and restore the applicable movement restraints, including blocks at wheels remaining on the ground. Once the car rests on its tires, tighten the nuts on clean, dry threads to **150 lb.ft (204 Nm)** in a star/cross pattern. This pattern limits brake-disc runout and resulting vibration. Retighten within **160 km (100 mi)** after reinstallation because initial tightening can settle. Complete this installation routine before every subsequent road test. [Movement restraints](#/document/G1693189) [Final wheel tightening](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: For a persistent pull, let the shop isolate tire forces
steps.body:
Use this branch after loading, pressure and tire-condition checks pass. Ford’s diagnostic exchanges the front wheel-and-tire assemblies left to right, then tests the complaint again. Have the facility confirm the actual assembly fit and tire markings before the exchange, and complete step 4 before driving. [Pull diagnostic A1–A3](#/document/G1686610) [Wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

If the pull reverses direction, Ford identifies tire forces and directs a front-to-rear rotation; confirm fit before that move as well. If the pull disappears, tire forces were responsible and the complaint has been corrected. If the pull stays in the same direction, continue to the brake-drag branch. This diagnostic exchange is conditional, not a requirement for every alignment check. [Tire-force decisions](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Have brake drag checked if the pull remains
steps.body:
The next shop check is to spin all four wheel-and-tire assemblies by hand and assess whether they turn freely. Arrange this with the car safely supported and the facility controlling vehicle movement. If its setup requires Neutral or a released parking brake, those conditions belong only to the supported test; reapply the parking brake and restore the applicable wheel restraints before lowering or ground-level wheel tightening. [Brake-drag test](#/document/G1686610) [Support and restraint precautions](#/document/G1693189)

A wheel that does not turn freely sends the job to brake diagnosis. If all four turn freely, proceed to alignment measurement. The test does not require wheel removal. [Pull diagnostic A4–A5](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Set the car to curb load for numerical measurements
steps.body: For alignment and ride-height comparison, Ford specifies **curb load: full service fluids, a full fuel tank, no passengers and no cargo**. Use a flat, level surface and correct tire pressures. This differs from the normal-load pressure check earlier: remove passengers and cargo before taking the measurements against the factory table. [Measurement load](#/document/G1686608) [Ride-height setup](#/document/G1686616)

steps.title: Measure ride height when lean or a low stance calls for it
steps.body:
Use this branch for a lean, bottoming or low ride height after checking loading. Measure both sides with a surface gauge, recording the individual floor-to-component heights before subtracting. [Ride-height concerns](#/document/G1686610) [Measurement method](#/document/G1686616)

**Front:** measure from the floor to the center of the rear control-arm ball-joint cap, identified as measurement 2, and to the center of that arm’s inboard bolt, measurement 3. Front ride height is **measurement 3 minus measurement 2**. Here, “rear control arm” identifies an arm within the front suspension. [Front measurement](#/document/G1686616)

**Rear:** measure from the floor to the toe-link inboard cam-bolt center, measurement 2, and to the toe-link outboard bolt center, measurement 3. Rear ride height is **measurement 2 minus measurement 3**. Do not carry the front subtraction order over to the rear. [Rear measurement](#/document/G1686616)

For the factory models within this guide, compare the results with **front 48.8 mm (1.921 in) ± 12 mm (0.472 in)** and **rear 32.1 mm (1.264 in) ± 10 mm (0.394 in)**. Maximum side-to-side differences are **7.5 mm (0.295 in) front** and **6.3 mm (0.248 in) rear**. These are suspension-reference measurements, not wheel-arch gaps. An out-of-limit height or lean calls for suspension investigation before choosing an alignment correction. [Ride-height and lean limits](#/document/G1686608) [Diagnostic next steps](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Measure both axles with the steering centered
steps.body: Set up the alignment system according to its manufacturer’s instructions on the level platform. Place the steering wheel straight ahead and secure it with the holding device. Measure front and rear toe on both sides and front and rear camber. Retain the starting readings. Include front caster and rear thrust angle in the report for comparison with the reference values below; this guide does not prescribe a caster or thrust-angle correction. [Steering hold and rear setup](#/document/G2361401) [Front toe measurement](#/document/G2361399) [Front camber measurement](#/document/G2361398) [Rear camber measurement](#/document/G2361400) [Additional reference angles](#/document/G1686608)

steps.title: Compare the front readings with the correct factory row
steps.body:
All values below are in **decimal degrees at curb load**. LH and RH mean left and right; the camber and caster split is the side-to-side comparison. Choose the row for the fitted factory configuration. [Front specifications](#/document/G1686608)

| Factory configuration | Camber, each side | Camber split | Caster, each side | Caster split |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base Coupe, Base Convertible, Performance Package Convertible, Track Package Convertible | −0.72° ± 0.75° | 0.0° ± 0.75° | 7.12° ± 0.75° | 0.0° ± 0.75° |
| Performance Package Coupe, Track Package Coupe | −1.03° ± 0.75° | 0.0° ± 0.75° | 6.91° ± 0.75° | 0.0° ± 0.75° |

For every model within this guide, **front total toe is 0.0° ± 0.20°**. Ford does not list separate LH/RH front-toe targets in this table; do not present half the total tolerance as a supplied per-wheel specification. Record both sides with the steering centered and assess the total. [Front camber, caster and toe table](#/document/G1686608)

steps.title: Compare the rear readings without rounding away a requirement
steps.body:
At curb load, the factory rear specifications for the models within this guide are:

| Reading | Target and tolerance |
| --- | --- |
| LH camber | −1.50° ± 0.75° |
| RH camber | −1.50° ± 0.75° |
| LH toe | 0.12° ± 0.20° |
| RH toe | 0.12° ± 0.20° |
| Total toe | 0.23° ± 0.20° |
| Rear thrust angle | 0.0° ± 0.5° |

Use the individual and total toe values as printed. Ford lists a **0.23° total** despite the displayed individual targets being **0.12° each**; do not replace the total target with a recalculated 0.24°. GT350 and GT350R rows belong to configurations outside this article’s engine scope. [Rear specifications](#/document/G1686608)

steps.title: Choose the correction from the complete picture
steps.body:
Compare the initial readings with the applicable targets, tolerances and split limits. An off-center steering wheel can involve unequal front or rear toe, so review both axles. Correct an obvious damaged or loose component before adjusting around it. If alignment is within specification and the preceding tire and brake checks pass, a continuing pull moves to steering-system diagnosis. [Symptom and pull decisions](#/document/G1686610) [Acceptance specifications](#/document/G1686608)

Use only the correction branches justified by the measurements. Complete required camber work before accepting final toe readings: Ford requires alignment to be checked after camber changes, with the corresponding toe adjusted if necessary. [Front camber follow-up](#/document/G2361398) [Rear camber follow-up](#/document/G2361400)

steps.title: Commission front-camber modification as a separate repair
steps.body:
Ford’s front-camber correction modifies the upper strut-to-spindle mounting hole. It is specialist work to commission when measurements justify it, not a casual adjustment to try in the driveway. The illustrated change is **horizontal enlargement by 1.0 mm on each side of the upper hole**, preserving its height and leaving the lower hole unchanged. The worked area must be deburred, cleaned and painted. [Front camber correction](#/document/G2361398)

The separate repair plan must include wheel removal, unclipping and moving the wheel-speed-sensor harness aside on both sides, supporting the spindle with mechanic’s wire, recording the bolt/flag-nut orientation and discarding the removed strut-to-spindle bolts and nuts. Flag nuts must be held with tools, not fingers, because they can spin unexpectedly. [Repair preparation and hardware](#/document/G2361398) [Flag-nut handling](#/document/G1693189)

Ford requires **two new service bolts and nuts per side**. The service bolts are smooth and smaller in diameter than the original splined bolts. They remain snug until alignment is corrected. The repair then restores and secures the sensor harness, reinstalls the wheels, remeasures camber, and finally tightens the strut-to-spindle hardware to **184 lb.ft (250 Nm)** on both sides. Another alignment check and any necessary front-toe correction follow. Replacement suspension hardware must match the specified or equivalent quality and design. Verify these items in the commissioned repair; this planning step does not authorize dismantling the strut joint during inspection. [Front camber repair sequence](#/document/G2361398) [Wheel completion](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: If required, correct rear camber at the facility
steps.body:
Using the alignment system and its manufacturer’s instructions, monitor rear camber. Loosen the upper control-arm inboard nut approximately **two turns**, then slide the arm inward or outward to obtain the applicable setting. Tighten the nut to **85 lb.ft (115 Nm)**. Remeasure to verify the change and check rear toe, adjusting it if necessary. [Rear camber adjustment](#/document/G2361400) [Camber target](#/document/G1686608)

If replacement hardware is needed, use the specified or equivalent quality and design and tighten it as prescribed. These fasteners secure critical suspension joints; a convenient substitute is not a repair plan. [Fastener requirements](#/document/G2361400)

steps.title: If required, set rear toe and preserve the clamp
steps.body:
Keep the steering wheel held straight ahead. On both sides, clean the toe-link cam-bolt and cam-nut area using **mild liquids only**, keeping foreign material out of the joint and its clamping area. Dirt here can prevent correct clamping. [Rear toe preparation](#/document/G2361401)

Loosen each toe-link nut approximately **one full turn**. Rotate the toe-link bolt while monitoring the readings until the individual and total rear toe settings meet the applicable specifications. Tighten the nuts to **129 lb.ft (175 Nm)** without disturbing the settings. Recheck rear toe on both sides and repeat if necessary. A good reading before tightening is only half the job. [Rear toe adjustment and tightening](#/document/G2361401) [Rear toe specifications](#/document/G1686608)

steps.title: If required, set front toe and secure the boots
steps.body:
With the steering straight ahead, loosen the outer tie-rod-end jam nuts on both sides and move the steering-gear boot clamps aside. Rotate the inner tie rods while monitoring both front readings and total toe. Do not allow the flexible steering-gear bellows to twist as the rods turn. [Front toe adjustment](#/document/G2361399) [Front total-toe specification](#/document/G1686608)

Restore the boot clamps to their secured positions and tighten the jam nuts to **76 lb.ft (103 Nm)**. Confirm the bellows are untwisted, then remeasure toe and adjust again if needed. [Front toe completion](#/document/G2361399)

steps.title: Verify the clamped readings and complete the camera branch
steps.body:
Record the final readings after the selected fasteners receive their final tightening. Check them against the correct configuration’s specifications, including relevant split and total values. Confirm the toe rechecks after any camber correction. Save the before-and-after report with the configuration and ranges used; an unexplained green display is a lousy souvenir. [Factory acceptance values](#/document/G1686608) [Camber rechecks](#/document/G2361398) [Rear camber recheck](#/document/G2361400) [Front toe recheck](#/document/G2361399) [Rear toe recheck](#/document/G2361401)

If rear toe was adjusted and the car has **Lane Departure Warning**, connect the scan tool and perform the **IPMA camera-alignment procedure**, following the tool’s directions. Ford requires this for the lane-keeping alert and aid to function correctly. Complete the routine before treating that branch as finished. [Camera-alignment requirement](#/document/G2361401)

steps.title: Road-test the result and keep a wear reference
steps.body:
Once the selected work is physically complete, remove the alignment equipment and steering holder and road-test the car. Compare steering-wheel position and the original pull or wander with the starting complaint. The adjustment procedures require a road test. If a pull remains with correct alignment and completed tire/brake checks, continue steering diagnosis rather than choosing an out-of-spec setting to hide it. [Front toe road test](#/document/G2361399) [Rear toe road test](#/document/G2361401) [Rear camber road test](#/document/G2361400) [Front camber road test](#/document/G2361398) [Persistent-pull decision](#/document/G1686610)

For your own record, photograph the existing tire wear and keep it with the report. Use future inspections to compare the same locations. Record any unresolved complaint and the next diagnostic action instead of calling the job successful because a bolt was turned.

watchFor.title: The right numbers at the wrong load
watchFor.body: Alignment and ride-height specifications require full service fluids, a full fuel tank, no passengers and no cargo. Record that setup before accepting the comparison. [Curb-load requirement](#/document/G1686608)

watchFor.title: Factory settings applied to a modified car
watchFor.body: Ford excludes aftermarket steering, suspension, wheel and tire configurations from these factory specifications. Establish suitable criteria for the actual configuration before adjusting it. [Aftermarket-equipment check](#/document/G1686610)

watchFor.title: A loose or damaged part behind a tidy report
watchFor.body: An obvious component or fastener fault needs correction before continuing. An angle adjustment does not repair a damaged joint, spring, bearing or steering component. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686610)

watchFor.title: Dirty rear toe hardware or twisted front bellows
watchFor.body: Rear toe clamping areas must remain clean, and front steering bellows must remain untwisted with their clamps secured. Check these details as well as the displayed readings. [Rear toe precautions](#/document/G2361401) [Front toe precautions](#/document/G2361399)

watchFor.title: Front-camber work presented as a quick tweak
watchFor.body: The documented correction requires a precisely limited mounting-hole modification and new service hardware. Ask for the measured reason and the separate repair plan before commissioning it. [Front camber correction](#/document/G2361398)

notes: Scope is the factory-configuration 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. GT350 and GT350R specification rows are outside this article’s engine scope.
Wheel removal, tire-force isolation, brake-drag testing and ride-height measurement are conditional branches, not a universal alignment checklist.
This guide adds no fixed alignment interval.

procedures.purpose: Inspect the car and distinguish alignment concerns from loading, tire, brake and steering causes.
Compare configuration-specific alignment readings, ride height and side-to-side lean at curb load.
Measure front and rear ride height using the correct reference points and subtraction orders.
Understand front-toe adjustment, final tightening and steering-bellows protection.
Understand rear-toe adjustment, joint cleanliness and the conditional IPMA camera-alignment routine.
Understand rear-camber adjustment and its required alignment and rear-toe rechecks.
Assess and commission the separate specialist front-camber modification with its required service hardware.
Complete wheel removal and installation when a selected diagnostic or repair branch requires it.
Identify supported lifting locations and protect the vehicle during facility access.

stepGroups.title: Find the clues
stepGroups.summary: Confirm the complaint and inspect tires, loading and chassis condition.

stepGroups.title: Follow the pull when necessary
stepGroups.summary: Complete any wheel exchange safely and distinguish tire forces from brake drag.

stepGroups.title: Put numbers to the concern
stepGroups.summary: Use curb load, measure ride height when relevant and compare the correct factory alignment values.

stepGroups.title: Understand the selected correction
stepGroups.summary: Choose justified work, separate front-camber modification and follow the relevant adjustment sequence.

stepGroups.title: Check the finished result
stepGroups.summary: Verify tightened readings, complete any camera routine and test the original complaint.

diagnostics.finding: Rapid center wear or wear on both shoulders
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect tire pressure is among Ford’s listed causes; the pattern alone does not establish an alignment fault. [Wear diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Correct cold pressures to the vehicle label and resolve tire damage before alignment measurement. [Tire checks](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Inner- or outer-edge wear
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive toe or camber can be involved, and suspension condition also needs inspection. [Wear diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Inspect the chassis, then compare measured angles with the applicable factory values in steps 10–11. [Alignment limits](#/document/G1686608)

diagnostics.finding: Pull reverses or disappears after the shop’s front-wheel exchange
diagnostics.meaning: Ford’s test identifies tire forces as the cause. [Pull diagnostic A3](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: If it reverses, arrange the specified front-to-rear rotation after confirming fit; if it disappears, verify that the complaint is resolved. Complete wheel installation before driving. [Diagnostic decision](#/document/G1686610) [Wheel completion](#/document/G1686507)

diagnostics.finding: Pull stays in the same direction after tire isolation
diagnostics.meaning: Ford proceeds to brake-drag testing before alignment diagnosis. [Pull diagnostic A4](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Have all four assemblies checked for free rotation under the supported test setup. Diagnose brake drag if found; otherwise measure alignment. [Brake and alignment decisions](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Ride height or side-to-side lean exceeds a limit
diagnostics.meaning: With correct loading and measurement setup, the suspension requires investigation; an alignment adjustment alone does not resolve that finding. [Height and lean limits](#/document/G1686608) [Ride-height diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Record both sides’ measurements and arrange suspension inspection and any necessary separate repair before selecting the alignment correction. [Suspension next steps](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Steering wheel remains off-center
diagnostics.meaning: Unequal front or rear toe, or a steering-system fault, can be involved. [Symptom chart](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Review both axles’ final readings and steering condition with the wheel centered. Do not assume only a front adjustment is responsible. [Alignment diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: Pull remains with alignment within specification
diagnostics.meaning: After the preceding loading, tire and brake checks pass, Ford directs steering-system diagnosis. [Pull diagnostic A5](#/document/G1686610)
diagnostics.next: Continue that diagnosis rather than using an arbitrary out-of-spec alignment setting. [Persistent-pull route](#/document/G1686610)

verification.title: The measurement report matches the car
verification.body: Keep initial and final readings with the body style, factory package, curb-load setup and specification ranges used. Check individual readings, total toe and applicable split values rather than relying only on a screen color. [Factory specifications](#/document/G1686608)

verification.title: The selected adjustment is physically finished
verification.body: Confirm final tightening and subsequent measurements, any required camber-related toe correction, secured front boot clamps and untwisted bellows. A front-camber specialist repair must also have its new service hardware and restored sensor-harness attachment accounted for. [Front toe completion](#/document/G2361399) [Rear toe completion](#/document/G2361401) [Rear camber follow-up](#/document/G2361400) [Front camber completion](#/document/G2361398)

verification.title: Any disturbed wheels are complete
verification.body: Confirm clean seating faces, properly restricted XL-2 application, clean and dry wheel-nut threads, and final star-pattern tightening on the tires to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Retain the retightening requirement within 160 km (100 mi). Parking brake and applicable restraints must be restored before lowering from a free-rotation or Neutral setup. [Wheel completion](#/document/G1686507) [Movement precautions](#/document/G1693189)

verification.title: The electronic and driving branches have an outcome
verification.body: If rear toe changed on an LDW-equipped car, confirm completion of the scan-tool IPMA camera alignment. Record the road-test result against the original complaint and route any persistent pull to the remaining diagnosis. [Camera and road-test completion](#/document/G2361401) [Persistent-pull decision](#/document/G1686610)

guides.title: Bleed the MT82 clutch hydraulic circuit

applicability.equipment: MT82 six-speed manual transmission only; not the automatic transmission or the 5.2L/TR-3160 clutch system.

guides.summary: Use Ford’s reservoir-vacuum sequence to remove trapped air after hydraulic repair or diagnosis, then check pedal feel, clutch-pedal reserve and normal operation.
guides.introduction: A soft clutch pedal makes every shift feel like a negotiation with an unreasonable gearbox. I want a dependable response from the top of the pedal stroke. The MT82 clutch controls include the pedal, master cylinder, hydraulic tubes and slave cylinder; this job bleeds that circuit through the brake/clutch reservoir. [Component locations](#/document/G1704357) [Bleeding procedure](#/document/G1704358)
guides.why: Air and low fluid are possible causes of a soft pedal, clutch drag—where the clutch does not fully release—and difficult or grinding shifts. Leaking cylinders and damaged clutch parts can produce similar symptoms, so bleeding is a treatment for an identified hydraulic problem, not a damn parts lottery. Ford specifically requires bleeding after clutch-master-cylinder installation. [Clutch diagnosis](#/document/G1687369) [Master-cylinder installation](#/document/G1687295)

when.summary: After MT82 clutch hydraulic repair, or when diagnosis identifies trapped air causing poor release or a soft pedal.
notes: The clutch-master-cylinder installation procedure explicitly calls for hydraulic bleeding. The MT82 diagnostic chart also calls for it when air is involved in clutch drag, difficult shifting or an unusually soft pedal.
There is no fixed clutch-fluid flush interval established by these repair instructions. This guide does not apply to the 5.2L/TR-3160 system.

prepare.title: Confirm the car and the reason for bleeding
prepare.detail: This guide retains the 2015 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L scope with a confirmed MT82 six-speed manual transmission. Automatic transmissions and the 5.2L/TR-3160 application are outside this article. Use the procedure after hydraulic repair or when diagnosis identifies air; investigate fluid loss and repair leaks first. [MT82 bleeding](#/document/G1704358) [Clutch diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)

prepare.title: Gather the vacuum equipment
prepare.detail: Have Vacuum Pump Kit 416-D002, a suitable brake/clutch bleeder/filler kit and a tightly fitting reservoir stopper. Ford permits an alternative connection made from a 50 mm (1.96 in) rubber stopper with an 8 mm (0.31 in) pipe inserted through it. The gauge must allow you to read 15–20 inches of vacuum. Although the equipment list calls the bleeder/filler a pressure unit, this sequence applies vacuum at the reservoir. [Equipment and connection](#/document/G1704358)

prepare.title: Have the correct fluid and spill cleanup ready
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Read the product label and safety information before handling it; improper chemical handling can cause serious injury. Protect painted and plastic surfaces and keep water available to wash off any spill immediately. [Fluid and handling precautions](#/document/G1704358)

prepare.title: Prepare access and prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: You need access to the brake/clutch reservoir opening and the clutch pedal. The bleeding sequence does not require removing the pedal assembly, master cylinder, wheels or transmission. Keep the ignition off and the key out during service; disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup if fitted. Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Unexpected starting can cause serious injury. [Bleeding access and sequence](#/document/G1704358) [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Prepare for the running reserve test
prepare.detail: Have a cable tie and tape measure for the clutch-pedal reserve check. The test uses first gear and slowly engages the clutch until initial forward movement or a noticeable rpm drop, so choose a clear area where that movement can be safely controlled. Keep people and obstacles out of the vehicle’s path. [Reserve-test method](#/document/G1687369)

steps.title: Check the circuit and let the pedal rise fully
steps.body: Confirm that all hydraulic tubes are correctly seated. Inspect the accessible hydraulic connections for leakage, especially where repairs were made, and resolve any leak before continuing. If the reservoir level is low, inspect both the clutch and brake systems. Check that the floor mat does not restrict the clutch pedal, then leave the pedal in its highest position. [Bleeding setup](#/document/G1704358) [Hydraulic and pedal checks](#/document/G1687369)

steps.title: Open the reservoir and fill to MAX
steps.body: Remove the brake/clutch reservoir cap and fill to the MAX mark with Motorcraft PM-20 DOT 4 LV fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. MAX is the specified starting level for this service. Avoid spilling fluid; immediately wash any off painted or plastic surfaces with water to prevent damage. [Reservoir level and fluid](#/document/G1704358)

steps.title: Fit the sealed vacuum connection
steps.body: Connect the vacuum pump and suitable bleeder equipment to the rubber stopper, then fit the stopper tightly into the reservoir opening. Alternatively, use the specified 50 mm (1.96 in) stopper with an 8 mm (0.31 in) pipe through it. Hold the stopper in place for the vacuum operation. [Stopper and pump setup](#/document/G1704358)

steps.title: Draw vacuum, hold it and release it quickly
steps.body: With the stopper held in place, operate the pump until the gauge reads 15–20 inches of vacuum. Hold that vacuum for one minute, then quickly relieve it. Remove the stopper and vacuum equipment after releasing the vacuum. This is the specified vacuum sequence; do not substitute a brake-bleeding pressure setting. [Vacuum level and timing](#/document/G1704358)

steps.title: Restore the level and install the cap
steps.body: Check the reservoir level again and add the specified fluid to MAX. Install the reservoir cap before working the pedal. [Refill and cap sequence](#/document/G1704358)

steps.title: Cycle the clutch pedal and assess its feel
steps.body: Press and release the clutch pedal 10–12 times, or until the effort is consistent and positive at the top of its travel. Pay attention to the beginning of each press: you are looking for a repeatable response rather than a changing soft section. [Pedal cycling and endpoint](#/document/G1704358)

steps.title: Repeat the complete cycle as directed
steps.body: Repeat steps 3–6 two additional times, or until the pedal effort is consistent and positive at the top of travel. Each repeat includes fitting the stopper, drawing and holding 15–20 inches of vacuum for one minute, quickly releasing it, removing the equipment, refilling to MAX, installing the cap and cycling the pedal. If pedal effort remains inconsistent after the prescribed sequence, investigate the hydraulic fault before continuing. [Repeat sequence](#/document/G1704358) [Persistent soft-pedal diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)

steps.title: Set up the clutch-pedal reserve measurement
steps.body: Confirm that the reservoir cap is installed and remove the bleeding equipment from the work area. Attach a cable tie to the lower clutch pedal and attach the tape measure to the tie. Make sure the pedal can still travel fully without floor-mat interference. Fully depress the clutch, start the vehicle and select first gear. With the pedal still fully depressed, record the distance from the pedal to the seam on the steering wheel. [Bleeding completion](#/document/G1704358) [Reserve-test setup](#/document/G1687369)

steps.title: Measure travel to the first sign of engagement
steps.body: While watching the tape measure, slowly release the clutch pedal. Note the point where the vehicle first starts moving forward or the tachometer shows a noticeable engine-rpm decrease. Compare the tape reading at that point with the fully depressed reading: the change represents the pedal travel to initial engagement, or clutch-pedal reserve. Ford accepts reserve of at least 1 in (25 mm). Less than 1 in (25 mm) requires further clutch/control diagnosis. The limit is a test result, not a pedal-adjustment instruction. [Reserve measurement and limits](#/document/G1687369)

steps.title: Remove the measuring aids and check operation
steps.body: Once the measurement is finished, secure the vehicle and switch the engine off before removing the tape measure and cable tie. Check that the reservoir cap is fitted and the work area is clear. Then check normal clutch operation, including release and gear selection. A passing reserve result does not excuse continuing drag, grinding or difficult shifting; those symptoms still need diagnosis. [Required operating check](#/document/G1704358) [Symptom decisions](#/document/G1687369)

watchFor.title: Fluid loss after filling
watchFor.body: A falling level calls for inspection of both the clutch and brake systems. Repair the cause instead of repeatedly topping up and bleeding. [Leak checks](#/document/G1687369)

watchFor.title: Fluid on paint or plastic
watchFor.body: Wash the affected surface immediately with water. Leaving brake fluid on it can cause surface damage. [Spill response](#/document/G1704358)

watchFor.title: Unexpected movement during the reserve check
watchFor.body: Initial forward movement is one of the test’s engagement indicators. Keep the path clear and perform the test only where you can control the vehicle safely. [Running reserve test](#/document/G1687369)

watchFor.title: Transmission noise or a suspected transmission-fluid leak
watchFor.body: Check transmission-fluid level before driving to investigate these concerns. Ford warns that driving with low transmission fluid can damage the gearbox. This is separate from the brake/clutch reservoir level. [Transmission inspection precautions](#/document/G1687369)

notes: For ordinary owner checks, fluid between MIN and MAX is within the normal range and does not require topping up. The MAX instruction here belongs to the bleeding procedure. Ford advises immediate service when the level is outside the normal range because system performance may be compromised. [Ford fluid-level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Bleeding level](#/document/G1704358)

Master-cylinder replacement requires bleeding afterward, but its pedal/bracket removal operations are not prerequisites for this reservoir service. [Master-cylinder procedure](#/document/G1687295) [Bleeding procedure](#/document/G1704358)

procedures.purpose: Reservoir-vacuum equipment, fluid specification, bleeding sequence and required completion checks.
Clutch-pedal reserve measurement, acceptance limit and relevant symptom decisions.
Identify the MT82 clutch-control components.
Establish the requirement to bleed after master-cylinder installation.
Task-relevant personal protection and prevention of unexpected starting.

stepGroups.title: Check and fill the circuit
stepGroups.summary: Resolve leakage, ensure full pedal travel and establish the starting fluid level.

stepGroups.title: Bleed through the reservoir
stepGroups.summary: Apply the specified vacuum, refill, cycle the pedal and repeat to the stated endpoint.

stepGroups.title: Verify the result
stepGroups.summary: Measure clutch-pedal reserve and confirm normal operation.

diagnostics.finding: Pedal feel is consistent and reserve is at least 1 in (25 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The hydraulic system passes Ford’s reserve criterion. [Reserve criterion](#/document/G1687369)
diagnostics.next: Complete the normal-operation check; investigate any remaining clutch or shifting symptom on its own merits. [Completion check](#/document/G1704358)

diagnostics.finding: Reserve is below 1 in (25 mm), or a soft pedal and poor release remain.
diagnostics.meaning: The hydraulic result is not acceptable. Low fluid, air, master-cylinder leakage, and slave-cylinder leakage or binding are listed possibilities. [Hydraulic diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)
diagnostics.next: Recheck level and leakage, then arrange inspection of the master and slave cylinders as indicated. Do not treat more bleeding as proof that a leaking or binding component is sound. [Clutch symptom chart](#/document/G1687369)

diagnostics.finding: The pedal is unusually hard or binds.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford’s hard-effort path includes master-cylinder binding, pedal damage or binding, and pressure-plate wear or damage. [Hard-pedal diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)
diagnostics.next: Check for restricted pedal travel and arrange diagnosis of the indicated components rather than assuming trapped air. [Pedal and clutch checks](#/document/G1687369)

diagnostics.finding: Drag, grinding or difficult shifts continue after bleeding.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom chart also identifies clutch-disc damage, pressure-plate damage and input-shaft/pilot-bearing binding as possible causes. [Poor-release diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)
diagnostics.next: Have the remaining symptom diagnosed before choosing a repair; this bleeding guide does not establish a need to remove the transmission or replace clutch parts. [Clutch symptom chart](#/document/G1687369)

diagnostics.finding: The clutch slips.
diagnostics.meaning: Slip has a separate diagnostic path involving hydraulic-tube damage, friction components and a slave cylinder that binds or fails to retract. [Slip diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)
diagnostics.next: Arrange the relevant inspections instead of using repeated bleeding as a slip repair. [Clutch symptom chart](#/document/G1687369)

verification.title: Reservoir closed and equipment removed
verification.body: Finish the bleeding sequence with the reservoir filled to MAX and its cap installed. Remove the vacuum setup and pedal-measuring aids. [Bleeding completion](#/document/G1704358) [Reserve-test equipment](#/document/G1687369)

verification.title: Pedal feel and reserve both pass
verification.body: Confirm consistent, positive effort at the top of pedal travel and measured reserve of at least 1 in (25 mm). Record the result so a future change has something concrete to be compared with. [Pedal-feel endpoint](#/document/G1704358) [Reserve limit](#/document/G1687369)

verification.title: Normal release without recurring fluid loss
verification.body: Confirm normal clutch operation and check for renewed leakage. Continued drag, grinding, difficult shifting or falling fluid level means the underlying concern remains. [Operating check](#/document/G1704358) [Clutch diagnosis](#/document/G1687369)

guides.title: Diagnose brake pulsation and disc runout
guides.summary: Separate normal ABS feedback from brake roughness, inspect disc and hub seating, and use the correct runout and thickness limits before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: Runout is the side-to-side movement of an installed brake disc as it rotates. A disc, its mating surfaces and the way the wheel is tightened all contribute to the assembled result. Pulsation is a symptom rather than proof that a disc needs replacing: normal ABS operation, brake condition and suspension faults must be distinguished first.
guides.why: Replacing or machining a disc without checking how it seats can leave the underlying problem in place. The wheel-installation instructions specifically warn that incorrect tightening order can produce high disc runout and accelerate brake roughness. Measuring the installed assembly and checking its mounting surfaces makes the repair decision more useful than judging the disc by appearance alone.

when.summary: When braking repeatedly causes speed-related pedal pulsation, steering-wheel nibble or shudder outside normal ABS operation.
notes: The brake diagnostic chart distinguishes pulsation with ABS activity on loose, wet or snowy surfaces from a repeatable brake or suspension concern.
This is a condition-based diagnostic task, not a scheduled rotor-machining service. Noise alone is not a reason to machine a disc.

prepare.title: Record the symptom before disassembly
prepare.detail: Note whether vibration appears under braking or continues with the pedal released, and whether it is felt in the pedal, steering wheel or seat. Use the brake diagnostic chart to select the correct path and safe test conditions.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted brake package
prepare.detail: Select the actual front caliper and rear disc type before using thickness limits or removing parts. The specification table has different minimum disc thicknesses for the two-, four- and six-piston front systems and for solid versus vented rear discs.

prepare.title: Prepare measuring and support equipment
prepare.detail: Arrange a reliable installed-disc runout measurement with appropriate dial-indicator equipment and a disc-thickness measurement. Have proper lifting equipment, a torque wrench and a way to support a removed caliper without loading its hose.

prepare.title: Plan the measurement boundary
prepare.detail: The linked specifications give an installed-disc runout limit. They do not provide a separate hub-flange runout setup or tolerance, so do not condemn a hub by applying the disc limit to the bare hub.

steps.title: Confirm that the symptom needs brake diagnosis
steps.body: Follow the Brake System vibration pinpoint test. Normal ABS operation can cause hydraulic-unit noise and pedal pulsation during heavy braking or on low-grip surfaces. A repeatable speed-related nibble or shudder can involve brake or suspension components and needs the corresponding inspection.

steps.title: Inspect the mountings before blaming the disc
steps.body: Check the relevant suspension components and wheel installation. If a disc is removed, clean its mating surfaces with the specified brake-cleaning material and a wire brush as directed. Keep the caliper supported; never let it hang by its hose. Corrosion, dirt and incorrect seating must be addressed before relying on an assembled measurement.

steps.title: Record installed-disc runout against its own limit
steps.body: Have the installed disc measured with a repeatable, correctly secured gauge setup and record the indicated lateral movement. The listed maximum installed brake-disc runout is 0.05 mm (0.002 in). Treat that as an assembled-disc criterion, not a separate hub-flange tolerance. If the result is excessive, investigate seating and component condition rather than automatically replacing the hub.

steps.title: Check thickness and whether machining is permitted
steps.body: Measure disc thickness and compare it with the exact fitted-brake specification. Machining is not allowed for discs with cross-drilled friction surfaces. A disc must not be machined when its thickness is less than the minimum thickness plus 0.6 mm (0.0236 in). This machining allowance is separate from the final minimum-thickness limit.

steps.title: Choose a repair that addresses the measured condition
steps.body: Use the brake diagnosis and disc condition to decide whether cleaning and correct installation, disc replacement or permitted machining is appropriate. Where machining is selected, the procedure requires an on-vehicle lathe rather than a bench lathe; follow its complete setup, runout adjustment and post-cut thickness checks. Do not machine simply to treat squeal or other brake noise.

steps.title: Reassemble correctly and verify the original complaint
steps.body: Use the correct front or rear disc procedure, including fasteners that must be replaced. Clean the wheel and hub mating surfaces and tighten wheel nuts in the prescribed star pattern with clean, dry threads. Apply the brake pedal several times after disc work to verify operation, then complete the appropriate controlled road test. Recheck wheel-nut tightness within 100 mi (160 km) after wheel installation.

watchFor.title: Runout and thickness are different measurements
watchFor.body: A disc can meet one requirement and fail another. Keep the installed runout result, measured thickness and correct package-specific minimum together in the job record.

watchFor.title: Loose or damaged suspension parts
watchFor.body: The brake vibration pinpoint test checks suspension condition as well as discs. Correct the identified fault instead of repeatedly machining rotors.

watchFor.title: The wrong brake-package limit is used
watchFor.body: Match the front caliper and rear disc configuration before using thickness limits or choosing parts. Two-, four- and six-piston front brakes and solid versus vented rear discs do not all share the same minimum thickness.

watchFor.title: A hub is blamed without an applicable test
watchFor.body: No separate hub-flange runout limit is established by the linked material. Investigate seating and use an appropriate hub-specific diagnostic reference before condemning the hub.

notes: The 0.05 mm (0.002 in) value is the installed-disc limit; it must not be reused as a bare-hub tolerance. The machining article separately specifies the lathe’s adjustment conditions.
Use a suitably equipped brake shop for a reliable installed-disc measurement, and follow the complete linked procedure when carrying out the repair.

procedures.purpose: Separate normal ABS feedback from brake vibration and follow the suspension/disc diagnostic path.
Installed-disc runout and fitted-brake minimum-thickness specifications.
Front-disc access, caliper support, mating-surface cleaning and reassembly.
Rear-disc access, mating-surface cleaning and reassembly.
Machining eligibility, on-vehicle lathe requirements and final thickness checks.
Correct wheel/hub seating, star-pattern tightening and wheel-nut recheck.

guides.title: Measure wheel vibration and match the tire to the rim
guides.summary: Measure road force or radial runout, reposition the tire when appropriate, check the result and finish with correct wheel-to-hub seating.
guides.introduction: A shaking Mustang can make a lovely drive feel like a damn washing-machine audition. I’d rather measure the problem than buy increasingly expensive round-looking parts. This guide covers assembly measurement, tire-to-rim matching and hub optimization for the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. It teaches the half-turn and directional quarter-turn routes, with repeat measurements to establish the result. Bare-wheel testing and component replacement are specialist follow-on jobs. Tire-machine work requires a professionally trained operator and the equipment manufacturer’s instructions. [Matching workflow](#/document/G1686505) [Ford tire-service guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)
guides.why: Radial runout is a departure from a perfect circle—an egg shape measured at the center tread rib. Loaded Road Force testing also measures how the tire responds against a roller and reports the result as force; Ford prefers loaded testing for judging tire serviceability. Matching changes the tire’s position on the rim to reduce their combined variation. Hub optimization then uses the small clearance between the wheel and hub to offset the measured high spot during installation. Balancing remains part of the finish, but it does not replace these measurements. [Measurement explained](#/document/G1686502) [Matching explained](#/document/G1686505) [Hub optimization](#/document/G1686504)

when.summary: When diagnosis points to a wheel/tire vibration that persists after basic tire, pressure and wheel-condition checks.
notes: Do not perform this tire/wheel vibration diagnosis on tires with fewer than 200 mi (322 km) in service; initial flat spotting can change during that period. This does not postpone correcting obvious damage or unsafe tire condition.
Before runout matching, remove temporary flat spotting by driving 20 or more miles immediately before measurement, as directed in the matching procedure.
This is diagnostic correction when a concern is present, not a mileage-based tire-matching service.

prepare.title: Measurement and marking equipment
prepare.detail: Have a suitable balancer, its manufacturer instructions and correct vehicle-specific centering adapters, a digital tire-pressure gauge, tire crayon and a tread-depth gauge. Loaded Hunter Road Force measurement is preferred. The alternative needs a dial indicator and rigidly secured stand; masking tape may smooth the center tread rib beneath the indicator. [Measurement equipment](#/document/G1686502)

prepare.title: Tire-service equipment and operator
prepare.detail: Arrange a professionally trained tire-machine operator. For alloy or carbon-fiber wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face. Tabletop changers that grip the wheel internally and ride on its front flange can damage it. Have a valve-core tool, suitable fast-drying, corrosion-inhibiting bead lubricant and the machine’s operating instructions. Difficult bead seating additionally requires a remote inflation valve and pressure gauge, adequate stand-off space and, for the final permitted stage, an OSHA-approved tire safety cage. [Equipment and tire handling](#/document/G1686509) [Professional mounting requirement](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

prepare.title: Vehicle access and installation supplies
prepare.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications, with adapters positioned at the specified lifting points. Have wheel chocks, a socket matching the actual wheel nuts, a torque wrench capable of 150 lb-ft (204 Nm), cleaning materials and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2. The emergency tire-change jack is not the service lifting method for this job. [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Installation supplies](#/document/G1686507)

prepare.title: Personal protection and start prevention
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, plus protective gloves when handling sharp edges. Read the safety information for the materials used. Before service around the vehicle, disable remote start if equipped through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup, and remove the key to prevent an unexpected start. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Inspect and check inflation before driving
steps.body:
Check for loose wheel nuts, bent or damaged wheels, tire cuts, bruises, abrasions, blisters, embedded objects and uneven wear. Inspect valve stems for cracks or cuts. Replace tires worn to the wear bars; the minimum tread criterion is 1.6 mm (0.0629 in). Correct unsafe damage before the diagnostic drive. Matching cannot repair it. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686502)

Deflate a tire on a cracked wheel before removing the assembly. Never inflate a tire that has been run flat until it has been removed from the wheel and inspected internally: hidden damage can cause failure during inflation. Do not weld or peen a damaged wheel back into service. [Tire and wheel hazards](#/document/G1693193)

Before driving, measure all road-tire pressures with the digital gauge and correct them using the vehicle’s driver-door or door-pillar label. For a cold check, the tires must have stood out of direct sunlight for at least an hour and not have been driven 1 mi (1.6 km). For ordinary checks after driving, do not bleed hot tires down to the cold label value. Ford’s hot-pressure guidance uses a target 4 psi (27.6 kPa) above the recommended cold pressure; recheck when cold. This road-use guidance is separate from the balancer test setting in step 4. [Digital-gauge requirement](#/document/G1686502) [Cold and hot pressure guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Check tire size against the vehicle label and wheel size and offset against the original specification. Replacements must also meet the recommended speed rating, load range and construction type. [Fitment requirements](#/document/G1686502)

steps.title: Confirm the concern and prepare the tires
steps.body:
Once the vehicle is safe to drive and pressures are correct for road use, assess the vibration on a smooth road. If equipped, disable the Lane Keeping System for this diagnostic drive using its owner instructions; it can interfere with vibration assessment. Do not perform this tire/wheel vibration diagnosis on tires with fewer than 200 mi (322 km) in service. That restriction does not postpone correcting obvious damage. [Diagnostic conditions](#/document/G1686502)

Immediately before Road Force measurements, drive 20 or more miles to remove possible short-term flat spotting. [Flat-spot preparation](#/document/G1686505)

steps.title: Identify the assemblies and remove them safely
steps.body:
Mark each tire’s vehicle position on its inward sidewall so all four assemblies remain identifiable. Position the vehicle on the hoist with the transmission in Neutral. Use the lifting points identified by stamped triangles, and check that the adapters clear suspension, steering, exhaust and other vulnerable components. Incorrect positioning can let the vehicle shift or fall. [Position marks](#/document/G1686502) [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507) [Lift points](#/document/G1663631)

Confirm adequate hoist capacity before raising. Remove the wheel nuts and assemblies. Do not heat a seized nut: heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Measurements here take place on the balancer and do not require powering the vehicle’s wheels with its engine. [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189) [Removal precautions](#/document/G1686507) [Jack warning](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Set up the balancer and workshop test pressure
steps.body:
For the workshop measurement, Ford directs setting the tire to the pressure specified on the vehicle’s tire-pressure label, checked with a digital gauge. Apply that test setup on the balancer after the warm-up drive. It is a measurement condition, not the owner’s instruction for adjusting hot tires during ordinary road use. Restore road-use pressure using step 23 before the final drive. [Workshop pressure setup](#/document/G1686502) [Owner pressure guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Clean foreign material from the assembly. Select the correct centering adapters using the balancer’s vehicle application information and manufacturer instructions. Wrong adapters can introduce apparent runout or damage the wheel. Turn the balancer’s inflation station off for tires requiring 60.0 psi (414 kPa) or more; that restriction is not a recommended Mustang tire pressure. [Balancer setup and restriction](#/document/G1686502)

Use either the loaded method in step 5 or the indicator method in step 6.

steps.title: Preferred route: measure loaded Road Force
steps.body: Using the correctly centered Hunter equipment and its operating instructions, measure Road Force. Temporarily mark the high spot and force value on the sidewall. Above 20 lb (9 kg), continue to step 7 for matching. At or below 20 lb (9 kg), go to step 18 for permanent marking, balancing and installation. Keep the force units attached to the value; this reading is not inflation pressure. [Loaded measurement and decision](#/document/G1686502)

steps.title: Alternative route: measure with a dial indicator
steps.body:
With the assembly mounted on the balancer, secure the indicator stand so it cannot move and place the indicator tip on the center tread rib. Masking tape may provide a smoother contact surface. Rotate to find the low spot, zero the gauge, then turn one complete revolution to confirm the low spot and return to zero. [Indicator setup](#/document/G1686502)

Rotate slowly and steadily, observing the overall gauge sweep rather than each small tread-related flicker. With the low spot zeroed, the maximum reading is total radial runout. Above 1.14 mm (0.045 in), temporarily mark the high spot and reading and continue to step 7. At or below that limit, go to step 18. Unloaded runout can guide tire positioning, but cannot accurately determine whether a tire should be removed from service. [Indicator measurement, limit and restriction](#/document/G1686502)

steps.title: Select the approved matching route
steps.body:
Identify the machine before selecting its matching program:

- Hunter Gen I/II, GSP9702/GSP9712: use the machine for measurements only. Ignore its matching prompts and use the manual route below.
- Hunter Gen III, GSP9722: use “Match Without Rim Runout” when available; otherwise use the manual route. Select the approved method each time if it does not remain the default.
- Hunter Gen IV/V, RFT/RFE: select Road Force > Procedures > 180 Matching. Select it each time if necessary.
- Other brands: use the manual route; equivalent automatic matching is not established.

For an approved automatic route, follow the manufacturer’s operating instructions and apply the TPMS and inflation precautions in steps 8–12 whenever tire handling is requested. Repeat measurements as directed, then rejoin at step 18 once the applicable assembly limit is met. If the result remains above limit, retain the readings for further diagnosis. A completed screen sequence alone does not establish correction. Steps 10 and 14–16 describe the manual matching route. [Approved methods and equipment identification](#/document/G1686505) [Assembly limits](#/document/G1686502)

steps.title: Preserve the marks and fully deflate
steps.body:
Keep the first measured high spot and value identifiable. On the tire machine, add a separate reference mark on the tire directly at the valve stem; this tracks movement of the tire relative to the wheel. Also index-mark the wheel-weight positions before dismounting. [Matching reference](#/document/G1686505) [Dismounting marks](#/document/G1686509)

Remove the valve-stem core and fully deflate the tire before bead work. The tire-pressure monitoring system sensor is attached to the valve stem inside the wheel. Do not pull the stem from the wheel during matching: doing so can damage the sensor. [Deflation and sensor protection](#/document/G1686509)

steps.title: Separate the beads without striking the sensor
steps.body:
The beads are the tire edges that seat against the rim. With a paddle-type separator, position the valve stem at 12 or 6 o’clock and the paddle at 3 o’clock. With a roller-type separator, align the valve stem with the roller. Use the machine’s instructions for operating its controls. [Separator positions](#/document/G1686509)

As the beads are separated, do not push them beyond the wheel’s mid-plane—the middle of its width. Excessive bead travel or incorrect separator positioning can damage the TPMS sensor. These protections apply whenever this guide calls for bead separation. [Bead-travel restriction](#/document/G1686509)

steps.title: Manual route: rotate the tire half a turn
steps.body: Lubricate the beads with a suitable fast-drying, corrosion-inhibiting tire bead lubricant. Rotate the tire 180 degrees on the rim so the valve-stem reference mark finishes directly opposite the valve stem. Preserve the first measured high-spot mark. This operation separates the beads and repositions the existing tire; it does not require removing the valve stem or sensor. Approved automatic-route users make the positioning change requested by their approved program instead. [Half-turn matching](#/document/G1686505)

steps.title: Reseat and inflate normally
steps.body:
Restore the valve core for inflation and inflate to the pressure specified on the driver-door or door-pillar vehicle label, using a digital gauge. Confirm that the beads have seated. If the tire was fully dismounted, first use the mounting positions in step 17. [Assembly and inflation](#/document/G1686509)

If the beads do not seat at the specified pressure, do not casually add more air. The special procedure in step 12 applies only after they cannot be seated by inflation up to the maximum pressure marked on the tire sidewall. Match the tire and wheel size and type; incompatible assemblies can separate or fail during inflation. [Bead-seating conditions](#/document/G1686509) [Size and type safety](#/document/G1693193)

steps.title: Use the complete difficult-seating precautions
steps.body:
This is a professional tire-service branch. Exceeding the sidewall maximum without the required precautions can cause serious injury. If the beads have not seated by that maximum:

1. Relubricate the tire beads and wheel bead-seat areas.
2. Install a remote inflation valve and pressure gauge.
3. Wear eye and ear protection and stand at least 12 ft (3.65 m) away.
4. Inflate remotely only until the beads seat or the gauge reaches 20 psi (138 kPa) above the tire’s sidewall maximum. If they still have not seated, deflate the tire before proceeding.
5. Place the assembly in an OSHA-approved tire safety cage. Retain the remote equipment, distance and protection.
6. Inflate only until the beads seat or the gauge reaches 40 psi (276 kPa) above the sidewall maximum. Never exceed that final limit. If the beads still do not seat, install a new tire.

After seating, return the assembly to the specified vehicle-label pressure before measurement. These elevated pressures are temporary mounting limits, not driving pressures. [Difficult bead-seating sequence](#/document/G1686509)

steps.title: Take and record the second measurement
steps.body:
After the beads are seated and the workshop test pressure restored, repeat the same measurement method. Mark the second high spot and value while keeping the first result identifiable. An assembly at or below 20 lb (9 kg) Road Force, or 1.14 mm (0.045 in) radial runout for the indicator method, proceeds to step 18. [Second measurement](#/document/G1686505) [Applicable limits](#/document/G1686502)

For a manual half-turn that remains above its limit, compare the marks using steps 14–16. Approved automatic-method users follow their approved program’s continuation, retaining any unresolved results for further diagnosis. [Matching outcomes](#/document/G1686505)

steps.title: Manual route: identify a high spot that follows the tire
steps.body:
If both measurements are above specification and the high spots are within 4 in (101.6 mm) of each other on the tire, the high spot has followed the tire. Both above-limit results are required before drawing that conclusion. Ford’s branch directs tire replacement, balancing and hub optimization when the tire is the cause. [Tire-following decision](#/document/G1686505)

If the evidence consists only of unloaded indicator readings, obtain loaded testing before condemning the tire: unloaded runout alone cannot accurately establish serviceability. Arrange tire replacement as a separate service operation, including the required new valve stem. [Serviceability restriction](#/document/G1686502) [New-stem requirement](#/document/G1686509)

If the two high spots are not within that distance on the tire, continue to step 15. [Matching decision](#/document/G1686505)

steps.title: Manual route: identify a high spot that follows the wheel
steps.body:
If the second result remains above specification and its high spot is within 4 in (101.6 mm) of the position opposite the first high spot on the wheel, the wheel is the likely contributor. The marks alone do not justify replacement. Route the assembly to a specialist with the complete bare-wheel runout measurement procedure. Ford calls for dismounting the tire, measuring the wheel on a balancer and replacing the wheel if its runout exceeds 1.14 mm (0.0449 in), followed by balancing and hub optimization. [Wheel-following decision](#/document/G1686505)

If the second high spot follows neither the tire nor the wheel, continue to step 16. [Quarter-turn branch](#/document/G1686505)

steps.title: Manual route: make the directional quarter-turn and check it
steps.body:
When the second high spot follows neither component and the result remains above specification, draw an arrow on the tire sidewall from the second high spot toward the first, taking the shortest direction around the tire. Fully deflate the tire and separate the beads using steps 8–9. Lubricate the beads, then rotate the tire 90 degrees—one-quarter turn—in the arrow’s direction. [Quarter-turn direction](#/document/G1686505) [Deflation and bead protection](#/document/G1686509)

Reseat the beads and inflate using steps 11–12, restoring the workshop test pressure. Repeat the same assembly measurement from step 5 or 6, and record the new high spot and value without losing the earlier results. [Inflation procedure](#/document/G1686509) [Repeat measurement methods](#/document/G1686502)

At or below 20 lb (9 kg) Road Force, or 1.14 mm (0.045 in) for the indicator method, continue to step 18. If the result remains above its applicable limit, retain all measurements and route further diagnosis to the tire specialist. Do not invent another rotation sequence or choose a replacement part from this result alone. [Acceptable-result route and limits](#/document/G1686502)

steps.title: When a separate test requires full tire dismounting
steps.body:
Full dismounting is not an extra prerequisite for repositioning the existing tire on its rim. When a specialist’s test does require removal, fully deflate and separate the beads with steps 8–9. On the tire-machine turntable, put the valve stem at 11:30 and the machine arm at 12 o’clock, then dismount the outer bead. Reset those same positions and dismount the inner bead. Follow the machine’s operating instructions while maintaining the sensor clearances. [Dismounting sequence](#/document/G1686509)

For remounting the same tire, lubricate the beads with suitable fast-drying, corrosion-inhibiting bead lubricant and position the bottom bead on the wheel before mounting. Align the valve stem with the machine arm at 6 o’clock and mount the bottom bead. Reposition to that same valve-stem/arm alignment at 6 o’clock and mount the top bead. Then use steps 11–12 for seating and inflation, followed by assembly measurement. [Mounting sequence](#/document/G1686509) [Measurement](#/document/G1686502)

Matching the existing tire and wheel does not require removing their undamaged valve and sensor assembly. A replacement tire or wheel requires a new valve stem; wheel replacement also requires a new sensor screw. Those replacement jobs must include the appropriate snap-in or bolt-on valve procedure. Reusing the existing sensor on a new wheel does not itself require TPMS training. [Conditional replacement requirements](#/document/G1686509)

steps.title: Permanently mark an acceptable result and balance
steps.body:
Once the assembly meets the limit for the measurement method used, permanently mark the final high spot and value on the inward sidewall. Include its units and preserve the vehicle-position identification. Balance using the correct adapters and equipment that protects the wheel face. [Final recording and balancing](#/document/G1686502) [Matching record](#/document/G1686505) [Wheel protection](#/document/G1686507)

Proceed with hub optimization after an acceptable assembly result. If further diagnosis or replacement was required, have that work and its measurement check completed first. [Measurement completion route](#/document/G1686502)

steps.title: Clean the seating surfaces and lubricate only the pilot
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting face and the hub/brake-disc mounting face. Check that any rotor-to-hub fasteners are secure and cannot interfere with wheel seating. Contamination or interference can allow wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to detach, causing loss of control and serious injury. [Mounting-surface preparation](#/document/G1686507)

Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only where the wheel’s central pilot bore fits over the hub pilot. Keep it off the flat mating faces, studs, nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The specified wheel-nut torque requires clean, dry stud and nut threads. [Pilot lubrication and dry threads](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Fit the wheel with its high spot at the bottom
steps.body: Position the assembly on the vehicle with its final measured high spot at 6 o’clock. Install the wheel nuts by hand until snug. This position lets the available wheel-to-hub clearance offset the measured high spot during optimization. [Positioning and initial tightening](#/document/G1686504)

steps.title: Restore vehicle restraints before lowering
steps.body: Before any tire touches the ground, set the parking brake. With the engine off, select Park for an automatic transmission or reverse for a manual transmission, restoring the vehicle’s stationary restraints after the Neutral lifting setup. Block wheels remaining on the ground and keep the vehicle restrained through lowering and final tightening. Do not leave it free to roll while applying wheel-nut torque. [Parking brake and wheel blocking](#/document/G1693189) [Transmission parking positions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

steps.title: Apply slight tire loading and torque in the star order
steps.body:
Lower until the tires contact the ground and the suspension takes only a slight load. Keep the hoist supporting the remaining weight: during this specific optimization operation, do not allow the full vehicle weight to rest on the tires while tightening. [Optimization loading](#/document/G1686504)

Tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm) in the illustrated star order. With one nut at the top, the sequence is top, lower left, upper right, upper left, then lower right. The cross pattern helps avoid excessive brake-disc runout and subsequent shudder or vibration. [Torque and five-nut order](#/document/G1686507)

The general wheel-installation procedure describes final tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires. For this optimization job, use the specific slight-loading instruction above, then lower fully after tightening. [Specific loading instruction](#/document/G1686504)

steps.title: Restore road-use pressure and reassess the vibration
steps.body:
Once tightening is complete, lower fully and clear the lifting equipment. Confirm every installed assembly has its final measurement recorded, has been balanced and has received the specified wheel-nut torque. [Measurement completion](#/document/G1686502) [Wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

Before the road assessment, use the digital gauge to restore pressure for road use. The label-pressure setting used on the balancer does not count as a cold-pressure verification. If the tires are cold, set the vehicle-label pressure. If still hot from driving, use Ford’s hot-pressure guidance: 4 psi (27.6 kPa) above the recommended cold pressure, followed by a cold recheck. During ordinary hot-tire checks, do not bleed pressure down to the cold label value. Refit the valve caps. [Digital-gauge requirement](#/document/G1686502) [Road-use pressure and valve caps](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539674&Uid=G1635847&ProcUid=G1638644&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

Remove the wheel blocks when ready to move and repeat the smooth-road assessment. If the original vibration persists, continue diagnosis rather than assuming another tire-position change is justified. Record installation mileage and arrange wheel-nut retightening within 100 mi (160 km); nuts can loosen after installation, allowing a wheel to work loose. [Road assessment and continuing diagnosis](#/document/G1686502) [Required nut recheck](#/document/G1686507) [Removing wheel blocks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G539673&Uid=G1635855&ProcUid=G1638646&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web)

watchFor.title: A convincing false reading
watchFor.body: Dirt, incorrect centering adapters or a moving indicator stand can create misleading runout. Correct the setup before making a parts decision. [Measurement precautions](#/document/G1686502)

watchFor.title: Force mistaken for pressure
watchFor.body: The 20 lb (9 kg) Road Force threshold is a force reading. Indicator runout has a dimensional limit. Neither supplies the tire’s inflation setting. [Measurement methods](#/document/G1686502)

watchFor.title: A tire condemned from one unloaded reading
watchFor.body: The tire-following decision requires two above-limit measurements with the specified high-spot relationship. Unloaded runout alone cannot accurately establish tire serviceability. [Matching decision](#/document/G1686505) [Serviceability restriction](#/document/G1686502)

watchFor.title: Sensor contact during bead work
watchFor.body: Keep the separator in its specified relationship to the valve stem and prevent the beads passing the wheel’s mid-plane. Do not pull the valve stem during matching. [TPMS handling](#/document/G1686509)

watchFor.title: A mechanically damaged TPMS sensor
watchFor.body: Severe sensor damage can expose hazardous battery chemicals. If chemicals reach skin or eyes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes and obtain prompt medical attention. Seek immediate medical help if any battery material is swallowed, and dispose of damaged sensors through appropriate hazardous-material procedures. [Sensor battery precautions](#/document/G1686525)

watchFor.title: Lubricant on the wrong surfaces
watchFor.body: Only the pilot interface receives XL-2. Flat mounting faces and wheel-fastener threads stay clean and dry, and brake friction surfaces must remain uncontaminated. [Installation precautions](#/document/G1686507)

notes: The assembly indicator criterion is 1.14 mm (0.045 in); the bare-wheel replacement threshold is greater than 1.14 mm (0.0449 in). Keep each value with its own test. [Assembly criterion](#/document/G1686502) [Wheel threshold](#/document/G1686505)
The 200 mi (322 km) restriction and immediate premeasurement drive are diagnostic conditions, not a recurring matching interval. [Test conditions](#/document/G1686505)

Matching an existing tire does not automatically require valve-stem or sensor removal. New tire or wheel installation requires a new valve stem; a new wheel also requires a new sensor screw. Those conditional replacement operations use the appropriate valve-type procedure. [Tire-service branches](#/document/G1686509)

procedures.purpose: Preliminary inspection, vibration diagnosis, measurement setup, loaded and indicator methods, limits and serviceability restrictions.
Approved matching methods, reference marks, half-turn and directional quarter-turn changes, and high-spot diagnostic branches.
TPMS-safe deflation, bead separation, dismounting, mounting, inflation restrictions and conditional valve-service requirements.
Six-o’clock high-spot positioning and slight-loading wheel-to-hub optimization.
Wheel removal, equipment protection, mounting-surface preparation, pilot lubricant, torque, tightening order and nut recheck.
